Job Summary
The Research Scientist is a member of Innovations for Poverty Action's Applied Research & Methods (ARM) team, which designs and leads technical research for IPA's global program portfolio with a focus on randomized controlled trials (RCTs), quasi-experimental impact evaluations, and survey methodology.
ARM research scientists work closely with IPA's country offices and advisory units on monitoring, evaluation, and learning.

The person in this role designs and leads coverage surveys and program audits for a large-scale infectious disease prevention program in Sub-Saharan Africa, combining technical survey design, health systems expertise, and field research management to generate credible, timely evidence for program partners and funders.
The role carries intellectual leadership of coverage surveys, data audits, and impact evaluations focused primarily on malaria prevention interventions, along with other health policies and programs across Sub-Saharan Africa.

Team Supervision and Research Development:
AcademicConferences & Publications

PhD or equivalent in epidemiology, biostatistics, public health, health economics, or related social science.
Substantive expertise in health systems, including how health facilities operate, the quality and limitations of facility-level data, and methods for working with facility staff to extract and validate data.

Experience writing research proposals, including study design and budgeting.

Job Title: MEL Associate, Poverty Embedded Evidence Lab
Job Description:
Job Summary
IPA Nigeria is seeking a MEL Associate to support an embedded evidence lab established within a partner government agency implementing social protection programmes for vulnerable populations.
The partner agency’s portfolio spans areas such as nutrition and education support, conditional cash transfers, and economic empowerment and livelihoods programmes.
The MEL Associate will work as part of an embedded team to strengthen the agency’s capacity to systematically generate, manage, analyze, and use data and evidence for programme improvement and policy decision-making.
This position requires hands-on MEL expertise, strong capacity-building skills, and the ability to work effectively within government systems.
The MEL Associate will collaborate closely with agency staff across multiple departments to co-create practical MEL systems, deliver training and technical assistance, support data analysis and visualization, and foster a culture of evidence-informed decision-making.
This is an opportunity to apply MEL expertise in a high-impact setting at the intersection of social protection policy and practice, working directly within government to build the systems, skills, and organizational culture needed to improve outcomes for vulnerable populations.
The ideal candidate combines technical MEL knowledge with practical implementation experience, excellent training and mentoring abilities, and a passion for sustainable capacity development in government institutions.
The MEL Associate may also be called upon to support other IPA Nigeria embedded lab engagements as organizational needs evolve.
Responsibilities
MEL Systems Development and Implementation:
Support the development and implementation of an agency-wide MEL framework, working collaboratively with agency staff to develop theories of change, results frameworks, and indicator frameworks aligned with strategic objectives and reporting requirements.
Design programme-specific MEL plans for individual programme teams, including data collection instruments, monitoring protocols, and quality assurance mechanisms tailored to each programme’s context and decision-making needs.
Conduct data needs assessments across agency departments, mapping information requirements against existing data sources, identifying gaps, assessing data quality, and recommending solutions to strengthen data systems.
Develop standard operating procedures, guidelines, and protocols for data collection, management, quality assurance, reporting, and data use that are practical, user-friendly, and appropriate to staff capacity levels.
Implement data quality assurance mechanisms including verification protocols, spot-checks, data audits, and corrective action processes to ensure reliable and accurate programme data.
Capacity Building and Technical Support:
Design and deliver MEL training workshops and learning sessions for agency staff at various levels on theories of change, indicator design, data collection methods, data analysis, data visualization, and evidence-informed decision-making.
Provide ongoing hands-on technical assistance and mentoring to M&E officers, programme managers, and field staff on practical MEL tasks including designing data collection instruments, conducting data quality checks, preparing reports and visualizations, and using evidence for programme decisions.
Build staff capacity to use data analysis and visualization tools including advanced Excel, statistical software (Stata, R, SPSS), database management tools, and visualization platforms (Power BI, Tableau).
Facilitate learning events, data review meetings, and evidence-to-action workshops to promote peer learning, institutionalize data use practices, and foster an organizational culture of continuous learning and evidence-informed adaptation.
Develop training materials, guidance notes, job aids, and tools to create institutional knowledge resources that support sustainable capacity strengthening.
Data Analysis, Visualization, and Reporting:
Analyze primary and secondary programme data using quantitative and qualitative methods to generate actionable insights, and prepare clear data summaries, analytical reports, dashboards, and visualizations for various audiences.
Support the development and maintenance of real-time monitoring dashboards displaying key performance indicators to enable programme managers and leadership to track progress and make timely adjustments.
Contribute to high-quality technical outputs including evaluation reports, policy briefs, evidence syntheses, and lessons learned documents that communicate programme achievements, challenges, and learning.
Support the partner agency’s external reporting obligations to relevant government leadership, donors, and other stakeholders, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and compliance with reporting requirements.
Translate complex data findings into accessible, actionable insights for non-technical audiences through effective data visualization and clear written communication.
Evidence Generation and Coordination:
Support the design and implementation of primary data collection activities including surveys, focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and case studies aimed at answering learning questions and generating evidence for programme improvement.
Collaborate with IPA researchers and the assigned Lab Manager to support programme evaluations and research studies embedded within agency programmes, ensuring alignment with agency priorities and contribution to organizational learning.
Coordinate with agency departments, the Lab Manager, IPA Nigeria team, and external partners to ensure alignment and maximize synergies across MEL activities.
Support administrative and logistical requirements for lab activities including planning workshops, managing procurement, coordinating field visits, maintaining documentation, and contributing to work planning and reporting.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Economics, Demography, Social Sciences, Development Studies, Public Policy, International Development, or a related quantitative or social science field is required; a Master’s degree in a relevant field is preferred.
Minimum of 3 years of professional experience in monitoring, evaluation, and learning, preferably in social protection, poverty reduction, livelihoods, or international development programmes.
Proficiency in data analysis and visualization tools, including advanced Microsoft Excel, at least one statistical software package (Stata, R, or SPSS), and data visualization platforms such as Power BI or Tableau.
Hands-on experience designing, strengthening, or implementing Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) systems, including data collection, management, and analysis frameworks.
Proven ability to manage multiple programmes or workstreams simultaneously, including coordinating stakeholders, tracking progress, and managing deliverables.
Demonstrated ability to train, coach, or mentor others in MEL systems, including building institutional capacity for data use.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate technical analysis into clear, structured, and policy-relevant insights for non-technical audiences.
Experience working with government institutions or regulatory agencies is highly desirable.
Willingness to be a team player and identify connections between work streams.
Cultural and political sensitivity and demonstrated ability to work successfully with diverse constituencies.
Passion for making data-driven decision-making a reality in the development sector.

Company Details:
Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, natural disasters and exclusion from healthcare. MSF offers assistance to people based on need, irr...read moreespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation.

Our actions are guided by medical ethics and the principles of neutrality and impartiality.

A worldwide movement

MSF was founded in Paris, France in 1971. Its principles are described in the organisation's founding charter. It is a non-profit, self-governed organisation.

Today, MSF is a worldwide movement of 24 associations, bound together as MSF International, based in Switzerland.

Thousands of health professionals, logistical and administrative staff - most of whom are hired locally - work on programmes in some 70 countries worldwide.

Humanitarian action

MSF's work is based on humanitarian principles. We are committed to bringing quality medical care to people caught in crisis, regardless of race, religion or political affiliation.

MSF operates independently. We conduct our own evaluations on the ground to determine people’s needs. More than 90 per cent of our overall funding comes from millions of private sources, not governments.

MSF is neutral. We do not take sides in armed conflicts, we provide care on the basis of need, and we push for independent access to victims of conflict as required under international humanitarian law.

Bearing witness and speaking out

MSF medical teams often witness violence and neglect in the course of their work, largely in regions that receive scant international attention.

At times, MSF may speak out publicly in an effort to bring a forgotten crisis to public attention, to alert the public to abuses occurring beyond the headlines, to criticise the inadequacies of the aid system, or to challenge the diversion of humanitarian aid for political interests.

Quality medical care

MSF rejects the idea that poor people deserve third-rate medical care and strives to provide high-quality care to patients. In 1999, when MSF was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, the organisation announced the money would go towards raising awareness of and fighting against neglected diseases.

Through the Access Campaign, and in partnership with the Drugs for Neglected Diseases initiative, this work has helped lower the price of HIV/AIDS treatment and stimulated research and development for medicines to treat malaria and neglected diseases like sleeping sickness and kala azar.

Job Description:
Responsibilities
Workplan Development & Project Scheduling:
Expected Result
:
The project has a realistic, resource-loaded workplan aligned to design, BOQ and site conditions that provides a reliable basis for execution and control.
Develop and issue the baseline construction programme (WBS to activity level) covering all road construction phases earthworks, sub-base, base course, drainage, structures and surfacing.
Translate design, BOQ and specification information into a resource-loaded schedule, aligning manpower, plant and materials to programme milestones.
Sequence activities logically, reflecting realistic productivity rates, weather/seasonal constraints and site access.
Secure Project Manager/PMO sign-off on the baseline programme before issue.
Update and reissue the programme whenever scope, design or site conditions materially change.
Targets:
Baseline programme issued and approved before mobilisation — 100%
Programme reflects current approved scope/design — 100%
Programme revisions issued following an approved change — Within 3 working days
Progress Monitoring, Tracking & Execution:
Expected Result: Actual site progress is tracked accurately and continuously against the approved programme, giving management a reliable, real-time picture of project status.
Track daily/weekly site progress against the baseline and working programme.
Produce S-curves, progress dashboards and variance analysis comparing planned versus actual progress.
Conduct 2–4 week rolling look-ahead planning to drive short-interval execution on site.
Verify reported progress against physical site conditions before issuing updates.
Maintain an accurate, current master schedule at all times.
Targets:
Weekly/monthly progress reports issued within agreed cutoff — Within 24 hours
Variance between reported and verified site progress — Less than 5%
Look-ahead activities completed as scheduled — At least 85%
Site Coordination & Resource Alignment:
Expected Result
:
Materials, manpower and equipment are mobilised ahead of programme need dates, and planning is fully integrated with site execution.
Coordinate with procurement, stores and site teams to ensure resources are available ahead of scheduled activities.
Attend site progress and management meetings, providing technical planning input.
Work with Site/Project Managers to translate the programme into practical daily/weekly work orders.
Flag resource-driven schedule risks before they affect the critical path.
Targets:
Resource-driven delays attributable to late planning input — Zero
Scheduled planning/site coordination meetings attended — 100%
Delay Identification, Escalation & Recovery Planning:
Expected Result: Schedule risks and delays are identified early, escalated promptly, and addressed through realistic recovery plans that protect the overall completion date.
Continuously monitor the critical path and identify activities at risk of slippage.
Investigate root causes of delay in coordination with Site/Project Managers.
Develop and issue recovery/mitigation plans for confirmed delays.
Escalate schedule risks and delays that may affect overall project completion.
Targets:
Schedule risks flagged ahead of critical path impact — At least 2 weeks' notice
Recovery plan issued after a confirmed delay — Within 3 working days
Unresolved critical delays without escalation — Zero
Reporting, Documentation & Programme Control:
Expected Result: Programme documentation is accurate, current and properly controlled, giving management and clients confidence in reported project status.
Maintain full version control and approval trail for all programme issues and revisions.
Prepare and issue accurate progress and variance reports to management and, where required, client/consultant teams.
Support cost/time impact assessment of variations, delays and change orders.
Maintain organised records of planning data, productivity rates and lessons learned for future projects.
Targets
Programme updates version-controlled and approved before reissue — 100%
Monthly S-curve/variance report issued — By agreed date, error-free
Planning records maintained and retrievable — 100%
Schedule Projection Accuracy & Accountability:
Expected Result: The Planning Engineer holds full, direct accountability for the accuracy and reliability of the project's schedule projection from baseline to completion; projections are realistic, defensible and current at all times.
Own the end-to-end integrity of the project's time projection, ensuring it reflects true site status at every reporting cycle.
Treat any projection failure — an inaccurate, outdated or undisclosed projection — as a critical planning lapse requiring immediate correction.
Proactively verify projections against actual progress rather than relying on assumed rates or unconfirmed inputs.
Immediately disclose and correct any identified projection error, however it arose.
Targets:
Projection accuracy verified against actual site progress — Every reporting cycle
Unexplained or undisclosed projection failure — Zero tolerance
Identified projection errors corrected from detection — Within 48 hours.

Job Description:
Job Summary
We are seeking a qualified and responsible Pharmacist to oversee the safe and effective dispensing of medications and provide professional pharmaceutical care to customers.
The ideal candidate should have 2–3 years of relevant pharmacy experience, sound knowledge of medications and pharmaceutical practice, excellent customer service skills, and a strong commitment to regulatory compliance and patient safety.
Key Responsibilities
Dispense prescription and over-the-counter medications accurately and in accordance with prescriptions and applicable regulations.
Review prescriptions for accuracy, appropriate dosage, potential drug interactions, contraindications, and other medication-related concerns.
Counsel customers/patients on the proper use, dosage, storage, side effects, and precautions associated with medications.
Provide professional advice on minor health conditions and recommend appropriate OTC products where necessary.
Maintain proper records of prescriptions, controlled medicines, and other pharmaceutical transactions as required.
Ensure medicines are properly stored under appropriate temperature and environmental conditions.
Monitor stock levels, expiry dates, and product movement to minimise shortages, wastage, and expired products.
Support inventory management, including stock receipt, verification, arrangement, and periodic stock counts.
Ensure the pharmacy complies with relevant PCN, NAFDAC, and other applicable regulatory requirements and professional standards.
Maintain high standards of cleanliness, organisation, confidentiality, and professionalism within the pharmacy.
Supervise and provide appropriate guidance to pharmacy assistants and other support staff where applicable.
Identify and appropriately escalate medication errors, adverse drug reactions, suspected counterfeit products, and other pharmaceutical concerns.
Build positive relationships with customers and provide courteous and professional service.
Perform other pharmacy-related duties as may be assigned by management.
Requirements
Bachelor of Pharmacy (B.Pharm) from a recognised institution.
Must be a registered Pharmacist with the Pharmacists Council of Nigeria (PCN) and possess a valid practising licence.
2–3 years of relevant post-qualification experience, preferably in a community/retail pharmacy.
Good knowledge of prescription and OTC medications, drug interactions, dosage, and pharmaceutical care.
Sound understanding of pharmacy regulations and professional standards.
Good inventory and stock management skills.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, and customer service skills.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to patient safety.
Ability to work independently and responsibly with minimal supervision.
Good computer and record-keeping skills.
Key Competencies:
Professional integrity and confidentiality; attention to detail; pharmaceutical knowledge; customer/patient care; inventory management; communication and interpersonal skills; problem-solving; teamwork; and regulatory compliance.
Company Details: Casmolar Healthcare Limited is a registered retail pharmacy, supermarket, and healthcare hub located in the heart of Isolo, Lagos. The company bridges the gap between reliable healthcare services and daily essential shopping by providing a convenient, one-stop experience for the local community.

Job Title: Executive Assistant / Personal Assistant to the CEO
Job Description:
The Executive Assistant/PA to the CEO provides high-level executive support to the CEO by coordinating priorities, managing schedules and itineraries, conducting research, supporting planning and budgeting, and ensuring effective follow-through across key activities. The position requires an individual who can think ahead, research independently, analyse information, coordinate with different levels of the organisation, and translate the CEO's priorities into well-organised plans and actions.
The ideal candidate is highly organised, commercially aware, analytical and capable of working with limited supervision while maintaining confidentiality and sound judgement.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Executive Planning & Coordination
Manage and coordinate the CEO's professional calendar, priorities, appointments and commitments.
Develop daily, weekly and monthly schedules that reflect the CEO's priorities.
Plan and coordinate business itineraries, travel arrangements and logistics.
Anticipate upcoming requirements and ensure the CEO is adequately prepared for engagements, meetings and key activities.
Track commitments, deadlines and agreed actions to ensure timely follow-through.
Coordinate with members of the CEO's team to obtain updates, information and required deliverables.
Support the CEO in organising priorities across multiple projects and areas of responsibility.
Research & Business Intelligence
Conduct detailed research on industries, markets, companies, competitors, clients and emerging opportunities.
Prepare competitive and market analysis to support executive decision-making.
Gather, analyse and summarise information from multiple sources and present clear findings to the CEO.
Research potential business opportunities, partnerships, investments, events and strategic initiatives.
Monitor relevant industry developments, trends and competitor activities.
Prepare briefing notes, background reports and executive summaries ahead of important meetings or decisions.
Strategic & Project Support
Support the CEO in developing plans, timelines and priorities for strategic initiatives.
Break broad objectives into actionable tasks, milestones and deliverables.
Coordinate with relevant team members to monitor progress on CEO-led initiatives.
Maintain project trackers and provide regular updates on progress, outstanding actions and potential issues.
Identify gaps, delays or emerging issues and bring them to the CEO's attention early.
Support the preparation of presentations, reports, proposals and other executive-level documents.
Budgeting & Financial Planning Support
Assist with the preparation and monitoring of budgets for projects, travel, events and other CEO-related activities.
Research and compare costs to support informed financial decisions.
Track approved expenditure and maintain accurate records.
Support financial planning by gathering relevant information, analysing costs and preparing summaries for the CEO.
Liaise with relevant internal team members on budgets, expenses and financial requirements.
Team & Stakeholder Coordination
Serve as a key coordination point between the CEO and members of the executive or management team.
Follow up with team members on agreed actions and deadlines on behalf of the CEO.
Obtain information, reports and updates required by the CEO.
Coordinate internal activities and information flow without assuming responsibility for the CEO's relationships or representing the CEO in external meetings.
Maintain professional relationships with key internal and external contacts as required.
Executive Office Administration
Prepare meeting agendas, briefing materials and relevant documentation.
Maintain organised records of key documents, reports, plans and correspondence.
Handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion.
Manage routine correspondence and communications requiring the CEO's attention.
Ensure important information is appropriately prioritised and brought to the CEO's attention.
Undertake other executive office responsibilities that support the effective functioning of the CEO's office.
KEY COMPETENCIES
Executive planning and organisation
Research and analytical thinking
Commercial awareness
Strategic thinking
Financial and budget awareness
Project coordination
Excellent written and verbal communication
Attention to detail
Problem-solving and initiative
Ability to prioritise competing demands
Confidentiality and discretion
Ability to work with senior executives and diverse teams
Strong follow-through and accountability
Ability to anticipate needs rather than simply respond to instructions
EDUCATIONAL & EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS
Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Economics, Social Sciences, Management, Communications or a related discipline.
3-5 years' relevant experience, preferably supporting a CEO, Managing Director, Founder, Executive Director or senior executive.
Experience in research, business analysis, consulting, project coordination or strategy support will be an advantage.
Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office/Google Workspace, particularly Excel, PowerPoint and Word.
Ability to conduct structured online research and synthesise information into concise executive-level reports.
Experience working with budgets, schedules, project plans or business reports is desirable.
PERSONAL ATTRIBUTES
The successful candidate should be:
Intelligent and naturally curious.
Highly organised and structured.
Proactive rather than purely reactive.
Comfortable working independently.
Commercially minded and interested in understanding how the business operates.
Comfortable dealing with senior executives and different levels of staff.
Able to handle confidential information with maturity.
Calm under pressure and capable of managing multiple priorities.
A strong researcher who can distinguish useful information from noise.
Someone who thinks ahead, plans ahead and follows through.
SUCCESS IN THE ROLE
Success will be measured by the extent to which the Executive Assistant enables the CEO to operate more effectively by:
Keeping priorities, schedules and commitments well organised.
Providing timely and useful research and analysis.
Ensuring important actions are followed through.
Improving the CEO's preparation for key decisions and engagements.
Supporting effective planning and budget management.
Keeping the CEO informed without creating unnecessary administrative noise.
Anticipating requirements and resolving issues before they become problems.

Company Details:
International cooperation between Germany and Nigeria commenced in 1974. GIZ was initially represented by an office in Lagos until 2003, but since 2004 it has maintained a country office and four project offices in the new capital Abuja. At present, GIZ has around 25 seconded staff, 100 Nigerian and...read moreregional experts, and four CIM experts working in Nigeria.

Nigeria is Africa’s largest economy and has a population of 175 million, making it the continent’s most populous country. With a young, highly motivated and growing population, abundant natural resources and an increasingly diversified economy, Nigeria is not only a regional power but also an increasingly significant political player on the African continent and in the world. However, Nigeria faces major challenges. So far, its substantial oil revenues have had little impact on poverty. More than two-thirds of the population still live in extreme poverty and unemployment remains high. Sustainable economic and social development is hampered by corruption and by regional, ethnic, religious and social differences and the associated conflicts, which sometimes lead to attacks and unrest.

As agreed between the Nigerian and German Governments, GIZ’s activities since 2002 have focused on sustainable economic development. GIZ is also engaged in the energy sector, agriculture and regional integration.

The 'Pro-poor Growth and Employment Promotion in Nigeria’ (SEDIN) programme aims to increase income-generating employment in micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), and improve access to financial services. The programme is currently being implemented in Abuja and in Niger, Ogun and Plateau states.

The Nigerian and German Governments also cooperate in the energy sector. On behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), GIZ provides advisory services to Nigerian partners on topics such as rural electrification, energy efficiency and renewable energies, and is contributing to the success of the Nigeria-German Energy Partnership (NGEP) as well.

GIZ provides support to the ECOWAS Commission (Economic Community of West African States) in Abuja, focusing on the management, implementation and monitoring of ECOWAS decisions on economic and trade policy, and peace and security.

In addition, two regional programmes focusing on agriculture are under way in Nigeria. The first aims to promote African rice value chains; the second builds the capacities of market-oriented small-scale farming. The purpose of both programmes is to achieve sustainable improvements in the livelihoods and food security of poor farmers in Nigeria and other West African countries.

A distinctive feature of GIZ’s activities in Nigeria is the high level of cofinancing obtained from other sources, primarily the European Union (EU) and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. These additional funds make it possible to broaden the scope and intensity of the programmes being implemented on behalf of the BMZ, boosting the effectiveness of German development cooperation with Nigeria.

Job Title: Call for Proposal for Consultancy to Review and Strengthen the LGA Development Plans of Biu, Kwaya Kusar and Guyuk to Make them More Gender Responsive and Climate Smart
Job Description:
Project Title:Support to Improving Social Cohesion through Community Development Planning in 3 LGAs in North-East Nigeria
Implementing Partners:
CODERHI, CRUDAN and YAHARAKARI, in partnership with Oxfam
Project Locations:
Biu and Kwaya Kusar LGAs, Borno State, and Guyuk LGA, Adamawa State
RFQ Reference No.: CODERHI/CDP/RFP/CON/2026
Background
CODERHI, CRUDAN and YAHARAKARI, in partnership with Oxfam, are implementing the project
“Support to Improving Social Cohesion through Community Development Planning”
across 31 wards in Guyuk LGA of Adamawa State and Biu and Kwaya Kusar LGAs of Borno State, with support from Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH and funding from the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the European Union (EU).
The project promotes inclusive governance, social cohesion and participatory development planning by strengthening engagement between communities and Local Government Area (LGA) authorities. Through participatory Community Development Planning (CDP) processes, communities have identified and articulated their development priorities, which have informed the development of LGA Development Plans for Biu, Kwaya Kusar and Guyuk.
The three LGA Development Plans provide a framework for addressing development priorities across ten sectors in each LGA. They are intended to support more effective linkage between community priorities, LGA planning and budgeting processes, implementation and service delivery.
However, for these plans to remain relevant, inclusive and responsive to emerging development challenges, there is a need to assess the extent to which gender considerations and climate change adaptation measures are adequately reflected across the plans.
Women, men, youth, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable and marginalized groups may experience development challenges differently and may have unequal access to resources, services, opportunities and decision-making processes. Similarly, climate-related risks such as flooding, drought, heat, water scarcity, soil degradation and changing agricultural conditions can affect sectors and population groups differently.
The consortium therefore seeks to engage a qualified consultant or consulting firm to
review and strengthen the existing LGA Development Plans for Biu, Kwaya Kusar and Guyuk
, with particular focus on gender responsiveness, inclusion, climate change adaptation and climate-smart development.
The assignment is
not intended to develop new LGA Development Plans
. Rather, it will strengthen the existing plans while preserving the original community-identified problems, priorities, demands and overall planning structure.
Purpose of the Consultancy
The purpose of this consultancy is to strengthen the existing LGA Development Plans for Biu, Kwaya Kusar and Guyuk by systematically identifying gender and climate-related gaps and integrating appropriate, practical and context-specific measures into the existing priorities and interventions.
The review should improve the plans' usefulness for LGA planning, budgeting, implementation and monitoring while ensuring that the original community priorities remain substantially intact.
Objectives of the Consultancy
The specific objectives are to:
Conduct a systematic gender gap analysis of the existing LGA Development Plans for Biu, Kwaya Kusar and Guyuk.
Assess the extent to which the plans reflect the differentiated needs and circumstances of women, men, youth, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable and marginalized groups.
Assess the extent to which climate change risks, adaptation measures and climate-smart considerations are reflected across the ten sectors of each plan.
Identify gender and climate-related gaps, risks, opportunities and practical entry points for strengthening the existing plans.
Incorporate appropriate gender considerations, gender-responsive language and relevant gender-responsive projects into the existing plans.
Incorporate appropriate climate change adaptation measures and climate-smart projects into relevant sectors and priorities.
Ensure that proposed gender-responsive and climate-smart interventions are practical, contextually relevant and capable of informing subsequent LGA planning and budgeting processes.
Facilitate stakeholder validation of the proposed revisions in the three LGAs.
Produce three validated and strengthened LGA Development Plans, together with an integration matrix and final consultancy report.
Scope of the Assignment
The consultant/consulting firm will review the existing LGA Development Plans for:
Biu LGA – Borno State
Kwaya Kusar LGA – Borno State
Guyuk LGA – Adamawa State
The review will cover the
ten sectors contained in each LGA Development Plan
.
The assignment will include:
Review of Existing Plans
The consultant will conduct a systematic review of the existing plans to understand the existing problems, priorities, proposed solutions, projects and interventions and assess the extent to which gender and climate considerations are already reflected.
Gender Gap Analysis
The consultant will:
Identify gender gaps across the ten sectors;
Assess the extent to which the needs of women, men, youth, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups are reflected;
Assess issues relating to participation, access to services and resources, decision-making and expected benefits;
Identify areas requiring gender-responsive strengthening; and
Apply appropriate gender analysis tools and frameworks.
Climate Change and Adaptation Assessment
The consultant will:
Assess existing climate change and environmental considerations within the plans;
Identify relevant climate risks and vulnerabilities;
Assess the adequacy of existing adaptation measures;
Identify opportunities for strengthening climate resilience;
Identify appropriate climate-smart projects and interventions; and
Consider the differentiated effects of climate change on vulnerable groups.
Integrated Gender and Climate Mainstreaming
The consultant will ensure that gender and climate considerations are appropriately integrated rather than treated only as separate components.
The review should establish a clear relationship between:
Identified gap/risk → affected population → proposed adjustment/intervention → expected result → indicator/target, where applicable.
Proposed interventions should also avoid creating or worsening environmental problems and should promote environmentally sustainable approaches where relevant.
Stakeholder Engagement and Validation
The consultant will engage relevant stakeholders, including:
LGA political and administrative leadership;
Relevant LGA departments and sector officials;
Planning and budgeting officials;
WDSCs/LGDCC/CDPIT and community representatives;
Women and youth representatives;
Persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups;
Traditional and community leaders;
Relevant state-level stakeholders; and
Other stakeholders considered necessary.
Stakeholder engagement will help verify findings, identify additional gaps and validate the proposed revisions.
Particular attention shall be given to ensuring that the revised plans
do not change the original community-identified problems and priorities without proper justification and stakeholder agreement
.
Expected Deliverables
The successful consultant/consulting firm will be expected to deliver:
Deliverable 1: Inception Report and Detailed Workplan
The inception report should include:
Understanding of the assignment;
Proposed methodology;
Review and assessment approach;
Gender analysis approach;
Climate assessment approach;
Stakeholder engagement and validation approach;
Proposed team composition and roles; and
Detailed start-to-finish workplan for the 19-working-day assignment.
Deliverable 2: Gender and Climate Assessment
A systematic assessment of the three existing LGA Development Plans and their ten sectors, identifying:
Gender gaps;
Climate-related gaps and risks;
Opportunities for strengthening;
Relevant gender considerations;
Climate adaptation opportunities; and
Proposed practical adjustments to existing priorities and interventions.
The assessment findings should directly inform the revised plans.
Deliverable 3: Gender and Climate Integration Matrix
A practical matrix demonstrating how identified gaps and risks have informed the strengthening of the plans.
The matrix should, as appropriate, include:
Existing Sector/Priority
Gender Gap
Climate Gap/Risk/Opportunity
Proposed Gender-Responsive Adjustment
Proposed Climate Adaptation/Climate-Smart Adjustment
Indicator/Target, where applicable
Deliverable 4: Three Strengthened LGA Development Plans
The consultant will submit strengthened and revised plans for:
Biu LGA;
Kwaya Kusar LGA; and
Guyuk LGA.
The revised plans must maintain the existing planning structure and incorporate agreed and relevant gender and climate considerations, including gender-responsive and climate-smart projects.
Deliverable 5: Stakeholder Validation Outputs
The consultant will facilitate and document validation of the proposed revisions and incorporate agreed feedback into the final plans.
Deliverable 6: Final Consultancy Report
The final report should document:
Activities undertaken;
Methodology used;
Key findings;
Gender gaps identified;
Climate-related gaps identified;
Adjustments and interventions incorporated;
Stakeholder engagement and validation;
Key recommendations;
Lessons learned; and
Relevant annexes.
Duration
The assignment is expected to be completed within
19 working days
across Borno and Adamawa States.
Interested consultants/consulting firms should demonstrate that the proposed methodology and workplan can realistically deliver all required outputs within the specified timeframe.
The consultant will be required to provide a detailed start-to-finish workplan showing activities, locations, timelines and expected deliverables.
Required Qualifications and Experience
The assignment may be undertaken by an individual consultant or a consulting firm.
Academic Qualifications
The lead consultant/team leader should possess at least a
Master's degree or equivalent advanced qualification
in one or more of the following fields:
Gender Studies;
Development Studies;
Social Sciences;
Sociology;
Public Policy;
Policy and Strategic Studies;
Local Government Administration;
Environmental Sciences;
Climate Change;
Social Protection; or
Other relevant fields.
Where a consulting firm is applying, the proposed team should collectively demonstrate complementary qualifications relevant to the assignment.
Professional Experience
Applicants should demonstrate:
At least
5 years of relevant professional experience
in gender equality, social development, development planning, governance or related fields;
Demonstrated experience in gender analysis and gender mainstreaming;
Experience reviewing policies, development plans or programmes;
Experience integrating gender considerations into development planning;
Knowledge and practical understanding of climate change adaptation and climate-smart development;
Experience in local government development planning and/or participatory planning;
Understanding of local government planning and budgeting processes;
Experience facilitating stakeholder consultations and validation processes;
Experience working with government institutions and community structures;
Understanding of the socio-cultural and governance context of North-East Nigeria;
Strong analytical, report-writing and facilitation skills; and
Demonstrated ability to deliver assignments within tight timelines.
Experience working in Borno and/or Adamawa States will be an advantage.
Knowledge of relevant local languages, particularly
Hausa and/or Bura
, will be an added advantage.
For consulting firms, the proposal should clearly identify the proposed team members, their roles and relevant experience.
8. Key Guiding Principle
A fundamental requirement of this assignment is the
preservation of community-identified priorities
.
The consultant shall not remove, substitute or materially alter existing community-identified problems, priorities or demands.
Gender and climate considerations should be used to
strengthen, clarify, make more inclusive, sustainable and actionable
the existing priorities.
Where a proposed adjustment could materially change an existing priority or introduce what could reasonably be considered a new priority, the proposed change must be clearly identified and subjected to stakeholder validation and agreement before incorporation.
Proposal Requirements
Interested consultants/consulting firms should submit a
Technical and Financial Proposal
containing the following:
A. Technical Proposal
The technical proposal should include:
Understanding of the assignment;
Proposed methodology and approach;
Approach to reviewing the ten sectors across the three LGAs;
Approach to gender gap analysis;
Approach to climate change and adaptation assessment;
Approach to integrating gender and climate considerations;
Approach to stakeholder engagement and validation;
Proposed team composition and roles, where applicable;
Relevant previous experience; and
Detailed workplan demonstrating how the assignment will be completed within 19 working days.
B. Financial Proposal
The financial proposal should provide a clear and detailed cost breakdown, including:
Professional fees;
Applicable logistics/operational costs;
Applicable taxes;
Any other relevant costs.
The financial proposal should represent
value for money
and remain realistic in relation to the scope and duration of the assignment.
Supporting Documents
Applicants should provide:
Current professional CV(s);
Evidence of relevant previous assignments;
At least one sample/report of a similar completed assignment;
Certificate or evidence of satisfactory completion of similar work, where available;
Registration documents, where applicable;
Tax clearance/TIN documentation;
SCUML certificate, where applicable; and
Any other relevant supporting documents.
10. Proposal Evaluation
Proposals will be assessed based on the following broad criteria:
Evaluation Area
Consideration
Understanding of the assignment
Demonstrated understanding of the purpose, scope and expected results
Methodology and technical approach
Quality, practicality and relevance of proposed methodology
Relevant experience
Experience in gender, climate, development planning, governance and related assignments
Team qualifications
Qualifications and experience of proposed consultant/team
Workplan
Realistic and achievable 19-working-day workplan
Similar assignments
Evidence of successful delivery of comparable assignments
Financial proposal
Cost reasonableness and value for money
The consortium reserves the right to seek clarification from applicants where necessary during the evaluation process.
Consultancy Management and Coordination
The consultancy will be implemented collaboratively by
CODERHI, CRUDAN and YAHARAKARI
, with CODERHI providing overall operational coordination and managing the approved budget line.
Oxfam will provide strategic guidance, technical support, quality assurance and oversight.
The selected consultant/consulting firm will work closely with the consortium, relevant LGA authorities and other identified stakeholders throughout the assignment.
A designated CODERHI focal person will serve as the primary day-to-day contact for the consultant, with CRUDAN, YAHARAKARI and Oxfam involved as appropriate.
12. Payment
Payment will be made against satisfactory completion and acceptance of agreed deliverables.
The proposed payment structure is:

Payments will be subject to applicable financial procedures, statutory deductions and the terms of the consultancy contract.

Risk Management & Cost Control

JOB PURPOSE
The Internal Auditor provides independent and objective assurance on the effectiveness of the school’s risk management, internal control, and governance systems. The role ensures that financial and operational activities are conducted in compliance with established policies, legal requirements, and best practices, safeguarding the school’s assets, promoting transparency, and supporting sustainable growth.
OVERVIEW OF THE ROLE
This position is responsible for leading the design, implementation, and review of internal audit frameworks across all departments. The Internal Auditor evaluates the adequacy of controls, identifies risks, ensures compliance with policies, and provides recommendations to enhance efficiency, accountability, and value for money
RELATIONSHIPS
The Internal Auditor is selected by the Director of Schools in consultation with the Head of Operations and HR.
The Internal Auditor reports directly to the Director of School. However, in the absence of the Director, he/she will report to the Head of Operations who will also provide strategic leadership and day to day oversight. The Internal Auditor works closely with the Accounts team, staff, vendors, and external auditors.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Internal Control Framework
Design, implement, and continuously improve internal control systems to safeguard school assets, prevent fraud, and ensure operational efficiency.
Establish clear processes for authorization, approval, and accountability across departments.
Risk Management & Assessment
Conduct periodic risk assessments across academic and administrative functions to identify vulnerabilities and recommend corrective measures.
Maintain a risk register and report emerging risks to senior leadership.
Internal Audits & Monitoring
Carry out routine and surprise internal audits covering finance, procurement, payroll, admissions, inventory, and other key operations.
Track compliance with policies, identify gaps, and recommend improvements.
Governance & Compliance
Develop and maintain governance frameworks, policies, and procedures to ensure transparency and accountability.
Ensure compliance with financial regulations, labour laws, safeguarding standards, and international best practices relevant to schools.
Reporting & Documentation
Prepare timely reports on internal control effectiveness, risks, and incidents for the Head of School, Board, and Audit Committee.
Maintain accurate records of audit findings, follow-ups, and resolutions.
Training & Capacity Building
Deliver training sessions for staff on internal controls, financial discipline, compliance, and risk awareness.
Provide guidance to managers to strengthen departmental controls and accountability.
Incident Investigation & Resolution
Investigate reported cases of fraud, mismanagement, or policy breaches, ensuring confidentiality and fairness.
Recommend disciplinary or corrective actions where necessary.
Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement
Work closely with external auditors, regulators, and other stakeholders during audits, inspections, or reviews.
Partner with Finance, HR, Admin, and Academic teams to embed strong internal control practices across the school
QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Risk Management, or related field
Professional certification in internal auditing, risk management, or related field (e.g., CIA, CRMA, CIMA)
Experience working in internal controls, risk management, or auditing, preferably in an educational setting
Knowledge of financial regulations and laws applicable to schools
Excellent analytical, communication, and organisational skills
Ability to work accurately and attention to detail

Job Description:
Background
The Gombe State Delivery and Insights Unit (SDIU) aims to strengthen the state’s existing health-system architecture by creating a consistent mechanism that connects data, management decisions, coordinated implementation, follow-up and escalation.
The SDIU works to strengthen existing statutory functions and connect them into one repeatable evidence-to-decision-to-action cycle. it will connect leadership structures, technical forums, delivery agencies and data systems into one government-led decision-to-action mechanism.
The SDIU is not intended to operate as a parallel programme management unit, replace existing government institutions, duplicate technical committees, or assume responsibility for programme implementation.
Role Purpose
To serve as the analytical-management bridge within the DMU by converting fragmented technical updates, committee submissions, Execution Grant progress, AOP tracking and DIU findings into concise management problems and decision-ready briefs.
The role interprets implementation, institutional dependencies and programme progress and translates them into management decisions.
Key Responsibilities
Consolidate implementation evidence:
Receive and synthesize submissions from existing technical committees and TWGs.
Review Execution Grant milestones, AOP actions and partner implementation updates.
Identify duplicate, inconsistent or conflicting progress reports across mechanisms.
Frame management problems:
Work with DIU colleagues to determine whether a programme concern is supported by available evidence.
Develop structured problem statements covering what is happening, where, since when, likely drivers, what has already been tried and what decision is needed.
Distinguish technical issues, coordination issues and matters requiring leadership authority.
Prepare decision products:
Prepare TMT decision briefs with options, implications and recommended accountable institutions.
Maintain a cross-cutting view of dependencies across service delivery, financing, supply chain, HRH and data.
Support the Senior TA in identifying repeated system constraints requiring policy or structural action.
Minimize reporting burden:
Avoid creating additional programme reporting requests where AOP, grant or committee reports can provide the necessary information.
Work with the TMT Secretary to establish one authoritative action narrative for each priority issue.
Key Deliverables
Monthly integrated programme-performance narrative.
Decision briefs for TMT agenda items.
Cross-cutting risk and dependency register.
Quarterly analysis of repeated delivery bottlenecks.
Consolidated view of AOP and Execution Grant risks.
Suggested performance indicators:
Percentage of TMT agenda items supported by decision-ready briefs.
Reduction in agenda items returned because evidence or decision asks are unclear.
Evidence that TMT decisions increasingly address root causes rather than symptoms.
Recommended Profile / Capabilities
Mid-to-senior programme-management professional with strong public-health understanding and background
Minimum of 7 years of relevant professional experience in programme analysis, management
Master’s Degree in a relevant field is desirable.
Strong analytical reasoning and structured problem solving.

Background

The Gombe State Execution Grant and technical support to the State Delivery/Health Delivery Implementation Unit (SDIU/HDIU).
Health-facility performance, PHC functionality, implementation discipline, quality improvement, and accountability initiatives.
Technical assistance to the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, including Health Systems Strengthening (HSS) and Human Resources for Health (HRH).

Job Description:
Job Objective
The Soft Service Supervisor will be responsible for the direct, hands-on supervision and coordination of daily soft service operations within the hospital. The role holder will ensure the effective execution of all housekeeping, portering, and minor front-of-house tasks to the highest standards of cleanliness, safety, and efficiency.
He/ She will monitor daily operations, train staff, and uphold the pristine environmental standards required in an international healthcare setting.
Key Accountabilities/Responsibilities
Daily Operational Supervision & Task Management
Conduct daily briefings with housekeeping, portering, and front-of-house teams to assign tasks and communicate priorities.
Create and distribute daily work schedules and assignment sheets for all direct reports.
Perform continuous rounds across all assigned zones (patient rooms, ORs, public areas) to monitor cleanliness and service delivery in real-time.
Reallocate resources dynamically in response to emergencies, spills, or high-priority requests.
Ensure all daily, weekly, and monthly cleaning checklists are completed and signed off by the relevant staff.
Verify the completion and quality of terminal cleans upon patient discharge.

Perform scheduled and random quality audits using standardized checklists for all cleaning and portering activities.
Ensure all cleaning practices adhere to IPC policies and relevant standards (JCI, ISO, etc.).
Monitor and enforce strict compliance with isolation cleaning procedures in designated patient rooms.
Check and ensure all cleaning carts are properly stocked, organized, and compliant with safety standards.
Audit documentation, such as cleaning logs and checklists, for accuracy and completeness.
Report any non-compliance issues immediately to the Soft Services Manager and take provisional action.

Perform daily checks of cleaning supply levels on carts and in storage closets; initiate restocking requests.
Supervise the proper use, storage, and basic maintenance of all cleaning equipment (e.g., vacuums, scrubbers, buffers).
Report faulty equipment to the maintenance team or vendors and track until resolved.
Ensure all chemicals are correctly labeled, stored in compliance with SDS, and used at the appropriate dilutions.
Manage the inventory of portering equipment (wheelchairs, stretchers), ensuring they are clean, functional, and available.
Conduct monthly physical inventory counts of supplies and equipment.
Patient Portering & Transport Coordination
Monitor the portering request system (digital or manual) and dispatch porters efficiently.
Supervise porters to ensure timely, safe, and courteous transport of patients and specimens.
Audit porter adherence to patient handling techniques and infection control protocols (e.g., hand hygiene, cleaning transport equipment after each use).
Investigate and resolve delays or complaints related to patient transport services.
Coordinate portering support for emergency cases and scheduled admissions/discharges.
Maintain a log of portering activities and response times for performance review.
Customer Service & Stakeholder Communication
Serve as the first point of contact for cleaning and portering-related queries from patients, visitors, and clinical staff.
Proactively engage with nursing unit managers to understand specific departmental needs and concerns.
Ensure front-of-house staff provide a warm, professional, and helpful welcome to all visitors.
Respond promptly and professionally to service complaints, resolving them where possible and escalating complex issues to the Manager.
Collect and document feedback from internal customers to identify trends and improvement areas.
Maintain a positive and collaborative relationship with the on-site teams from outsourced service providers.
Safety, Risk Management & Incident Reporting
Enforce strict adherence to occupational health and safety protocols, including PPE usage and ergonomic practices.
Conduct regular safety inspections of work areas, storage rooms, and equipment.
Lead the initial response to spills, accidents, or incidents, ensuring proper containment and cleanup.
Investigate and document all safety incidents, near-misses, and hazardous conditions within the team.
Promote a culture of safety by encouraging staff to report hazards and near-misses without fear.
Ensure the correct and safe disposal of general and clinical waste according to hospital policy.
Pest Control & Waste Management Monitoring
Conduct daily visual inspections in key areas (kitchens, pantries, waste holding areas) for signs of pest activity.
Ensure bait stations are intact and report any issues to the pest control vendor via the Manager.
Supervise the segregation and disposal of different waste streams (clinical, general, recyclable) by housekeeping staff.
Monitor the cleanliness of waste storage areas and ensure schedules for waste removal are followed.
Train staff on integrated pest management (IPM) principles and proper waste handling procedures.
Maintain accurate logs for pest sighting reports and waste management checks.
Administrative Duties & Reporting
Maintain daily attendance and timekeeping records for all direct reports.
Compile and submit daily activity reports to the Soft Services Manager, highlighting achievements, issues, and metrics.
Complete incident reports and hazard identification forms in a timely and accurate manner.
Assist the Manager in preparing data for monthly performance and KPI reviews.
Manage the leave roster, ensuring adequate coverage for all shifts and areas.
Participate in departmental meetings and contribute to operational planning.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Facilities Management, Hospitality Management, Business Administration, Public Health, or a related field.
Experience in housekeeping or environmental services management, preferably within the healthcare industry.
Experience in optimizing workflows, reducing costs, and improving service delivery.
Knowledge of integrated pest management (IPM) and sanitation protocols.
Experience managing departmental budgets and cost-saving initiatives.
Proficiency in using facilities management software, inventory management systems, and MS Office Suite.
Experience working in JCI-accredited or international hospitals is a strong advantage.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, and negotiation skills, with a strong focus on customer service.
Must have skills
Clinical Cleaning
Public Health
Infection Control andPrevention

Job Summary
The Cashier is responsible for accurately processing all customer payments and financial transactions at the filling station while maintaining excellent customer service and strict accountability for cash received.
The role involves receiving payments for fuel, lubricants and other products or services sold at the station, issuing receipts, maintaining accurate transaction records, reconciling daily sales and cash collections, and ensuring that all funds are properly accounted for and handed over in accordance with company procedures.
The Cashier reports directly to the Station Manager and is expected to maintain the highest standards of integrity, accuracy, confidentiality, professionalism and financial accountability.
Key Responsibilities
Cash Handling & Payment Processing:
Receive and process payments from customers for fuel, lubricants and other products sold at the station.
Process cash, POS/card, bank transfer and other approved payment methods accurately.
Verify payments before confirming transactions or releasing goods/services where applicable.
Provide customers with accurate receipts and appropriate change.
Maintain strict accountability for all cash and payment transactions handled during each shift.
Ensure personal funds are never mixed with company funds.
Daily Sales Reconciliation:
Reconcile cash collected against sales records, POS transactions, transfers and other payment records at the end of each shift.
Ensure that total collections correspond with recorded sales.
Prepare accurate daily/shift cashier reports.
Immediately report shortages, overages, payment discrepancies or suspicious transactions to the Station Manager.
Properly hand over cash, transaction records and supporting documents at the end of each shift.
Transaction Recording & Documentation:
Maintain accurate and complete records of all transactions.
Ensure receipts, POS slips, transfer confirmations and other transaction documents are properly maintained.
Follow established procedures for cancelled, reversed, failed or disputed transactions.
Assist with maintaining financial records required for daily, weekly and monthly station reconciliation.
Ensure transaction information is entered correctly into the station's approved system or register.
Customer Service:
Attend to customers courteously, promptly and professionally.
Respond appropriately to customer enquiries relating to payments, receipts and transactions.
Escalate customer complaints or transaction disputes to the Station Manager where necessary.
Maintain a professional attitude even when handling difficult customers or payment disputes.
Help create a positive and efficient customer experience at the station.
Cash & Financial Control:
Safeguard cash and other financial instruments under the Cashier's custody.
Follow all company cash-handling, banking and financial-control procedures.
Never approve unauthorized discounts, refunds, credits or transaction adjustments.
Maintain confidentiality regarding company sales, revenue and other financial information.
Immediately report suspected fraud, theft, counterfeit currency or other irregularities.
Cooperate fully with internal audits, cash counts and financial reviews.
POS & Payment Terminal Management:
Operate POS terminals and other approved payment systems correctly.
Confirm successful POS transactions before treating payments as completed.
Monitor failed or reversed transactions and escalate unresolved issues.
Keep POS terminals and related equipment secure.
Report malfunctioning payment equipment or connectivity problems promptly.
Shift Handover:
Complete all required reconciliation before handing over to another cashier.
Clearly document outstanding transactions or unresolved discrepancies.
Ensure cash, receipts and transaction records are properly transferred and acknowledged.
Never leave the cashier position unattended without following the approved handover procedure.
Compliance, Safety & Station Procedures:
Comply with all company policies, operational procedures and financial-control requirements.
Observe filling-station safety procedures and applicable health and safety requirements.
Maintain a clean, organized and secure cashier/work area.
Participate in staff meetings, training programmes and operational briefings.
Carry out other reasonable duties assigned by the Station Manager.
Requirements
Interested candidates should possess relevant qualifications with experience.
Eligible Applicants: Female applicants preferably for gender balance.

Job Summary
The Cashier is responsible for accurately processing all customer payments and financial transactions at the filling station while maintaining excellent customer service and strict accountability for cash received.
The role involves receiving payments for fuel, lubricants and other products or services sold at the station, issuing receipts, maintaining accurate transaction records, reconciling daily sales and cash collections, and ensuring that all funds are properly accounted for and handed over in accordance with company procedures.
The Cashier reports directly to the Station Manager and is expected to maintain the highest standards of integrity, accuracy, confidentiality, professionalism and financial accountability.
Key Responsibilities
Cash Handling & Payment Processing:
Receive and process payments from customers for fuel, lubricants and other products sold at the station.
Process cash, POS/card, bank transfer and other approved payment methods accurately.
Verify payments before confirming transactions or releasing goods/services where applicable.
Provide customers with accurate receipts and appropriate change.
Maintain strict accountability for all cash and payment transactions handled during each shift.
Ensure personal funds are never mixed with company funds.
Daily Sales Reconciliation:
Reconcile cash collected against sales records, POS transactions, transfers and other payment records at the end of each shift.
Ensure that total collections correspond with recorded sales.
Prepare accurate daily/shift cashier reports.
Immediately report shortages, overages, payment discrepancies or suspicious transactions to the Station Manager.
Properly hand over cash, transaction records and supporting documents at the end of each shift.
Transaction Recording & Documentation:
Maintain accurate and complete records of all transactions.
Ensure receipts, POS slips, transfer confirmations and other transaction documents are properly maintained.
Follow established procedures for cancelled, reversed, failed or disputed transactions.
Assist with maintaining financial records required for daily, weekly and monthly station reconciliation.
Ensure transaction information is entered correctly into the station's approved system or register.
Customer Service:
Attend to customers courteously, promptly and professionally.
Respond appropriately to customer enquiries relating to payments, receipts and transactions.
Escalate customer complaints or transaction disputes to the Station Manager where necessary.
Maintain a professional attitude even when handling difficult customers or payment disputes.
Help create a positive and efficient customer experience at the station.
Cash & Financial Control:
Safeguard cash and other financial instruments under the Cashier's custody.
Follow all company cash-handling, banking and financial-control procedures.
Never approve unauthorized discounts, refunds, credits or transaction adjustments.
Maintain confidentiality regarding company sales, revenue and other financial information.
Immediately report suspected fraud, theft, counterfeit currency or other irregularities.
Cooperate fully with internal audits, cash counts and financial reviews.
POS & Payment Terminal Management:
Operate POS terminals and other approved payment systems correctly.
Confirm successful POS transactions before treating payments as completed.
Monitor failed or reversed transactions and escalate unresolved issues.
Keep POS terminals and related equipment secure.
Report malfunctioning payment equipment or connectivity problems promptly.
Shift Handover:
Complete all required reconciliation before handing over to another cashier.
Clearly document outstanding transactions or unresolved discrepancies.
Ensure cash, receipts and transaction records are properly transferred and acknowledged.
Never leave the cashier position unattended without following the approved handover procedure.
Compliance, Safety & Station Procedures:
Comply with all company policies, operational procedures and financial-control requirements.
Observe filling-station safety procedures and applicable health and safety requirements.
Maintain a clean, organized and secure cashier/work area.
Participate in staff meetings, training programmes and operational briefings.
Carry out other reasonable duties assigned by the Station Manager.
Requirements
Interested candidates should possess an HND / Bachelor`s Degree with 1 - 5 years experience

Company Details:
The Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is a humanitarian, non-governmental, non-profit organisation founded in 1956 that works in more than 30 countries throughout the world.

DRC fulfils its mandate by providing direct assistance to conflict-affected populations - refugees, internally displaced people...read more(IDPs) and host communities in the conflict areas of the world; and by advocating on behalf of conflict-affected populations internationally, and in Denmark, on the basis of humanitarian principles and the Human Rights Declaration. We understand "durable solutions" as any means by which the situation of refugees can be permanently and satisfactorily resolved, enabling them to live normal lives. Durable solutions can be voluntary repatriation, local integration or resettlement. In Denmark, DRC assists refugees in all aspects of integration as well as asylum procedures. Internationally, DRC actively participates in supporting the protection of refugees, and promoting durable solutions for conflict-affected populations.

The DRC’s supreme authority is the Council, which consists of up to three representatives of each member organisation, six representatives of the voluntary groups and refugee counselling organisations cooperating with the Danish Refugee Council, and of the Executive Committee.
DRC is an umbrella organisation and is currently consisting of 30 organisation members and voluntary groups, committed to the refugee cause. Membership of the DRC is open to non-party-political, voluntary, nationwide humanitarian and international organisations that work on a democratic basis, and whose aims conform to those of the DRC.

Job Summary
We are seeking an experienced SRE to engineer the reliability of our highly distributed platform.
You will combine deep knowledge of distributed systems with strong coding skills to define SLOs, lead incident response, and build automation and self-healing mechanisms into our systems.
You will balance immediate operational stability with long-term strategic engineering to ensure our services scale linearly with our hyper-growth.
Responsibilities
Participate in on-call rotations as the primary technical lead. Act as the Incident Commander during major severity incidents: initiating war rooms, coordinating cross-functional teams, and providing clear status updates.
Instrument code to expose high-cardinality metrics and distributed traces. Collaboratively define, measure, and defend Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and Error Budgets with product owners.
Write high-quality, production-ready code (in Java, Go, or Python) to build internal tooling, automation platforms, and self-healing mechanisms that eliminate manual operator intervention.
Partner with Product Engineering teams during the design phase to ensure new services are built with reliability, scalability, and observability patterns (circuit breakers, rate limiting, backpressure, fallback strategies) from day one.
Analyze system performance and traffic patterns to model future capacity needs. Conduct load testing and chaos engineering experiments to verify system resilience under failure conditions.
Requirements
Minimum of 5 years of experience in SRE or Backend Engineering with a strong ability to write clean, performant, and tested code in Java, Go, Rust, or Python.
Deep understanding of distributed systems architecture and design patterns. You possess a strong command of microservices fundamentals, event-driven architectures, and the underlying principles required to build systems that scale.
Extensive experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP) or similar cloud providers (AWS/Azure). You are proficient in running production workloads on Kubernetes (GKE/EKS) and troubleshooting cluster/infrastructure issues.
Experience designing observability strategies using OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, New Relic, Datadog, or SigNoz to improve system visibility.
Familiarity with operating and tuning production data stores (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL) and streaming platforms (e.g., Kafka, RabbitMQ) in a high-throughput environment.
What we can offer you
Culture - We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human.
Learning - We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks.
Compensation - You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, annual bonus, plus other benefits.
What to expect in the hiring process
A preliminary phone call with the recruiter
A technical interview with the Hiring Manager
A behavioural and technical interview with a member of the Executive team.

Job Description:
The successful candidate will be the technical focal point for upper and lower completion applications, responsible for developing fit-for-purpose completion solutions, supporting field execution, and driving technical excellence throughout the project lifecycle.
This role requires extensive experience in completion design, packers, safety valves, tubing stress analysis, sand control, and Open Hole Gravel Pack (OHGP) applications.
The candidate must be capable of working directly with customers, field operations, product line teams, and global engineering organizations to deliver safe, reliable, and cost-effective completion systems.
Responsibilities
As an Application Engineer, you will be responsible for:
Leading the design and application engineering of upper and lower completion systems for offshore and onshore projects.
Developing optimized completion architectures based on reservoir, wellbore, and operational requirements.
Selecting and specify completion equipment including production packers, retrievable and permanent packers, SCSSVs, gas lift systems, flow control devices, sliding sleeves, landing nipples, seal assemblies, and intelligent completion components.
Providing technical ownership of OHGP and sand control applications, including screen selection, gravel pack design, and execution support.
Performing detailed engineering analysis including tubing stress, burst, collapse, tension, compression, buckling, thermal effects, packer load calculations, and seal movement evaluations.
Utilizing engineering software such as WellCat and other completion design tools to validate completion designs and operating envelopes.
Reviewing customer requirements and recommend technically compliant and commercially optimized solutions.
Supporting tenders, technical proposals, and customer presentations.
Participating in design reviews, risk assessments and lessons learned workshops.
Providing operational support during equipment preparation, installation, commissioning, and well start-up activities.
Troubleshooting field issues and lead technical investigations, failure analyses, and corrective action recommendations.
Acting as the primary technical interface between the customer, operations teams, manufacturing facilities, and global engineering resources.
Mentor junior engineers and support competency development within the organization.
Requirements
To be successful in this role you will:
Bachelor’s degree in petroleum engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
Minimum 12 years of completion engineering experience with strong exposure to both upper and lower completions.
Proven experience with:
Production Packers
SCSSV Systems
Intelligent Completions
Gas Lift Systems
Sand Control Technologies
Open Hole Gravel Pack (OHGP) Applications
Deepwater and offshore completion systems
Tubing Stress Analysis Software
Demonstrated experience supporting major operator projects and customer-facing engineering activities.
Excellent understanding of well integrity, completion reliability, and field execution best practices.
Experience supporting multidisciplinary project teams in complex drilling and completion environments.
Have excellent customer engagement and communication skills.
Proven ability to lead technical discussions and influence customer decision-making.
Excellent analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced project environment.
Results-oriented mindset with a strong focus on execution and operational excellence.

Job Description:
Job Summary
The scrum master serves as a point person responsible for understanding the big development picture of each sprint. They ensure the team is working on the right tasks at the right time. They also want to ensure the team is fully deployed and not idle. The role of scrum master often involves working closely with the product owner, Business Analyst, Software Developers to translate epics, stories, and other items on the sprint list into actionable tasks for developers and create a transparent outcome-driven delivery environment.
Job Details
Facilitate sprint planning, daily stand-ups, backlog refinement, sprint reviews, retrospectives, and other Agile ceremonies with clear objectives and outcomes.
Facilitating the daily stand-up (sometimes called the daily scrum) and helping the team reach consensus on each of the three questions.
Identify, track, escalate, and drive resolution of blockers, dependencies, risks, and delivery impediments affecting the team.
Promote realistic sprint commitments based on team capacity, historical performance, technical dependencies, and operational obligations.
Encourage Definition of Ready, Definition of Done, acceptance criteria, testability, documentation, and engineering quality practices.
Maintain transparent Agile artefacts, action logs, dependency logs, impediment registers, and delivery dashboards as required.
Support release planning and coordination across Engineering, QA, DevOps, Product, Security, Operations, and other dependent teams.
Facilitate root-cause discussions and improvement actions when delivery targets, quality expectations, or sprint goals are missed.
Support multiple squads or one complex delivery squad depending on organizational structure and delivery needs.
Serves the product owner by:
Making sure everyone on the team understands the project’s goals and scope.
Helping the product owner maintain the product backlog.
Facilitating scrum events (daily stand-ups, other meetings) as needed.
Serves the development team by:
Coaching the development team on self-organization.
Helping to remove obstacles to the developers’ progress.
Facilitating scrum events (daily stand-ups, other meetings) as needed.
Serves the entire organization by:
Encouraging the organization to adopt the scrum methodology in their own workflow.
Coaching the organization on the transition to a scrum working framework.
Keeping the organization, particularly the project’s stakeholders, up to date on the progress of the scrum team’s projects.
