Job Description:
Position Summary
The SRH/GBV Engagement Officer will support IRC's efforts to increase access to and utilization of quality sexual and reproductive health (SRH) and gender-based violence (GBV) services among women, girls, adolescents, and other vulnerable populations affected by conflict and displacement.
The position will serve as an important link between communities, health facilities, WPE/GBV services, and referral partners, helping to ensure that women and girls understand available services, can safely access them, and receive appropriate support throughout the referral process.
The Officer will work closely with community health workers, community volunteers, women's and youth groups, health providers, WPE staff, government counterparts, and other community-based structures to identify barriers to service access and develop appropriate engagement strategies. This will include community dialogue, targeted awareness activities, social and behaviour change approaches, feedback mechanisms, referral support, and engagement with trusted community influencers.
The role will also support the integration of survivor-centered principles into community engagement and referral activities, ensuring that all interactions uphold confidentiality, informed choice, dignity, safety, non-discrimination, and the autonomy of survivors and clients.
The SRH/GBV Engagement Officer will report to the Roving SRH Manager and contribute to IRC's broader objective of improving equitable access to quality SRH and GBV services in humanitarian and underserved settings.
Major Responsibilities
Community Engagement and Service Uptake
Develop community activities that raise awareness and encourage people to use available sexual and reproductive health (SRH) and gender-based violence (GBV) services.
Work with community health workers, volunteers, women’s groups, youth groups, traditional and religious leaders, and other trusted community members to share clear and relevant information with women and girls.
Organize community meetings and small-group discussions on SRH, GBV prevention, available services, referral options, and challenges people face when seeking care.
Identify barriers to accessing services, including social, cultural, financial, distance, and other practical challenges, and work with communities and programme teams to find realistic solutions.
Promote informed, voluntary, and respectful access to SRH services, including family planning and maternal health care, while raising awareness of GBV support services in ways that protect survivors from further harm.
Ensure activities are inclusive and suitable for different ages, genders, abilities, languages, literacy levels, and cultural backgrounds, with particular attention to adolescent girls, women with disabilities, displaced people, and other underserved groups.
SRH/GBV Information and Demand Generation
Support the development and sharing of clear, accurate, and culturally appropriate information on sexual and reproductive health (SRH) and gender-based violence (GBV).
Make sure community messages explain where, when, and how women and girls can safely access available services.
Help address misinformation, stigma, misunderstandings, and harmful beliefs that may prevent people from seeking support.
Raise awareness of available services, including family planning, maternal health, post-violence care, psychosocial support, and protection services.
Use suitable ways to reach different groups, such as one-on-one discussions, community meetings, radio, women’s groups, youth groups, and other local communication channels.
Ensure all communication respects people’s right to make their own informed choices, and work with health and WPE teams to ensure that information is accurate and consistent with approved programme guidance.
GBV Survivor-Centered Engagement and Referral
Put the safety, privacy, choices, and needs of survivors first in all community engagement and referral activities.
Support safe and confidential referrals for people who choose to access GBV-related services.
Keep up-to-date information on available health, GBV case management, mental health and psychosocial support, legal, child protection, and other services.
Clearly explain available support and referral options so individuals can decide what is right for them, without pressure.
Do not pressure survivors to share personal information or use any service against their wishes. Collect and share only the information that is necessary and with appropriate consent.
Work with WPE and health teams to address challenges that may prevent survivors from getting timely and appropriate support, while following established procedures for urgent safety, protection, and safeguarding concerns.
Strengthening Community–Facility Linkages
Build strong connections between community groups and IRC-supported or government health facilities.
Help community members understand available SRH and GBV services and how to access them safely.
Work with health facility teams to identify and address barriers that prevent women and girls from using services.
Maintain regular communication between community representatives, outreach teams, and service providers.
Share community concerns and referral challenges with the supervisor and support practical solutions.
Engaging Men, Boys, Leaders, and Influencers
Engage men and boys as partners in preventing GBV and supporting better SRH outcomes.
Work with traditional, religious, youth, women’s, and other community leaders to promote support for women’s and girls’ access to services.
Encourage open discussions about harmful gender norms, stigma, discrimination, and practices that limit access to care.
Promote community values based on safety, dignity, equality, and respect for women and girls.
Identify community champions who can share accurate information and promote positive attitudes while protecting survivors’ privacy and safety.
Community Feedback and Accountability
Create safe and accessible ways for women, girls, and other community members to share their views about SRH and GBV services.
Collect and review feedback regularly to identify concerns, service gaps, and barriers to care.
Handle feedback confidentially and refer concerns through the appropriate channels when action is needed.
Work with programme teams to use community feedback to improve services and community engagement.
Make sure feedback channels are accessible to adolescents, people with disabilities, displaced people, and other groups who may face additional barriers.
Coordination and Community Capacity
Work closely with Health, WPE, Protection, MHPSS, and other IRC teams to coordinate community activities and services.
Participate in programme meetings, community assessments, outreach planning, and service mapping.
Maintain good working relationships with government health authorities, LGA structures, community leaders, local organizations, and referral partners.
Train and mentor community health workers, volunteers, peer educators, and other community actors on approved SRH and GBV approaches.
Provide refresher training and coaching on services, referrals, confidentiality, safeguarding, and survivor-centred support.
Monitoring, Learning, Reporting, and Safeguarding
Keep accurate records of community activities, outreach, referrals, training, feedback, and other programme work.
Track community reach, awareness of services, referrals, and other key programme results, and use the findings to improve activities.
Document lessons learned, community concerns, successful approaches, and challenges, and share timely reports with the supervisor.
Protect the privacy and safety of survivors by collecting and sharing only necessary information and following IRC confidentiality, safeguarding, and information-sharing procedures.
Apply principles of safety, dignity, informed choice, confidentiality, and non-discrimination, and report safeguarding or protection concerns through established IRC channels.
Experience and Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification in Public Health, Community Health, Nursing, Midwifery, Social Work, Psychology, Gender Studies, Development Studies, Sociology, or a related field.
At least 3–5 years of relevant experience in SRH, GBV, community engagement, health promotion, protection, or humanitarian and development programmes, with hands-on experience working with communities and local groups.
Practical experience working with women and girls, adolescents, displaced people, and other vulnerable groups, including leading community discussions, training, awareness activities, and outreach.
Good knowledge of SRH and GBV services, referral systems, survivor-centred support, confidentiality, informed consent, safeguarding, protection, and the principle of doing no harm.
Strong communication, coordination, facilitation, and reporting skills, with the ability to work with government health teams, community organizations, humanitarian partners, and service providers. Fluency in relevant local languages (Hausa and/or Kanuri) and willingness to travel regularly to communities and supported facilities, including hard-to-reach areas, are highly desirable.
Key Competencies
Strong understanding of SRH and GBV/VAWG and the ability to engage communities and promote access to appropriate services.
Ability to mobilize communities, create awareness, encourage positive behaviour change, and facilitate meaningful discussions.
Skilled in communicating with survivors in a respectful and sensitive manner, while supporting safe referrals and protecting confidentiality.
Ability to work effectively with women, girls, adolescents, men, boys, community leaders, and other local groups in an inclusive and gender-responsive way.
Strong skills in coordination, partnership building, community feedback, data collection, reporting, and programme learning, with a clear commitment to safeguarding and accountability.
Ability to Travel:
30–40% of time, depending on programme requirements, geographic coverage, and security/access conditions.

We are looking for a Junior Data Engineer with foundational knowledge of PostgreSQL, PL/pgSQL and PostGIS to support data management, data processing and the development of data pipelines for a health information platform.
The ideal candidate should have a basic understanding of relational databases and some practical experience working with PostgreSQL. The successful candidate will work with experienced data and software engineers to build, maintain and improve data pipelines and support the preparation of reliable datasets for reporting and visualisation.

Support the development and maintenance of data pipelines.
Work with PostgreSQL databases to store, query and manage data.
Write and maintain SQL queries for data extraction and transformation.
Develop basic PL/pgSQL functions, procedures and database logic under guidance.
Support the management and processing of geospatial data using PostGIS.
Assist with data transformation, validation and quality checks.
Prepare and transform datasets for reporting and visualisation.
Support the development of data pipelines that feed Power BI dashboards and reports.
Assist with troubleshooting data pipeline and database issues.
Document data processes, queries and pipeline configurations.
Work with software and data engineers to integrate data from different sources.
Support data quality, consistency and integrity across systems.
Participate in testing and optimisation of database queries and data processes.
Required Skills & Qualifications
Basic to intermediate knowledge of SQL.
Practical knowledge of PostgreSQL.
Basic understanding of relational database concepts and data modelling.
Some exposure to PL/pgSQL.
Basic understanding of data pipelines and ETL/ELT processes.
Familiarity with data cleaning and validation.
Basic understanding of APIs and data integration.
Familiarity with Git/version control.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Willingness to learn new data technologies and work with an existing data platform.
Desirable
Experience with PostGIS and spatial/geographic data.
Experience writing PL/pgSQL functions, procedures or triggers.
Experience building data pipelines for Power BI.
Familiarity with Power BI or other business intelligence tools.
Experience with Python for data processing or automation.
Exposure to Apache Airflow, Azure Data Factory, Apache NiFi or similar pipeline/orchestration tools.
Experience working with APIs, JSON or other structured data sources.
Experience working with health, research or other large datasets.
Experience
0–3 years of relevant experience is acceptable. Candidates with relevant academic projects, internships, personal projects or practical database/data engineering experience are encouraged to apply.
Candidates should have some hands-on experience with PostgreSQL, even if they are still developing their skills in PL/pgSQL, PostGIS and data pipeline development.
What matters most: a strong foundation in SQL/PostgreSQL, some exposure to the required technologies and the ability to learn quickly while working alongside experienced data engineers.

This role is accountable for driving long-term customer satisfaction, retention, and growth by ensuring customers maximise value from the Moniebook solution, achieve their business objectives, and remain engaged, successful partners.
Operating as a proactive customer advocate, you will own the customer relationship lifecycle, monitoring signals, conducting regular business reviews, identifying expansion opportunities, resolving issues, and driving feature adoption that deepens product stickiness.
Success is measured by customer retention (churn prevention), Net Promoter Score (NPS), expansion revenue (upsell/cross-sell), and customer satisfaction (CSAT) scores.
Key Responsibilities
Customer Relationship Ownership: Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned customer accounts. Build trusted relationships with key stakeholders (business owners, managers, staff) through proactive communication, responsiveness, and genuine commitment to their success.
Proactive Customer Engagement & Support: Regularly check in with customers to assess satisfaction, understand evolving needs, provide guidance on best practices, and address questions or concerns before they escalate. Be the first responder for customer queries and issues, delivering quick, efficient solutions.
Adoption & Value Realization: Drive ongoing adoption of Moniebook features by educating customers on underutilised capabilities, sharing relevant use cases, and providing training refreshers. Monitor usage data to identify adoption gaps and proactively intervene to increase engagement and product stickiness.
Customer Health Monitoring & Risk Management: Track customer health signals, including login frequency, transaction volume, support ticket trends, and feature adoption. Identify at-risk accounts showing signs of disengagement or dissatisfaction, and implement targeted retention strategies to prevent churn.
Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs): Conduct structured business review sessions with customers to analyse their usage data, showcase ROI and value delivered, align on business goals, surface insights and recommendations, and co-create success plans for the upcoming period.
Revenue Growth & Expansion: Identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities based on customer needs, business growth, and product usage patterns. Collaborate with Sales to introduce additional features, premium tiers, or complementary products that drive incremental revenue and customer value.
Issue Resolution & Escalation Management: Troubleshoot technical issues, configuration challenges, and operational questions. Coordinate with Product, Engineering, and Support teams to resolve complex issues while maintaining transparent communication with customers and managing their expectations throughout.
Customer Advocacy & Voice-of-Customer: Serve as the internal voice of the customer by collecting and synthesising feedback, feature requests, pain points, and competitive insights. Share these with Product and Leadership teams to inform product roadmap decisions and business strategy.
Renewal Management: Own the renewal process for assigned accounts, ensuring contracts are renewed on time with minimal friction. Proactively address renewal concerns, negotiate terms where appropriate, and secure long-term commitments that reflect the value delivered.
Continuous Learning & Product Expertise: Develop and maintain deep expertise in Moniebook's product capabilities, retail industry trends, competitive landscape, and customer success best practices. Participate in team training, product updates, and AM strategy initiatives to continuously elevate your impact.

Proven track record of managing customer relationships, driving retention, and achieving customer satisfaction targets
Strong interpersonal and communication skills with ability to build trust, influence stakeholders, and navigate difficult conversations with empathy and professionalism
Excellent problem-solving and conflict-resolution skills, able to diagnose issues, think critically, and deliver practical solutions under pressure
Technical aptitude with ability to quickly learn software products, troubleshoot issues, and effectively demonstrate product features to diverse audiences
Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple customer accounts, priorities, and projects concurrently without compromising quality
Data-driven mindset, comfortable analysing customer usage data, identifying trends, and translating insights into actionable strategies
Self-motivated, proactive, and results-oriented with strong sense of ownership and accountability for customer outcomes
Bachelor's degree in Business, Technology, Communication, or related field (or equivalent work experience)

Job Title: Legal Officer – Erroneous Transfers & Court Process Operations
Job Description:
Department: Legal & Dispute Resolution
Reports To: Head, Litigation & Dispute Resolution
About the Role
We are seeking a detail-oriented, proactive, and analytical Legal Officer to join our Litigation & Dispute Resolution team.
In this role, you will serve as the primary legal driver managing court processes, bank-to-bank dispute notices, motions on notice, and judicial orders relating to erroneous transfers, mistaken deposits, and disputed merchant transactions.
You will ensure that the internal NIP/Operations complies with judicial directives while protecting the institution from third-party liabilities, regulatory sanctions, and fund dissipation risks.
Key Responsibilities
Court Orders & Process Management: Review, log, and analyze all court orders (ex-parte, motions on notice and court orders for reversal of funds) served on the company regarding erroneous transfers or disputed wallet funds.
Lien & Hold Enforcement: Coordinate with internal NIP, Operations, and Compliance teams to ensure immediate, precise execution of post-no-debit (PND) restrictions or liens on subject-matter wallets upon receipt of legal notice.
Lifecycle Monitoring & Unfreeze Overrides: Monitor the lifecycle of pending litigation to ensure temporary holds on disputed funds are maintained in compliance with the doctrine of lis pendens until formal court resolution, preventing premature automated release of funds.
Key Requirements & Qualifications
Education: Bachelor of Laws (LL.B) and Call to the Nigerian Bar (B.L).
Experience: 2–4 years of post-call experience in corporate litigation, banking operations legal support, or a fast-paced fintech environment.
Domain Knowledge: Deep practical understanding of Nigerian civil procedure, garnishee proceedings, lis pendens, CBN guidelines on instant interbank transfers (NIP), and anti-money laundering (AML/CFT) frameworks.
Technical & Process Skills: Ability to analyze transaction logs, account histories, and bank statements alongside complex court affidavits.
Stakeholder Management: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the ability to interface effectively with internal tech/NIP teams, and executive management.
High Integrity & Sound Judgment: Strong problem-solving capabilities with a high level of discretion in handling sensitive financial data and law enforcement requests.
Why Join Us?
Direct exposure to cutting-edge payment infrastructure and high-volume financial dispute resolution.
Dynamic work environment with significant room for professional growth in tech and financial law.
Competitive compensation package and health benefits.

Job Purpose / Mission
The Line Operator / Warehouse Driver role is to ensure the safe, timely and cost-effective movement of products, inventory and operational materials between the warehouse, Service Centres and other approved locations, while maintaining product custody, accurate delivery documentation, vehicle compliance and required safety standards.
Key Responsibilities
Transportation and Delivery:
Safely transport products, inventory and operational materials to approved Service Centres, warehouses and other business locations.
Execute scheduled primary, secondary and inter-location stock movements.
Follow approved routes and delivery schedules and communicate delays or exceptions promptly.
Support urgent operational movements where duly approved.
Loading, Offloading and Product Handling:
Support the loading and offloading of products and materials.
Verify quantities and product condition before departure and at the point of delivery.
Ensure products are properly arranged and secured to minimize transit damage.
Immediately report damaged, missing, excess or wrongly dispatched products.
Inventory Custody and Documentation:
Maintain traceability of items collected from Service Centres or other locations.
Verify waybills, stock transfer documents and other dispatch documentation before departure.
Obtain appropriate proof of delivery (POD) and ensure completed documents are returned promptly.
Ensure that no unauthorized products, materials or passengers are carried in company vehicles.
Reverse Logistics:
Support the collection and return of defective products, swap units, refurbishment stock, empty packaging and other approved returns.
Ensure returned products are properly documented, secured and handed over to the designated receiving team.
Maintain traceability of items collected from Service Centres or other locations.

Job Description:
Are you a great teacher? Bring your subject to life on camera and help thousands of Nigerian students learn with ease.
ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY
EES Tech Limited is building a curriculum-aligned video learning platform for Nigerian secondary school students (JSS1 to SS3), fully mapped to the NERDC
curriculum and the BECE, WAEC and NECO examination requirements.
We are looking for experienced subject teachers to develop lesson content and deliver it on camera at our Lagos studio. This is not a full-time job and it does not require you to leave your current role. It is a flexible, delivery-based engagement: you are contracted to produce a defined set of lessons for your subject, you develop the content, you film it at our studio on scheduled dates, and you are paid on successful delivery, based on an agreed budget per assignment.
HOW IT WORKS
You keep your current job.
You work from an agreed lesson list.
You film at our studio on scheduled dates.
You get paid when your content is delivered and approved. Simple.
WHAT YOU WILL DO
Develop lesson scripts and outlines for your assigned subject and class levels, using the EES lesson framework and templates provided.
Work with our Head of Department to get your scripts reviewed and approved before filming.
Attend scheduled filming sessions at our Lagos studio and deliver your lessons on camera — our production team handles all filming, sound and editing.
Make reasonable revisions where our quality review team requests corrections or re-takes.
Deliver your full assigned lesson set within the agreed schedule.
SUBJECTS WE ARE RECRUITING FOR
Arts
Humanities and Commercial Government
History and Civic Education
WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR
A degree in your subject area or in education (B.Ed, B.Sc, B.A or higher).
Minimum 3 years of secondary school teaching experience with direct exposure to BECE, WAEC or NECO examination preparation.
Strong command of the NERDC curriculum and the examination syllabus for your subject.
Clear spoken English and the ability to explain difficult concepts simply.
Confidence presenting, on camera or in front of a class, and openness to coaching on camera delivery.
Reliability: you deliver what you commit to, on schedule.
A plus, but not required: prior experience creating educational videos or online tutoring content, or experience as a WAEC/NECO examiner or marker.
ENGAGEMENT AND PAYMENT
Engagement type: Independent contractor, delivery-based (not employment).
Commitment: Flexible. Content development on your own time; filming at scheduled studio sessions in Lagos.
Payment: Fixed fee per assigned lesson set, agreed upfront and paid on successful delivery and approval.
Location: Content development — anywhere. Filming — our studio in Lagos.
Duration: Per assignment, with the opportunity for repeat assignments as our Library grows.
Requirements:
Signed contributor agreement, NDA and content rights assignment before commencement.
Note on content ownership: all lesson content produced under this engagement is the exclusive property of EES Tech Limited. Tutors appear on camera as presenters of EES content and may not reproduce, distribute or publish the content independently. Full terms are set out in the contributor agreement.
Shortlisted candidates will be invited for discussion of assignment scope and fees.

Job Description:
Job Purpose
The Safety Officer will support the Head of HSE in promoting, enforcing, and maintaining a proactive zero-harm safety culture across site operations. The role is strictly focused on Occupational Health and Safety (OHS), including field risk assessments, haulage and heavy equipment traffic safety, incident prevention, worker health monitoring, and regulatory safety compliance. Note: Environmental compliance and management functions are outside the scope of this role.
Scope of Work & Key Responsibilities
Daily Field Supervision & Inspections:
Conduct regular daily safety walk-throughs across mining pits, processing plants, haul roads, workshops, and dumps. Identify and address unsafe acts and conditions immediately.
Hazard Identification & Risk Assessment (HIRA):
Assist operational teams in performing Job Safety Analyses (JSA) and risk assessments for routine and non-routine high-risk tasks (e.g., machinery maintenance, working at heights, heavy haulage).
Toolbox Talks & Safety Inductions:
Prepare and deliver daily/weekly pre-shift safety toolbox talks and conduct OHS orientation/inductions for new employees, contractors, and site visitors.
Traffic & Haulage Safety Enforcement:
Enforce the Traffic Management Plan (TMP), including blind spot awareness, 50m heavy equipment exclusion zones, speed limits, and proper spotter positioning.
Incident Reporting & Initial Investigation:
Respond promptly to workplace accidents, near-misses, and first-aid cases. Conduct initial root-cause investigations, log reports, and track corrective action closures under the direction of the Head of HSE.
Occupational Health & Hygiene Monitoring:
Ensure strict adherence to occupational health protocols, including heat stress management, fatigue monitoring, noise exposure controls, and proper usage of personal protective equipment (PPE).
Lockout / Tagout (LOTO) & Safe Work Permits:
Inspect and verify LOTO compliance during mechanical/electrical maintenance and audit the issuance of high-risk work permits.
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Proactive Field Inspections:
Conduct and document daily OHS workplace inspections across assigned operational sectors.
Hazard Resolution:
Track identified unsafe acts/conditions and ensure timely closure of corrective actions.
Safety Training & Engagement:
Lead pre-shift toolbox talks and complete OHS inductions for all assigned
Incident Reporting & Closure:
Report near-misses/incidents immediately and complete initial investigation reports within 24 hours.
Safe Work & LOTO Audits:
Perform weekly compliance audits on Lockout/Tagout procedures and high-risk work permits.
Qualifications & Experience Requirements
Education & Professional Certification:
B.Sc/HND/OND in Occupational Health & Safety, Engineering, Earth Sciences, or related field. Professional OHS certification (e.g., NEBOSH IGC, IOSH, or ISPON) is mandatory.
Work Experience:
Minimum of 3–5 years of direct experience as a Safety Officer in open-pit mining, heavy civil construction, quarrying, or heavy industrial operations.
Technical Knowledge:
Strong knowledge of mine safety regulations, hazard identification, heavy machinery/haulage safety, LOTO protocols, and emergency response procedures.
Core Skills:
Excellent hazard reporting, communication, leadership, hazard communication skills, and proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).

Job Description:
About the role:
The
Senior Product Designer (UX Designer),
based in Nairobi or Lagos. You will report to the Head of Product, Enterprise Products.
You will own the experience of the products our customers, field agents and our staff teams use every day. That covers the apps our Energy Officers use to sell, onboard and service customers. It also covers the products our customers use to buy, pay for and manage their energy. It covers the tools our staff uses to manage the inventory, sales, collections, incentives, etc every day. And it covers the design system that holds all of it.
The people you design for are not like you. Many are first-time smartphone users. They work outdoors, on low-end Android devices, on patchy networks, often in their second or third language. A design succeeds here when an agent can close a sale in a village at the end of a long day. It is not judged by how the screen looks in a portfolio.
We also want an AI-first approach to design. You reach for AI to explore concepts, generate variants and pressure-test copy. You prototype before writing a specification. You ask “can AI do this better” first, not as an afterthought.
This role covers design end to end. Research, flows, interaction design, visual design, prototyping and handoff. We expect all of it done the AI-first way: faster, sharper, and built to scale.
What you would be expected to do:
Research with the people who actually use our products
Spend time in the field with Energy Officers, customers and operations teams. Watch them work. Do not rely on second-hand reports.
Run usability tests, contextual interviews and concept tests in market.
Turn what you learn into choice the team acts on, not decks that get filed away.
Flows and interaction design
Design the end-to-end journeys behind sales, onboarding, collections, servicing and assist.
Map the offline steps as well as the on-screen ones. Most of our journeys start on paper or in conversation.
Simplify flows that have grown complicated over years of feature additions.
Visual design and craft
Take work from rough concept to production-ready screens.
Hold a high bar on typography, spacing, ranking and legibility in bright sunlight on small screens.
Make the interface teachable. A new agent should be productive on day one.
Design for real constraints
Design for low-end Android devices, small screens and limited storage.
Design for intermittent flow. Offline states, sync and failure recovery are part of the design, not an engineering afterthought.
Design for low digital literacy and for multiple languages. Assume text will be longer once translated.
The design system
Own our collective component library and design standards.
Keep it in step with what engineering actually ships. A system nobody uses is worse than none.
Document patterns so other designers and engineers can apply them without asking you.
Prototype before spec
Build clickable prototypes to answer open questions early.
Use AI tools to generate variants, draft copy and explore directions quickly.
Put prototypes in front of real users and change your mind when they tell you to.
Handoff and working with engineering
Produce handoff-ready files, specs and states that engineers can build from without guesswork.
Cover the unglamorous cases: empty states, errors, loading, long names, missing data, poor network.
Review builds before release and hold the bar on implementation quality.
Measure whether the design worked
Define what success looks like before the design ships: task completion, time on task, error and drop-off rates.
Work with product and data teams to read adoption and funnel data after release.
Go back and fix what the data says is not working.
Team Work
Work closely with product managers, engineers and market operations teams through the full product lifecycle.
Bring evidence to design debates. Be willing to be overruled, and be willing to argue your case.
Keep stakeholders informed at every stage.
Travel
Travel as required to Sun King markets, including Kenya, Uganda, Nigeria, Tanzania and Myanmar, with regular field visits to agents and customers.
You might be a strong candidate if you have/are:
Background and approach
A portfolio of shipped product work (mandatory). We want two or three cases in depth: the problem, what you tried, what you did, and what happened after launch.
5–7 years designing digital products, with meaningful time on mobile.
Experience designing for users who are not like you, ideally in emerging markets, field operations, fintech or last-mile distribution.
Able to structure and evaluate ambiguous problems.
Clear communication in writing. You will explain design choice to people who are not designers.
A proactive attitude and willingness to get hands-on. We are small and you will do your own research, design and testing.
A formal design degree is welcome but not required. The portfolio matters more.
Language
Professional working proficiency in English (mandatory). You will work with colleagues and stakeholders across our markets in Africa and Asia.
A local market language such as Swahili, French, Hausa, Yoruba or Luganda is a strong plus for field research.
Essential skills
Expert in Figma, including components, variables, auto layout and prototyping.
Hands-on experience building or maintaining a design system.
Practical research skills: usability testing, contextual inquiry and field interviews, run by you rather than outsourced.
Android design conventions and Material Design, applied with judgement rather than by default.
Accessibility and legibility fundamentals: contrast, touch targets, text scaling, and patterns that work for low-literacy users.
Enough data literacy to read a funnel, an adoption chart or an A/B test result and act on it.
Comfortable using AI tools in your design workflow, for concepts, copy, research synthesis and prototypes.
Good to have
Experience designing offline-first or intermittently integrated applications.
Front-end familiarity (HTML, CSS, or React) — enough to talk to engineers about what is expensive to build.
Motion design or illustration.
Service design experience covering journeys that cross online and offline steps.
Exposure to pay-as-you-go, asset finance, microfinance or emerging-market lending.
Hands-on experience with SQL.

Job Description:
Role Summary
The Team Lead, Special Risks is responsible for the effective management, underwriting and administration of the Company's Special Risks portfolio. The role provides technical leadership in assessing complex and high-value risks, developing appropriate underwriting terms, ensuring adequate risk pricing and facilitating profitable portfolio growth in line with the Company's underwriting strategy, risk appetite and regulatory requirements.
The role will also provide guidance to underwriting team members, strengthen broker and client relationships, support business development initiatives and ensure that all Special Risks business is managed in accordance with approved policies, procedures and delegated underwriting authorities.
Key Responsibilities
Assess, analyse and underwrite complex and high-value risks within approved underwriting authority.
Review risk submissions, proposal forms, surveys, loss histories, financial information and other relevant documentation.
Determine the acceptability of risks based on the Company's underwriting guidelines and risk appetite.
Develop appropriate policy terms, conditions, warranties, exclusions, deductibles and other risk mitigation measures.
Ensure that risks are appropriately classified, rated and priced to achieve adequate technical profitability.
Refer risks exceeding delegated authority to the appropriate approving authority.
Monitor the performance of the Special Risks portfolio against agreed business and profitability targets.
Analyse portfolio trends, loss ratios, premium growth, retention and other key underwriting indicators.

Review underperforming accounts and recommend corrective actions.
Assess the adequacy of risk management and loss prevention measures implemented by insureds.
Work closely with Risk Management, Claims and Reinsurance teams on complex risks.
Liaise with the Reinsurance team on facultative and treaty requirements for Special Risks.
Ensure risks requiring facultative reinsurance are referred promptly and appropriately.
Review facultative reinsurance terms and ensure that the Company's exposure is adequately protected.
Ensure compliance with treaty capacity, retention limits and reinsurance guidelines.
Support the development of new Special Risks business through brokers, agents, corporate clients and strategic partners.
Maintain strong professional relationships with key brokers, intermediaries and clients.
Participate in client and broker meetings, presentations and negotiations on complex risks.

Professional qualification in Insurance, preferably
Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria (CIIN)
.

5 years' relevant experience
in general insurance, preferably with substantial experience in underwriting.
Minimum of

.
Demonstrable experience managing high-value and complex insurance risks.

Experience working with brokers, reinsurers and major corporate clients is highly desirable.

JOB SUMMARY
The Principal Technical Safety Engineer will provide senior technical leadership and specialist expertise in Technical Safety and Process Safety Engineering across engineering design projects within the Oil & Gas industry. The role is responsible for ensuring that technical safety requirements are effectively incorporated into the design of facilities and systems throughout the project lifecycle, from concept selection and FEED through detailed engineering, construction support, commissioning and handover.
MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES
Technical Safety Leadership
Provide technical leadership and specialist advice on Technical Safety and Process Safety Engineering activities.
Act as the senior technical focal point for technical safety matters within assigned projects.
Establish technical safety philosophies, design criteria, specifications and engineering requirements.
Ensure that technical safety considerations are incorporated into the design from the early project stages.
Provide technical direction to Technical Safety Engineers and other engineering disciplines.
Review and approve technical safety deliverables within delegated authority.
Provide technical support to project management and engineering leadership on safety-critical design issues.
Safety Studies & Risk Assessment
Lead, facilitate or provide technical oversight for major process safety and risk assessment studies, including:
HAZID – Hazard Identification Studies
HAZOP – Hazard and Operability Studies
SIL Assessment / SIL Classification
LOPA – Layer of Protection Analysis
QRA – Quantitative Risk Assessment
Bow-Tie Analysis
Fire and Explosion Risk Assessment
Escape, Evacuation and Rescue Analysis
Dropped Object Studies
Fire and Gas Mapping
Toxic and Flammable Gas Dispersion Studies
Blast and Explosion Analysis
Emergency Response and Emergency Systems Analysis
ALARP demonstrations and risk reduction assessments
Safety Critical Element identification and performance standard development.
Ensure that recommendations arising from safety studies are properly documented, assigned, tracked and incorporated into the design.
Design Safety & Engineering Assurance
Review engineering designs to identify hazards and ensure appropriate risk reduction measures are incorporated.
Ensure compliance with the approved Design Safety Philosophy and project specifications.
Review P&IDs, plot plans, equipment layouts, cause-and-effect diagrams, shutdown philosophies and other engineering documents from a technical safety perspective.
Participate in multidisciplinary design reviews and technical audits.
Review safety-related design calculations, reports, specifications and studies.
Ensure appropriate separation distances, hazardous area classifications, escape routes and access requirements are incorporated into facility designs.
Provide technical input into equipment and system specifications for safety-critical systems.
Fire Protection & Fire and Gas Systems
Provide technical oversight of fire protection and fire and gas engineering activities.
Review fire and gas detector layouts and coverage assessments.
Review firewater demand calculations and fire protection philosophies.
Provide input into fire protection systems, deluge systems, passive fire protection and emergency shutdown systems.
Ensure appropriate fire and gas detection, alarm and mitigation strategies are incorporated into facility designs.
Review fire and explosion protection requirements for process and utility facilities.
5. Functional Safety & Safety Instrumented Systems
Provide technical leadership in the application of functional safety principles.
Review Safety Instrumented System (SIS) requirements and safety functions.
Participate in SIL classification, SIL verification and safety requirements specification activities.
Ensure compliance with applicable functional safety standards.
Review Safety Instrumented Functions (SIFs), voting architectures, proof-test requirements and associated documentation.
Provide technical guidance on Emergency Shutdown (ESD), Fire & Gas (F&G) and other safety-critical control systems.
Hazardous Area Classification
Review and provide technical guidance on hazardous area classification studies.
Ensure appropriate classification of hazardous zones in accordance with applicable standards.
Review hazardous area drawings and ensure appropriate equipment selection and installation requirements.
Coordinate hazardous area classification requirements with Electrical, Instrumentation, Process and Mechanical disciplines.
Technical Safety Deliverables
Provide technical leadership and review of deliverables including, but not limited to:
Technical Safety Philosophy
Design Safety Cases
HAZID/HAZOP reports
Risk Assessment Reports
QRA reports
Fire Protection Philosophy
Fire and Gas Philosophy
ESD Philosophy
Hazardous Area Classification
Escape, Evacuation and Rescue Studies
Safety Critical Element Registers
Performance Standards
Safety Requirement Specifications
SIL Assessment and Verification Reports
Consequence Modelling Reports
Emergency Response Studies
Technical Safety Datasheets and Specifications
Technical Safety layouts and drawings.
Regulatory & Standards Compliance
Ensure engineering designs comply with applicable Nigerian regulations and regulatory requirements.
Ensure compliance with relevant international codes and standards, including applicable requirements of:
IEC
ISO
API
NFPA
ASME
NORSOK
IMO, where applicable
Client/company specifications and standards.
Monitor changes in applicable legislation, standards and industry practices and advise the project team accordingly.
ALARP & Risk Management
Ensure project risks are systematically identified, assessed and reduced to **As Low As Reasonably Practicable (ALARP)**.
Provide technical justification for risk acceptance and risk reduction decisions.
Identify safety-critical risks and recommend appropriate safeguards and mitigation measures.
Maintain and support project risk registers relating to process and technical safety.
Ensure residual risks are properly documented and communicated.
Interface & Multidisciplinary Coordination
Coordinate technical safety activities with Process, Mechanical, Electrical, Instrumentation & Control, Civil/Structural, Piping and other engineering disciplines.
Ensure technical safety requirements are reflected consistently across multidisciplinary engineering deliverables.
Participate in design reviews, model reviews, constructability reviews and project technical meetings.
Interface effectively with Clients, consultants, vendors, contractors and regulatory authorities.
Project & Client Support
Provide technical safety support throughout the project lifecycle.
Participate in Client meetings, technical clarification sessions and design reviews.
Prepare and present technical safety reports and recommendations to Clients and senior management.
Support tendering and proposal activities by developing technical safety scopes, man-hour estimates and deliverable lists.
Provide technical input into project schedules and resource requirements.
Construction, Commissioning & Operational Support
Provide technical safety support during construction, commissioning and start-up activities.
Review Management of Change (MOC) proposals from a technical safety perspective.
Participate in pre-start-up safety reviews (PSSR).
Support commissioning and start-up teams in resolving safety-related technical issues.
Provide technical input into operating and maintenance philosophies where required.
Support incident investigations and safety-related root cause analysis where required.
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, AND EXPERIENCE
Bachelor's Degree in Chemical, Process, Mechanical, Petroleum Engineering or another relevant engineering discipline.
Master's Degree in Process Safety, Engineering Management or a related discipline will be an advantage.
Professional engineering registration/membership with a recognized professional body is preferred.
Relevant certification in Process Safety or Functional Safety will be an advantage.
Minimum 15 years of relevant experience in Technical Safety / Process Safety Engineering within the Oil & Gas industry.
Demonstrable experience working within an Engineering Design / EPC / EPCM organization.
Significant experience in FEED and detailed engineering projects.
Proven experience leading or providing technical oversight for HAZID, HAZOP, SIL, LOPA, QRA and other process safety studies.
Strong experience in technical safety design for upstream, midstream, downstream, LNG, gas processing, refinery, petrochemical or related Oil & Gas facilities.
Experience with both greenfield and brownfield projects will be an advantage.
Experience interfacing with international Clients, engineering consultants and EPC contractors is desirable.
Proven experience leading multidisciplinary engineering teams and mentoring junior engineers.

Company Details:
Electric Power development in Nigeria started toward the end of 19th century when the first generating plant of 30KW was installed in the city of Lagos in 1898. From this date onwards and until 1950, the pattern of electricity development was inform of individual electricity under-taking set up in v...read morearious towns somewhere by Native or Municipal authorities. 
In 1946, the Nigerian Government Electricity undertaking was established within the then Public Works Development (PWD) to take over the responsibilities for electricity in Lagos State.
In 1950 the Government passed the Electricity Corporation of Nigeria Ordinance No.1 of 1950 to integrate power development and make it effective. This ordinance brought all the electricity undertakings and the electricity sections of PWD under control. The Electricity Corporation of Nigeria (ECN) then became the statutory body responsible for Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Sales of Electricity to all consumers in Nigeria.
In 1962, the Niger Dams Authority was established by an Act of the Parliament. The Authority was responsible for the construction and maintenance of Dams and other works on the river Niger and elsewhere, generating electricity by means of water, improving navigation and promoting fisheries and irrigation.
The Electricity Corporation of Nigeria (ECN) and the Niger Dams Authority (NDA) were merged to become National Electric Power Authority (NEPA) by decree No.24 of 1972. The Authority was to develop and maintain an efficient, co-ordinate an economic system of electricity supply for all parts of the Federation. The Authority generates electricity through two major sources: Hydro and Thermal. The Hydro Power stations are Kainji Hydro Power station with capacity of 760MW, Jebba Hydro Power station with 578.4MW capacity, Shiroro Hydro Power Station 600MW. The Thermal Power stations are: Afam Thermal Power station with 696MW, Lagos thermal power station, Delta IV thermal Power station with 600MW and Sapele Thermal Power station 1020MW.
However, the need to reform the Electricity industry necessitated the transformation of NEPA into Power Holding Company of Nigeria (PHCN) in 2004. 
The Electricity Reform Act of 2005, unbundled PHCN into 11 Distribution companies, 1 Transmission Company and 6 Generation companies. This Reform Act gave birth to Enugu Electricity Distribution Company (EEDC).

Achieving Health Nigeria Initiative (AHNi) is a non-profit organization that promotes socio-economic development by supporting global health and economic initiatives in Nigeria. It was established as indigenous organizational, registered in 2009 with its headquarter in Abuja, and presence in the four geopolitical regions of Nigeria. It aims to provide technical assistance to the government and people of Nigeria in the implementation of public health and development programs.
Through the Global Fund N-THRIP project, AHNi focuses on scaling up HIV prevention, identification, and treatment efforts among general and key populations in Anambra State, emphasizing facility-based and community-initiated approaches to achieve epidemic control. Additionally, the project prioritizes improving ART coverage for pregnant women and advancing programs for key populations (KP) and adolescent girls and young women (AGYW).
Hence, the consultant will support the implementation of the grant in all supported facilities in the LGA of the state as the
Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist.
Key roles:
The services of the consultant will include but not limited to the following:
S/He will support the implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and reporting of HIV program activities at assigned facilities, ensuring alignment with national guidelines and project objectives at all supported facilities in the LGA.
Ensure accurate data collection, collation, and reporting across platforms (NMRS, DHIS, NDR) with 100% reporting compliance at all supported facilities in the State.
Will be engaged to support planning, review, and implementation of core M&E activities with the view of ensuring highest data quality for evidence-based decision making and program improvement across GF N-THRIP supported facilities.
H/She will conduct routine data verification, validation, and quality assurance exercises at various service points in supported facilities in the State.
Provide support to sites in the state, including interacting with site Program Managers, M&E focal points, M&E officers of SACA/SASCP, other Implementing Agencies and local research groups on needs and ensuring that these parties understand and can support these requirements.
Facilitate daily data collation and reporting, ensuring concurrence between reporting platforms in all supported facilities in the LGA.
Collaborate with the Strategic Information (SI) unit for effective data analysis and decision-making in the LGA on the project.
Prepare program reports, highlight success stories, and address challenges to improve program outcomes in the State.
Liaise with IT officers for preventive maintenance of M&E computing resources and promptly address system errors.
S/He will support coordination and oversight functions on strengthening health information systems through strategic information processes and innovations at the state level and across AHNi supported facilities and in line with IHVN and Global Fund guidelines.
Also, s/he will work with program and technical staff to support the correct implementation and use of monitoring and evaluation tools, and adherence to complete, correct and timely reporting, ensuring that the quality of program/project activities adheres to SOPs by supporting the development and implementation of appropriate mechanisms to ensure quality.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Requirements
:
B. Tech, B.SC, or HND in statistics, Mathematics, pharmacy, microbiology, with 1 to 3 years’ experience in monitoring and evaluation systems.
Familiarity with GF reporting system is an advantage.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills
Ability to function effectively in multi-disciplinary teams to produce excellent results under pressure.
Excellent ability to communicate and maintain productive relations with the team; resourcefulness, flexibility, and ability to work in a fast changing and challenging environment.
Ability to use key computing applications e g MS Office Suite etc and knowledge of different databases (DHIS or NMRS) is a plus.
Experience in project-level or state/national-level monitoring and evaluation system implementation for Global Health Initiatives.

Job Description:
To build and lead the partnership function that powers CDL's two-track ecosystem strategy. The role exists to convert partnership activity into a disciplined commercial engine that materially contributes to CDL's ambition of becoming Africa's leading embedded finance provider. The Lead, Partnership and Ecosystem will own the partnership thesis, pipeline and outcomes across CDL's Built and Integrated ecosystems, and will build the team and operating model that sustains it at scale.
Job Details
Partnership Strategy & Thesis:
Develop the CDL Partnership Strategy. This includes segmenting the universe across Built and Integrated tracks, defining partner archetypes, and prioritizing targets by commercial fit, integration cost and strategic value.
Define deal economics frameworks for each archetype, including revenue share, take-rate floors, exclusivity, integration cost recovery and partner-of-record economics.
Maintain a rolling 12-month partnership pipeline with explicit conversion targets, reviewed monthly with the CRCMO and quarterly with the MD/CEO and ExCo.
Built Ecosystem Partnerships:
Lead partnerships that directly enrich CDL's proprietary consumer and SME platforms. Target categories include lifestyle and commerce merchants, ride-hailing and travel, telco and content, embedded insurance, investments and asset managers, payment scheme partners, and select fintech adjacencies.
Drive partnership-led customer acquisition campaigns and bundled propositions in coordination with marketing and product.
On the platform, own merchant and content partnership economics.
Integrated Ecosystem Partnerships:
Lead embedded credit, checkout and BNPL partnerships across e-commerce platforms, marketplaces, payroll providers, telcos, and other priority categories.
Originate and structure platform-of-record partnerships, API consumer relationships, and aggregator deals
Partner closely with Product, Engineering and the technology leadership on integration design and time-to-live.
Build the commercial framework for credit-as-a-service and underwriting-as-a-service offerings.
International Partnership Foundation:
Build and execute the partnership track of CDL's planned international expansion across other priority African markets.
Identify and qualify acquisition, greenfield and licensing partners aligned to CDL's expansion approach.
Establish partnership rails in each priority market, including local distribution partners, embedded finance hosts, and regulatory-aligned platforms.
Function Building & Team Leadership:
Design the partnership target operating model, covering coverage structure, deal stages, governance forums, account management cadence, and partner success motion.
Recruit and lead the team, with a clear progression and reward framework.
Stand up partnership tooling, including pipeline CRM, deal-room, partner scorecards, integration tracker, and contract repository, in coordination with technology and internal systems.
Own the Partnership Operating Calendar, including monthly reviews, quarterly council, and an annual partner summit.
Cross-functional Leadership & Governance:
Partner deeply with: CRCMO (commercial alignment), CPO (product propositions), Chief Digital & Technology Officer (integration and technology), CRO (credit and risk acceptance criteria for embedded credit), CFO (deal economics, capital allocation), Chief Legal Counsel (contract and regulatory), Head of Operations and Customer Experience (operational delivery).
Establish and chair the Partnerships Investment Committee, a forum that signs off material partnership commitments above defined thresholds.
Maintain partnership compliance with CBN and host-country regulatory frameworks, working with Legal and Risk.
Requirements
Bachelor's degree, with a postgraduate qualification in business, finance or technology preferred (MBA from a credible institution is a plus, not a requirement).
Demonstrable record of personally originating, structuring and closing partnerships of material commercial size, quantifiable in deal value, revenue contribution, GMV processed, or customers acquired.
Prior experience leading or building a partnership function from a low base, including team design, deal governance, and operating tooling.
Strong API-led commercial fluency; comfort in technical conversations with CTO and product leadership of partner organizations.
Active Pan-African network and credible deal experience beyond Nigeria.
Track record of working effectively in cross-functional environments alongside Product, Engineering, Risk, Legal and Finance.
12–15+ years of progressive experience, including 7+ years in partnerships, business development or commercial roles in financial services, payments, embedded finance, fintech infrastructure or platform technology
COMPETENCIES REQUIREMENTS:
Technical:
Partnership strategy and segmentation.
Deal structuring, covering revenue share, take-rate, exclusivity, integration economics, and partner-of-record models.
Embedded finance and platform commercial constructs.
Pipeline management and partnership CRM discipline.
Contract negotiation and term-sheet construction.
Partnership P&L management and unit-economics modelling.
Partnership compliance with CBN and equivalent regulatory frameworks
Behavioural:
Builder, not maintainer.
Commercially disciplined: closes deals that work, walks away from those that do not.
Cross-functionally credible. Earns the respect of product, engineering, risk and legal.
Direct and low-ego; comfortable with peer-level frankness.
Customer-back thinker. Every partnership must improve outcomes for CDL's customers.
Long-term builder of African finance, not a short-stay logo collector.

The ideal candidate must possess in-depth knowledge of the assigned sectors, understand industry-specific value chains and business dynamics, and demonstrate strong relationship management and credit analysis capabilities.
The successful candidate will be responsible for:
Relationship Management
Develop and manage profitable relationships with corporate clients across various sectors.
Identify new business opportunities and actively grow the bank's corporate customer base.
Maintain regular engagement with existing and prospective clients to understand their banking needs.
Deliver tailored banking solutions to clients while ensuring superior customer experience.
Business Development
Drive the acquisition of quality corporate accounts and revenue-generating opportunities.
Market the bank's products and services to existing and potential customers.
Achieve assigned financial and business development targets.
Increase wallet share and penetration within assigned portfolios.
Credit Analysis and CAM Preparation
Conduct detailed financial and credit analysis on corporate customers.
Prepare comprehensive and high-quality Credit Approval Memorandum (CAM) for credit facilities and renewals.
Assess credit risks and recommend appropriate mitigating measures.
Present credit proposals to internal approval committees where required.
Monitor approved credit facilities and ensure compliance with credit terms and conditions.
Sector Coverage and Advisory

Oil & Gas
Telecommunications
Power & Infrastructure
Agriculture & Non-Oil Exports
Manufacturing
Large Corporates
Conglomerates
Understand sector trends, market developments, key risks, and opportunities.
Provide industry insights and advisory support to clients and internal stakeholders.

Monitor portfolio performance and ensure asset quality.
Minimize non-performing loans through proactive portfolio monitoring.
Ensure timely renewal of facilities and compliance with regulatory and internal requirements.
Prepare portfolio reviews and management reports as required.
Compliance and Risk Management

Perform Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) requirements in line with regulatory guidelines.
Identify and escalate emerging risks within customer portfolios.

Company Details: Created by the Howdy Corporation in St. Louis, MO, 7UP was an optimistic venture from the very start. After great success with the Howdy Orange drink, company founder C.L. Grigg decided to try his luck with lemons and limes. C.L. Grigg spent more than two years testing over 11 different formulas,...read moreall in search of a drink that was refreshing enough to prove irresistible to the people of Missouri and the world at large. In 1929, C.L. Grigg’s bubbliest drink was born. The public quickly developed a taste for Grigg’s caramel colored lemon-lime soda. Bib-Label Lithiated Lemon-Lime Soda sold, and sold well. As the drink grew more and more popular, the original name was traded in for something short and sweet. Bib-Label Lithiated Lemon-Lime Soda became known as 7UP. Early advertising featured a winged 7UP logo with copy that read "a glorified drink in bottles only. Seven natural flavors blended into a savory, flavory drink with a real wallop." The drink was so successful by 1936 that Grigg changed the name of The Howdy Corporation to The Seven-Up Company. By the late 1940s, 7UP had become the third best-selling soft drink in the world. In the decades to follow, 7UP developed iconic branding, setting it apart from industry front-runners. In 1967, 7UP brought the phrase UNCOLA into the national vernacular. The UNCOLA campaign set 7UP apart from its competition and became part of a counter cultural that symbolized being true to yourself and challenging the status quo. Always at the frontier of taste and pop culture, 7UP was also among the first sodas to introduce sugar-free and caffeine free options. Through the years, advertising for 7UP featured everything from a cartoon mascot named Spot, to the "It’s an Up thing" and "Make 7UP yours" taglines.

Overview
We are building an AI-Native Engineering team and looking for a DevOps Engineer who will be a key player in our Product Development Outsourcing business.
Our engineers love to learn and have a passion for technology.
They’re known for their expertise in solving the most complex tech challenges while having fun and being part of a dynamic and collaborative team.

Work closely with developers and the architect to evaluate existing problems and offer process improvement solutions.
Identify bottlenecks in the coding development and implementation process.

Actively participate in the deployment of application devices in appropriate environments through compatible technologies and infrastructures.
Coordinate with developers and technical members of the organization to understand their main weaknesses in the coding and development process.
Collaborate with the team to provide coherent and holistic solutions.
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree or equivalent degree in computer science or another related field.
3-4 years of coding and scripting experience in implementing large-scale cloud architectures using modern cloud-based container platforms is highly desirable.
Knowledge of the implementation of automatic infrastructure provisioning solutions is a big advantage (i.e. Puppet, Chef, Ansible).
Knowledge of Linux OS, SQL, PL SQL, Scripting, and Container is required.
Knowledge of networks, cloud infrastructure, and management tools for computing components, storage, networking, caching, etc. is a plus.
Deep understanding of the Agile methodology.
Experience as a DevOps or SRE Engineer in an agile multifunctional team is preferred.
Ability to collaborate and create efficient and innovative solutions.
Strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills.
Passion for emerging technologies and their impact.
Open to new ideas and eager to learn and gain new skills.
A self-starter who thrives in a culture built around transparency and trust.
Professional fluency in English is vital,both written and spoken.
Must have completed the compulsory 1-year NYSC or have an exemption certificate.
A valid and up to date National Identity Card/NIMC slip is required upon commencement of this role.

Job Description:
Main Function
The HR Manager is responsible for providing administrative and operational support to the Human Resources department, ensuring that recruitment, employee records, onboarding, and day-to-day HR activities are effectively coordinated.
The role requires a highly organized, discreet, proactive, and dependable individual who can manage confidential employee information, support recruitment and onboarding processes, maintain accurate HR records, and assist in the smooth running of HR operations.
The ideal candidate must be capable of working independently, communicating professionally with staff and candidates, handling sensitive information with discretion, and serving as an effective link between the HR department and employees, applicants, and other stakeholders.
Role Responsibilities
Recruitment and Onboarding Support
Assist in posting job vacancies, sourcing candidates, and scheduling interviews.
Coordinate communication with applicants throughout the recruitment process.
Support the preparation of offer letters, employment contracts, and onboarding documentation.
Assist new employees with onboarding formalities and orientation arrangements.
Employee Records and HR Documentation
Maintain accurate and up-to-date employee files, both electronic and physical.
Prepare, organize, and update HR documents, letters, and correspondence.
Ensure confidentiality and proper storage of sensitive employee information.
Retrieve records and documents promptly when required by management.
HR Communication and Correspondence
Handle HR-related emails, calls, and correspondence professionally and promptly.
Draft, proofread, and format HR letters, memos, and internal communications.
Serve as a point of contact between employees and the HR department for routine enquiries.
Maintain professionalism and discretion when handling sensitive HR communications.
Attendance, Leave, and Payroll Support
Track staff attendance, leave requests, and absences.
Assist in maintaining leave schedules and updating records accordingly.
Support the HR/Payroll team with data required for payroll processing.
Follow up on outstanding attendance or leave documentation.
Training and Development Coordination
Assist in scheduling and coordinating staff training sessions and workshops.
Prepare training materials, attendance registers, and related documentation.
Track employee participation and maintain training records.
Employee Relations Support
Support the HR team in addressing routine employee queries and concerns.
Assist in coordinating employee engagement activities and events.
Escalate sensitive employee relations matters to appropriate HR personnel.
Policy and Compliance Support
Assist in ensuring staff compliance with company policies and procedures.
Support the update and distribution of HR policies and staff handbooks.
Help maintain records required for statutory and regulatory compliance.
HR Reporting and Data Management
Prepare HR reports, trackers, and summaries as required.
Maintain accurate HR data and assist with periodic audits of records.
Provide regular updates on HR matters requiring management\'s attention.
Office and Administrative Support
Coordinate with other departments to ensure HR requests and needs are attended to.
Assist with procurement or arrangements for HR-related meetings and events.
Support the smooth running of the HR office and daily administrative activities.
Stakeholder and Employee Support
Receive and attend to employees and visitors to the HR office in a professional manner.
Maintain positive working relationships with staff, applicants, and external contacts.
Represent the HR department professionally when communicating on approved matters.
Problem Solving and Proactive Support
Anticipate the needs of the HR department and take appropriate action within assigned authority.
Identify potential administrative or documentation issues and recommend practical solutions.
Handle multiple HR tasks efficiently while maintaining accuracy and professionalism.
Other Duties
Perform other reasonable HR or administrative support duties as assigned.
Support special HR projects and assignments as required.

Minimum of 3-5 years\' experience as an HR Manager , HR Officer, Administrative Assistant, or in a similar support role.

Experience assisting with recruitment, onboarding, or employee records administration is an added advantage.

Excellent proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook/email platforms.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Excellent organizational and time-management skills

Excellent written and verbal communication

Excellent record-keeping and follow-up ability
Strong interpersonal and relationship management skills

Ability to prioritize multiple tasks and meet deadlines

Resilient and result-driven, with great prospecting skills. Proven ability in developing strong relationships and partnerships with customers and relevant stakeholders.

Strong interpersonal skills with a collaborative and flexible work style. Willing to travel and engage with our customers at various locations

Job Description:
We are looking to hire a Public Health implementation officer to coordinate implementation within Kano state to oversee field activities and stakeholder engagement, monitor performance, and ensure programme targets and deliverables are achieved.
Responsibilities
State-Level Project Implementation:
Coordinate implementation of programme activities within the state in line with approved workplans, timelines, targets, and quality standards.
Translate programme plans and milestones into weekly and monthly state-level implementation activities.
Coordinate implementation across participating healthcare facilities, communities, community health workers, and other field partners.
Track state-level milestones and proactively identify and escalate implementation delays, risks, and operational challenges.
Coordinate state-level activities including sensitisation, training, recruitment drives, facility engagement, stakeholder meetings, and programme reviews.
User Recruitment and Activation:
Implement the state's user recruitment and activation strategy across participating facilities and communities.
Coordinate facility-based recruitment, CHW outreach, community activation drives, referrals, and partner-led recruitment activities.
Set and monitor recruitment targets for field personnel and participating facilities in line with programme targets.
Support field teams to identify eligible women and onboard them onto the digital platform.
Monitor recruitment and activation data to ensure reported users are appropriately onboarded and meet programme requirements.
Identify underperforming locations or recruitment channels and implement corrective actions with the project team.
Field Team and CHW Coordination:
Coordinate and supervise CHWs and other field personnel supporting programme implementation within the state.
Assign activities and performance targets and monitor delivery against agreed expectations.
Conduct regular field-team check-ins and provide implementation guidance and problem-solving support.
Ensure field personnel have the training, information, materials, and operational support required to carry out their responsibilities.
Review and validate field activity reports and supporting documentation.
Health Facility Coordination:
Build and maintain effective working relationships with participating public and private healthcare facilities.
Coordinate facility onboarding and implementation of programme activities within participating facilities.
Work with facility focal persons and recruitment stewards to support user recruitment, risk assessment, sensitisation, and adoption of the programme's digital tools.
Monitor facility participation and address or escalate implementation challenges.
Coordinate facility-level capacity-building and ongoing implementation support.
Government and Stakeholder Engagement:
Serve as the day-to-day programme liaison with relevant state-level government stakeholders, under the direction of the programme leadership team.
Maintain effective working relationships with the State Ministry of Health, participating facilities, community stakeholders, and implementation partners.
Support state kickoff meetings, advocacy engagements, dashboard reviews, programme reviews, and other stakeholder meetings.
Document agreed actions from stakeholder engagements and ensure appropriate follow-up.
Represent the programme at approved state-level meetings and engagements as required.
Training and Implementation Support:
Coordinate orientation and capacity-building activities for CHWs, facility personnel, and other relevant stakeholders.
Support field personnel and participating facilities in effectively using the programme's digital tools.
Identify recurring operational or user challenges and escalate technical issues to the appropriate central team.
Gather structured feedback from users, healthcare facilities, and field personnel to support continuous improvement.
Monitoring, Data Quality and Reporting:
Track state performance against programme indicators, recruitment targets, facility targets, and implementation milestones.
Maintain accurate records of recruitment, facility participation, field activities, training, stakeholder engagement, and other programme activities.
Review field data for completeness, accuracy, and consistency and ensure identified discrepancies are resolved.
Prepare and submit timely weekly and monthly implementation reports.
Use programme dashboards and other monitoring tools to identify performance gaps and support corrective action.
Document implementation lessons, challenges, beneficiary feedback, and relevant success stories.
Logistics and Resource Management:
Coordinate logistics for field activities, community activation drives, training, facility visits, and stakeholder engagements.
Ensure appropriate use and accountability for programme resources and materials assigned to the state.
Maintain accurate documentation of materials distributed, field activities, and other required implementation records.
Coordinate field schedules to support efficient use of programme resources.
Quality, Safeguarding and Compliance:
Ensure state-level implementation complies with approved programme protocols, organizational policies, data-protection requirements, and relevant ethical and regulatory requirements.
Ensure appropriate confidentiality and handling of participant and programme information.
Ensure recruitment and community-engagement activities are conducted respectfully and in accordance with approved programme procedures.
Identify and promptly escalate quality, safeguarding, or compliance concerns.
Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Public Health, Nursing, Community Health, Health Sciences, Social Sciences, or a related field.
Minimum of 4 years of relevant experience in public health programme implementation, community health, field operations, healthcare delivery, or a related area.
Demonstrated experience coordinating field-based health programmes and working with healthcare facilities, CHWs, government stakeholders, or community-based organisations.
Experience supervising or coordinating field teams and managing implementation and performance targets.
Strong understanding of community engagement, health programme implementation, and field-level monitoring.
Experience with maternal and reproductive health programmes is an advantage.
Experience working with digital health or technology-enabled healthcare interventions is an advantage.
Strong reporting, documentation, data-quality, and basic analytical skills.
Ability to interpret programme data and use performance information to guide implementation decisions.
Excellent communication, stakeholder-management, and interpersonal skills.
Strong organisational skills and ability to coordinate multiple activities and stakeholders simultaneously.
Ability and willingness to travel regularly within the assigned state.
Fluency in English and proficiency in relevant local languages is an advantage.
Resident in the Kano state.
Benefits
This role offers a competitive pay and other benefits and perks.
