Job Title: Senior Technical Advisor – Global Health Security & Surveillance
Job Description:
Summary
As the Lead consortium implementing a programme focused on Global Health Security, disease surveillance, outbreak preparedness and response, and sustainable health-system transition, we are seeking a highly experienced Senior Technical Advisor – Global Health Security & Surveillance.
The Role
The Senior Technical Advisor will serve as the organization's principal technical focal point and point of contact within the consortium for Global Health Security and surveillance-related activities.
The position will provide strategic and technical leadership to ensure effective coordination between the organisation, consortium partners, government institutions and other stakeholders.
The STA will support the design, implementation, monitoring and continuous improvement of interventions that strengthen infectious disease detection, surveillance, preparedness and outbreak response, while promoting integration of human and animal health systems through a One Health approach.
The STA will also contribute to the transition of donor-supported interventions toward sustainable, country-owned systems, with particular attention to subnational surveillance, laboratory networks, sample transportation, Emergency Operations Centers (EOCs), rapid response teams and diagnostic capacity.
Key Responsibilities
Consortium Technical Coordination:
Serve as the organization's primary technical representative and point of contact for the consortium.
Establish and maintain effective working relationships with consortium members, government counterparts and relevant technical stakeholders.
Represent the organisation in consortium technical meetings, working groups, coordination platforms and programme review sessions.
Coordinate the organization's technical contributions to consortium workplans, deliverables, reports and learning activities.
Promote harmonisation of approaches, tools, standards and implementation strategies across consortium partners.
Identify implementation challenges and facilitate timely technical solutions with consortium members.
Ensure effective communication and information flow between the organisation, consortium leadership and implementing partners.
Global Health Security and Outbreak Preparedness:
Provide technical leadership for activities supporting country readiness for infectious disease outbreak detection, preparedness and response.
Support government coordination platforms for joint programme supervision, strategic planning and outbreak preparedness.
Strengthen systems for timely detection, notification, investigation and response to infectious disease threats.
Support the strengthening of subnational Emergency Operations Centers and rapid response team capacity.
Promote evidence-based approaches to preparedness for high-priority infectious disease threats, including cholera, measles and zoonotic diseases.
Integrated Disease Surveillance and One Health:
Provide technical guidance for strengthening integrated disease surveillance systems at national and subnational levels.
Support implementation of integrated surveillance and outbreak response approaches consistent with the One Health framework.
Facilitate collaboration among human health, animal health and other relevant sectors.
Strengthen linkages between surveillance structures, laboratories, rapid response teams and emergency operations centers.
Support capacity building of district/provincial surveillance teams and other frontline personnel.
Laboratory Systems and Diagnostic Networks:
Provide technical support to strengthen subnational laboratory systems and diagnostic networks.
Support development and strengthening of sample collection, referral and transportation systems, including appropriate cold-chain arrangements.
Strengthen referral pathways between district and provincial laboratories.
Support improvements in specialized diagnostic capacity, including genomic sequencing, TB culture and drug susceptibility testing where applicable.
Promote quality assurance, biosafety and appropriate laboratory standards within supported facilities and networks.
Identify laboratory-system bottlenecks and work with consortium partners and government stakeholders to develop practical solutions.
Emergency Operations Centers and Rapid Response:
Support the establishment, operationalization and strengthening of subnational EOCs.
Strengthen district-level outbreak preparedness and response mechanisms, particularly in high-risk areas.
Support development and testing of outbreak response plans, SOPs, coordination mechanisms and escalation pathways.
Strengthen the capacity of Rapid Response Teams through training, mentorship, simulation exercises and supportive supervision.
Promote timely linkage of surveillance alerts to investigation, laboratory confirmation and response.
Infection Prevention and Control:
Provide technical support to strengthen Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) measures across supported levels of the health system.
Support assessment of IPC capacity, identification of gaps and implementation of improvement plans.
Promote integration of IPC into routine service delivery and outbreak preparedness activities.
Support capacity building and mentorship of healthcare workers on appropriate IPC practices.
Community and Health-Service Linkages:
Support approaches that strengthen community engagement in disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness.
Contribute technical support to interventions addressing PMTCT coverage and engagement of pregnant women and communities.
Promote linkages between community-based surveillance structures and formal health-system surveillance mechanisms.
Support strategies that improve early identification, referral and follow-up of priority health threats.
Sustainability and Transition to Country Ownership:
Provide technical leadership to support the transition of donor-supported programmes toward sustainable, country-owned systems.
Work with government counterparts to strengthen institutional ownership, capacity and accountability.
Support development of transition and sustainability plans for surveillance, laboratory, EOC and outbreak response functions.
Identify opportunities for integration of programme-supported systems into existing government structures and financing mechanisms.
Promote approaches that reduce dependence on parallel donor-supported systems.
Capacity Building and Technical Assistance:
Conduct capacity and systems assessments and translate findings into practical technical assistance plans.
Develop or contribute to development of training materials, SOPs, guidelines, job aids and other technical products.
Facilitate training, mentorship, coaching and supportive supervision for government and implementing-partner personnel.
Promote institutionalization of skills and knowledge within government structures.
Document lessons learned, promising practices and innovations for programme improvement and scale-up.
Monitoring, Learning and Reporting:
Contribute to development and implementation of programme indicators and technical performance frameworks.
Monitor progress against technical deliverables, milestones and agreed consortium commitments.
Analyze surveillance, laboratory, outbreak preparedness and response data to identify performance gaps and opportunities for improvement.
Prepare high-quality technical reports, presentations, briefs and success stories.
Contribute to donor reports, consortium reporting and programme review meetings.
Support documentation and dissemination of lessons learned and evidence generated by the programme.
Required Qualifications and Experience
Master's Degree or higher in Public Health, Epidemiology, Global Health, Health Systems Management, Infectious Disease, One Health, Laboratory Sciences, Veterinary Public Health or a closely related discipline.
Medical, veterinary, laboratory science or other relevant clinical/public-health professional qualification will be an advantage.
At least 8–10 years of progressively responsible experience in public health, global health security, disease surveillance, outbreak preparedness/response or health systems strengthening.
Demonstrated experience working with government health institutions and multi-partner/consortium programmes.
Strong technical experience in one or more of the following areas:
Integrated disease surveillance and response;
Global Health Security;
One Health;
Outbreak preparedness and response;
Emergency Operations Centers;
Rapid Response Teams;
Laboratory systems and diagnostic networks;
Infection Prevention and Control;
Health-system strengthening and transition.
Experience working at subnational/district/provincial level is highly desirable.
Experience supporting donor-funded health programmes and working within complex consortium arrangements.
Demonstrated experience in technical assistance, capacity building, mentorship and institutional strengthening.
Experience in programme planning, implementation monitoring and technical reporting.
Strong understanding of government health systems and stakeholder coordination mechanisms.
Core Competencies
The successful candidate will demonstrate:
Strategic technical leadership
Excellent consortium and stakeholder coordination skills
Strong understanding of Global Health Security principles
Expertise in surveillance and outbreak preparedness/response
Ability to work effectively across human, animal and environmental health sectors
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities
Excellent communication, facilitation and presentation skills
Strong report-writing and technical documentation skills
Ability to translate technical evidence into practical programme interventions
Strong interpersonal and relationship-management skills
Ability to work collaboratively in a multi-cultural, multi-disciplinary consortium
Commitment to country ownership, sustainability and health-system strengthening
Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality outputs within deadlines
Key Working Relationships
The Senior Technical Advisor will work closely with:
Consortium technical leads and partner organisations
Federal and subnational Ministries/Departments/Agencies of Health
Public health and disease surveillance institutions
Emergency Operations Centers
Rapid Response Teams
Public health and veterinary laboratories
Human and animal health authorities
Local government/district health teams
Community and civil society organizations
Donors and other technical partners.
Key Deliverables
The STA will be expected to contribute to or lead delivery of:
Consortium technical workplans and implementation plans.
Global Health Security and surveillance technical strategies.
Subnational surveillance strengthening plans.
Laboratory and sample transportation strengthening plans.
EOC and Rapid Response Team capacity-strengthening plans.
One Health coordination and implementation approaches.
IPC improvement and capacity-building plans.
Technical training and mentorship packages.
Transition and sustainability plans supporting country ownership.
Technical progress reports, presentations and programme briefs.
Documentation of lessons learned, innovations and best practices.
Other technical deliverables required under the consortium Scope of Work.
What We Offer
An opportunity to provide strategic leadership on a high-impact Global Health Security programme.
Collaboration with government institutions, leading consortium partners and technical stakeholders.
Opportunities to influence sustainable national and subnational health-system capacity.
A professional environment focused on learning, innovation and measurable public health impact.
Competitive remuneration and benefits commensurate with qualifications and experience.

Company Details:
Wellspring University is a private university promoted by Management Science Centre and approved by the Federal Government. It operates on Christian ethics and principles.

The vision of the university is to mould the new Nigerian who will have the intellectual knowledge and moral strength for app...read morelying science and technology to the piloting of national development. 

In 1983, a group of academics and professionals came together in Lagos under the name, Management Science Centre, to render consultancy and training services to the teeming population of working men and women who had the common problem of inability to leave their employments to undertake full-time tertiary education.

The Centre commenced operations on a modest scale with the private coaching of students of the University of Lagos Correspondence and Open Studies Institute (COSIT), later renamed Distant Learning Institute (DLI).

By 1995, the modest foundation of 1983 had brought Management Science Centre into joint relationships with several institutions of higher learning in Nigeria, among which are the Auchi Polytechnic, Auchi, Edo State; University of Ibadan, Ibadan, Oyo State and Ambrose Alli University, Ekpoma, Edo State.

Our achievements in the programmes undertaken gave rise to a desire for expansion in order to contribute optimally to the development of education in Nigeria. The result was the establishment of Wisdom Gate High School in 2001 and Wellspring College in 2003, both secondary schools of international standard that placed great emphasis on moral upbringing. Then in 2006, the Centre established the Cornerstone College of Education in Lagos.

The motive of serving as a Centre of learning where Nigerian children, who are hungry for university education that is based on sound moral and spiritual principles, can accomplish their ambitions has always been the core of our vision. Thus, after more than twenty five years of serving the education sector, Management Science Centre considered itself strong enough to establish a full-fledged university.

To the glory of God, Wellspring University (WU) was licensed by the Federal Government of Nigeria in November 2009. WU is founded on Christian principles and ethics. WU is committed to providing quality education that will impact on the intellect and morals of its students.

The dream of the founders of WU is for it to become a world class institution, capable of delivering locally and globally relevant university education. This dream came to fruition in 2011 when WU joined the league of international universities offering cross border university education. In August 2011, WU signed an MOU with the famed Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Kumasi, Ghana, to run joint international degree programmes. WU's collaboration with KNUST is under the auspices of the National Universities Commission (NUC), through its Pilot Scheme on Cross Border University Education.

This landmark achievement makes WU one of the first Nigerian universities that will be awarding joint international degrees. We give glory to our Lord!

WU and KNUST are committed to using the latest and the best in technology and teaching principles and methods to produce God-fearing world leaders in science, technology, business and the arts.

By 1995, the modest foundation of 1983 had brought Management Science Centre into joint relationships with several institutions of higher learning in Nigeria, among which are the Auchi Polytechnic, Auchi, Edo State; University of Ibadan, Ibadan, Oyo State and Ambrose Alli University, Ekpoma, Edo State.

Our achievements in the programmes undertaken gave rise to a desire for expansion in order to contribute optimally to the development of education in Nigeria. The result was the establishment of Wisdom Gate High School in 2001 and Wellspring College in 2003, both secondary schools of international standard that placed great emphasis on moral upbringing. Then in 2006, the Centre established the Cornerstone College of Education in Lagos.

The motive of serving as a Centre of learning where Nigerian children, who are hungry for university education that is based on sound moral and spiritual principles, can accomplish their ambitions has always been the core of our vision. Thus, after more than twenty five years of serving the education sector, Management Science Centre considered itself strong enough to establish a full-fledged university.

To the glory of God, Wellspring University (WU) was licensed by the Federal Government of Nigeria in November 2009. WU is founded on Christian principles and ethics. WU is committed to providing quality education that will impact on the intellect and morals of its students.

The dream of the founders of WU is for it to become a world class institution, capable of delivering locally and globally relevant university education. This dream came to fruition in 2011 when WU joined the league of international universities offering cross border university education. In August 2011, WU signed an MOU with the famed Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Kumasi, Ghana, to run joint international degree programmes. WU's collaboration with KNUST is under the auspices of the National Universities Commission (NUC), through its Pilot Scheme on Cross Border University Education.

This landmark achievement makes WU one of the first Nigerian universities that will be awarding joint international degrees. We give glory to our Lord!

WU and KNUST are committed to using the latest and the best in technology and teaching principles and methods to produce God-fearing world leaders in science, technology, business and the arts.

Job Description:
Job Summary
The Legal Executive will provide comprehensive legal and corporate advisory support to the organization, ensuring that the company’s activities, transactions, contracts, policies, and business decisions are legally sound and compliant with applicable laws and regulations. The role will be responsible for managing the company’s internal legal affairs, reviewing and drafting commercial agreements, identifying and mitigating legal risks, supporting corporate governance, and coordinating with external solicitors and regulatory authorities where required.
Duties and Responsibilities
Provide timely and practical legal advice to Management and various departments on corporate, commercial, operational, employment, contractual, and regulatory matters.
Draft, review, negotiate, and advise on contracts, agreements, Memoranda of Understanding, service agreements, leases, employment-related documents, NDAs, and other legal instruments.
Review business transactions and proposed engagements to identify legal risks and recommend appropriate measures to protect the organization.
Manage the organization’s internal legal affairs and maintain proper records of legal documents, agreements, notices, correspondence, and legal matters.
Ensure that contracts and other legal documents are properly executed, maintained, monitored, and renewed where applicable.
Monitor contractual obligations, key legal dates, renewals, expirations, and compliance requirements.
Conduct legal research and provide advice on applicable laws, regulations, industry requirements, and emerging legal developments affecting the organization.
Support the development, review, and implementation of company policies, procedures, terms and conditions, and internal legal frameworks.
Advise HR/Admin on employment-related matters, disciplinary issues, employee relations, workplace policies, and applicable labour laws.
Liaise with external solicitors and legal advisers on litigation, arbitration, regulatory matters, and other specialised legal issues.
Coordinate the preparation of legal responses, letters, notices, pleadings, affidavits, and other legal correspondence where required.
Support Management in corporate governance matters, statutory compliance, corporate filings, board and management documentation, and related corporate activities.
Monitor regulatory and statutory compliance requirements applicable to the organization and escalate areas of potential exposure.
Liaise with relevant government agencies, regulators, professional bodies, and other authorities on legal and regulatory matters.
Assist in conducting legal due diligence on clients, vendors, partners, projects, and prospectivebusiness engagements where required.
Review procurement, vendor, partnership, and client documentation to ensure appropriate legal protections are incorporated.
Develop and maintain a central register of contracts, legal matters, litigation, regulatory obligations, and other significant legal risks.
Support the organization in managing confidentiality, intellectual property, data protection, and information governance matters.
Provide legal guidance during negotiations with clients, vendors, partners, and other third parties.
Identify potential legal and commercial risks and recommend appropriate mitigation strategies to Management.
Maintain strict confidentiality of company information, legal advice, contracts, disputes, and other sensitive matters.
Carry out any other legal or corporate responsibilities assigned by Management.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in law (LL.B) from a recognised institution.
Called to the Nigerian Bar and in good standing.
Minimum of 7 years’ post-call legal experience in corporate, commercial, or in-house legal practice.
Demonstrable experience in managing corporate internal legal affairs, contract management, legal advisory, compliance, and risk management.
Strong experience in drafting, reviewing, and negotiating commercial and corporate agreements.
Experience working in an in-house legal department or advising corporate organisations will be highly advantageous.
Good knowledge of Nigerian corporate, commercial, employment, regulatory, and contract law.
Experience liaising with external solicitors, regulators, government agencies, and other professional advisers.
Strong legal research, analytical, negotiation, and problem-solving skills.
Membership of relevant professional bodies or additional certifications in corporate governance, compliance, contract management, or related areas will be an advantage.
Competency Description
Legal Advisory
Ability to provide sound, practical, and commercially focused legal advice to Management and business units.
Contract Management
Strong ability to draft, review, negotiate, and manage commercial and corporate contracts.
Corporate & Commercial Law
Strong understanding of corporate structures, commercial transactions, regulatory requirements, and business operations.
Legal Research
Ability to conduct thorough legal research and interpret legislation, regulations, case law, and legal developments.
Risk Management
Ability to identify legal and contractual risks and recommend effective mitigation measures.
Negotiation
Strong negotiation skills with the ability to protect the organization’s interests while achieving commercially practical outcomes.
Communication
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex legal matters clearly to non-legal stakeholders.
Analytical & Problem-Solving
Strong analytical ability and sound judgement in assessing legal and business issues.
Corporate Governance
Good understanding of corporate governance principles, statutory obligations, board documentation, and regulatory compliance.
Attention to Detail
High level of accuracy in reviewing contracts, legal documents, correspondence, and regulatory requirements.
Confidentiality & Integrity
Ability to handle highly confidential information with discretion, professionalism, and sound ethical judgement.
Stakeholder Management
Ability to work effectively with Management, employees, clients, vendors, regulators, external solicitors, and other stakeholders.

Job Description:
Summary
The Account Manager - Solar (Public Sector) will be responsible for driving business development, revenue growth, and account management across government institutions and publicly funded organisations.
The role will focus on identifying and converting opportunities across Federal and State Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), local government administrations, public hospitals, schools, water utilities, and other government-owned facilities. The successful candidate will leverage a strong understanding of public-sector procurement processes to identify opportunities, manage tenders and proposals, build strategic government relationships, and secure institutional contracts for reliable energy solutions.
Key Responsibilities
Public Sector Sales & Business Development:
Identify, develop, and manage business opportunities across Federal and State MDAs, local government administrations, and publicly owned facilities.
Target public hospitals, schools, water utilities, government offices, and other institutions with significant energy requirements.
Monitor government procurement portals, tender publications, RFPs, and relevant development-partner platforms for business opportunities.
Identify and pursue opportunities related to solar energy, distributed power, mini-grid, and other energy solutions.
Build and maintain relationships with technical officers, procurement teams, senior government officials, and other key decision-makers within target institutions.
Develop partnerships, consortiums, and subcontracting opportunities with infrastructure, construction, and EPC companies bidding for government projects with energy components.
Engage state energy agencies, rural electrification agencies, and other relevant institutions to identify programme and project opportunities.
Build and manage a strong public-sector sales pipeline and convert qualified opportunities into contracts.
Tender & Proposal Management:
Lead the end-to-end preparation and submission of public-sector bids, tenders, RFQs, RFPs, and Expressions of Interest.
Ensure tender submissions comply with procurement requirements, technical specifications, commercial conditions, and submission deadlines.
Coordinate with Technical, Finance, Legal, and Management teams to develop complete and competitive tender submissions.
Prepare high-quality tender documents, executive briefs, commercial proposals, and supporting documentation.
Maintain an up-to-date library of corporate registration documents, certifications, company profiles, financial credentials, and other documents required for government prequalification and tender submissions.
Track tender outcomes, maintain a database of opportunities, and identify areas for improving future submissions.
Develop and maintain relationships with Development Finance Institutions (DFIs), climate funds, grant-making organisations, and development partners to identify funding and partnership opportunities.
Government & Stakeholder Relations:
Build and maintain strategic relationships with relevant Federal and State government stakeholders.
Engage senior officials, including Directors, Commissioners, Directors-General, and other appropriate decision-makers within relevant agencies.
Represent the organisation at government energy forums, public-sector events, industry conferences, and policy engagement platforms.
Monitor government energy policies, regulatory developments, electrification programmes, and state energy initiatives to identify emerging business opportunities.
Develop strong institutional relationships that support long-term business development and account growth.
Account Management:
Manage active government and institutional accounts following contract award and project implementation.
Maintain strong relationships with government stakeholders throughout the contract lifecycle.
Monitor contract performance, project milestones, reporting requirements, and documentation.
Coordinate with relevant internal teams to address commercial, operational, or service-related issues affecting government accounts.
Identify opportunities for account expansion, additional projects, renewals, and repeat business.
Ensure continuity of relationships and effective stakeholder engagement throughout the project lifecycle.
Reporting & Market Intelligence:
Maintain accurate CRM records and submit daily, weekly, and monthly pipeline, activity, and revenue reports.
Track public-sector procurement activities, upcoming projects, government programmes, and development-funded initiatives.
Monitor competitor activity and market developments within the public-sector energy space.
Provide timely market intelligence and insights to support business development and sales strategy.
Track sales performance against agreed targets and KPIs.
Requirements & Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration, Marketing, Science, Engineering, or a related field.
Minimum 4 years' experience in public-sector sales within the Solar industy, business development, institutional sales, or government relations in Nigeria.
Proven track record of successfully securing government, institutional, or publicly funded contracts.
Strong understanding of public-sector procurement processes and government contracting.
Demonstrated experience preparing and managing competitive tenders, RFPs, RFQs, and Expressions of Interest.
Strong network and established relationships across Federal and State MDAs, parastatals, public institutions, and/or development partner organisations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, particularly in tender documentation, proposal writing, executive briefs, and formal presentations.
Proficiency in CRM systems and sales reporting platforms.
Understanding of solar PV, battery storage, distributed energy, mini-grid, or energy management solutions is an advantage.
Experience with asset financing or structured financing sales models.
Experience working with Development Finance Institutions (DFIs), climate funds, development agencies, NGOs, or grant-funded programmes.
Experience working with infrastructure, construction, or EPC companies on government projects.
Existing relationships with relevant government agencies, public institutions, or development partners.

Job Description:
Job Summary
The Finance Manager will be responsible for managing and coordinating the financial operations of the organization, ensuring accurate financial reporting, effective financial controls, prudent cash management, compliance with applicable financial and tax regulations, and the timely provision of financial information to Management for decision-making.
The role will oversee budgeting, financial planning and analysis, accounts payable and receivable, cash flow management, reconciliations, management reporting, statutory compliance, audit coordination, and financial controls. The Finance Manager will also support Management in monitoring financial performance, controlling costs, identifying financial risks, and improving the overall financial efficiency of the organization.
Duties and Responsibilities
Manage and coordinate the day-to-day financial and accounting activities of the organization.
Ensure accurate and timely preparation of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports.
Prepare management accounts, financial statements, financial analysis, and other reports required by Management.
Monitor the organization’s cash flow, working capital, receivables, payables, and overall liquidity position.
Prepare and monitor annual budgets and periodic financial forecasts in collaboration with relevant departments.
Analyse budget performance and investigate significant variances, providing explanations and recommendations to Management.
Develop and maintain effective financial controls to safeguard company assets and ensure the integrity of financial information.
Review payment requests, invoices, expenses, and supporting documentation to ensure accuracy, completeness, and compliance with approved processes.
Oversee accounts payable and receivable functions, ensuring timely processing, reconciliation, and collection of outstanding balances.
Monitor customer receivables and follow up on overdue accounts in collaboration with relevant departments.
Ensure timely bank reconciliations and reconciliation of relevant general ledger and subsidiary accounts.
Monitor banking activities, transfers, collections, payments, and other financial transactions.
Ensure proper maintenance and filing of accounting records, financial documents, invoices, receipts, and supporting schedules.
Coordinate the preparation and submission of statutory financial and tax returns in line with applicable requirements.
Liaise with tax consultants, external auditors, banks, regulators, and other financial advisers as required.
Coordinate internal and external audit activities and ensure timely provision of requested financial information and supporting documentation.
Monitor audit findings and coordinate the implementation of agreed corrective actions.
Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, tax regulations, company policies, and financial procedures.
Provide financial analysis and advice to Management on business decisions, investments, cost management, and financial risks.
Support Management in evaluating the financial implications of contracts, projects, business opportunities, and major expenditures.
Monitor operational costs and identify opportunities for cost optimisation and improved financial efficiency.
Review financial processes and recommend improvements to strengthen controls, efficiency, and accountability.
Support procurement and other departments in financial evaluations, vendor payments, pricing reviews, and commercial assessments where required.
Monitor fixed assets, company assets, depreciation schedules, and related financial records.

Lead the drive to strategically develop and fully integrate best practice technology in education in institution Schools.

Liaise with other functional/departmental managers to ensure they are fully informed of HR objectives, purpose, and achievements.

Master’s Degree in Education, Educational Management, Educational Administration, or a related field is highly preferred.
Relevant professional certifications in Educational Leadership or School Management will be an added advantage.
Minimum of 15 years’ experience in whole-school management, covering both academic leadership and school operations.
Proven experience in senior educational leadership, with responsibility for academic excellence, administration, staff management, curriculum development, student welfare, and operational performance.
Experience managing and coordinating Heads of Schools/Units and multidisciplinary teams within a structured educational institution.
Strong track record in strategic planning, performance management, quality assurance, accreditation, safeguarding, stakeholder management, and continuous school improvement.

Company Details:
Wellspring University is a private university promoted by Management Science Centre and approved by the Federal Government. It operates on Christian ethics and principles.

The vision of the university is to mould the new Nigerian who will have the intellectual knowledge and moral strength for app...read morelying science and technology to the piloting of national development. 

In 1983, a group of academics and professionals came together in Lagos under the name, Management Science Centre, to render consultancy and training services to the teeming population of working men and women who had the common problem of inability to leave their employments to undertake full-time tertiary education.

The Centre commenced operations on a modest scale with the private coaching of students of the University of Lagos Correspondence and Open Studies Institute (COSIT), later renamed Distant Learning Institute (DLI).

By 1995, the modest foundation of 1983 had brought Management Science Centre into joint relationships with several institutions of higher learning in Nigeria, among which are the Auchi Polytechnic, Auchi, Edo State; University of Ibadan, Ibadan, Oyo State and Ambrose Alli University, Ekpoma, Edo State.

Our achievements in the programmes undertaken gave rise to a desire for expansion in order to contribute optimally to the development of education in Nigeria. The result was the establishment of Wisdom Gate High School in 2001 and Wellspring College in 2003, both secondary schools of international standard that placed great emphasis on moral upbringing. Then in 2006, the Centre established the Cornerstone College of Education in Lagos.

The motive of serving as a Centre of learning where Nigerian children, who are hungry for university education that is based on sound moral and spiritual principles, can accomplish their ambitions has always been the core of our vision. Thus, after more than twenty five years of serving the education sector, Management Science Centre considered itself strong enough to establish a full-fledged university.

To the glory of God, Wellspring University (WU) was licensed by the Federal Government of Nigeria in November 2009. WU is founded on Christian principles and ethics. WU is committed to providing quality education that will impact on the intellect and morals of its students.

The dream of the founders of WU is for it to become a world class institution, capable of delivering locally and globally relevant university education. This dream came to fruition in 2011 when WU joined the league of international universities offering cross border university education. In August 2011, WU signed an MOU with the famed Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Kumasi, Ghana, to run joint international degree programmes. WU's collaboration with KNUST is under the auspices of the National Universities Commission (NUC), through its Pilot Scheme on Cross Border University Education.

This landmark achievement makes WU one of the first Nigerian universities that will be awarding joint international degrees. We give glory to our Lord!

WU and KNUST are committed to using the latest and the best in technology and teaching principles and methods to produce God-fearing world leaders in science, technology, business and the arts.

By 1995, the modest foundation of 1983 had brought Management Science Centre into joint relationships with several institutions of higher learning in Nigeria, among which are the Auchi Polytechnic, Auchi, Edo State; University of Ibadan, Ibadan, Oyo State and Ambrose Alli University, Ekpoma, Edo State.

Our achievements in the programmes undertaken gave rise to a desire for expansion in order to contribute optimally to the development of education in Nigeria. The result was the establishment of Wisdom Gate High School in 2001 and Wellspring College in 2003, both secondary schools of international standard that placed great emphasis on moral upbringing. Then in 2006, the Centre established the Cornerstone College of Education in Lagos.

The motive of serving as a Centre of learning where Nigerian children, who are hungry for university education that is based on sound moral and spiritual principles, can accomplish their ambitions has always been the core of our vision. Thus, after more than twenty five years of serving the education sector, Management Science Centre considered itself strong enough to establish a full-fledged university.

To the glory of God, Wellspring University (WU) was licensed by the Federal Government of Nigeria in November 2009. WU is founded on Christian principles and ethics. WU is committed to providing quality education that will impact on the intellect and morals of its students.

The dream of the founders of WU is for it to become a world class institution, capable of delivering locally and globally relevant university education. This dream came to fruition in 2011 when WU joined the league of international universities offering cross border university education. In August 2011, WU signed an MOU with the famed Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Kumasi, Ghana, to run joint international degree programmes. WU's collaboration with KNUST is under the auspices of the National Universities Commission (NUC), through its Pilot Scheme on Cross Border University Education.

This landmark achievement makes WU one of the first Nigerian universities that will be awarding joint international degrees. We give glory to our Lord!

WU and KNUST are committed to using the latest and the best in technology and teaching principles and methods to produce God-fearing world leaders in science, technology, business and the arts.

Job Title: Head of Mechanical: Rotating, Static, Lifting & Marine Equip
Job Description:
Job Details
Responsible for the Technical content of the Maintenance Methods in the field of Mechanical, including the responsibility for maintenance plans, spare parts coverage, working techniques, and the procedures, in accordance with the Maintenance Policy.
Revise the maintenance plans prepared by the various Contractors and ensure their proper implementation.
Coordinate with the Methods Department the consolidation of the Maintenance Plans.
Ensure suitable spare-parts availability/coverage through adequate stock management parameters; initiate the necessary improvements in accordance with the reliability, availability objectives and cost optimization.
Perform the duties of Technical Administrator for the Mechanical Spare Parts.Develop and control proper implementation/use of the techniques and tools required for an efficient maintenance, including both technical (condition monitoring, working tools, etc.…) and administrative/reporting aspects (Work reports, data trending, spare parts consumption, etc.…).
Responsible to control and ensure the data captured in SAP (UNISUP) are accurate; perform their analysis and propose optimization plans.Ensures proper management of the equipment support means including documentations, tooling, software, etc.
Provides technical expertise in view of timely and efficiently address the failures and losses of performance of equipment.Analyse the equipment performances, perform technical studies, provide technical support on any technical queries, and make proposals for improvement and optimization.
Perform modification studies as required. Ensure the operations under own authority are prepared and performed in accordance with Company rules, procedures and specifications, and in full compliance with the HSE standards.
Responsible for the mobilisation, the coordination, the logistic arrangements, of the external resources (vendors, contractors, means, etc.…) required for the operations in own field of competence (mechanical). Includes initiation of call off, or service order, definition of scope of work, work performance follow-up, control/acceptance of deliverables, and any other duty until satisfactory completion of the required service.
Ensure professionalism and competence of selected contractors, initiate or participate to audits for that purpose.
Contributes to the technical administration of Contracts (MTMC, MSC, CMOC, FMC, etc.…), control performance, and follow-up call-offs as required.Provides technical assistance of whatever nature to site operational staff, in accordance with the operational requirements.
Participates in budget preparation, contribute to cost control of operations under own technical authority.
Contributes to training and development of the National staff, and in particular of the engineers and technicians under his authority.
Coordinates these actions with concerned staff, from both offshore and onshore.Acting Maintenance Operation Manager when necessary.
Requirements
Engineer University Degree in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent.
Good Knowledge in Turbo machineries.

Lead the day-to-day operations of the company’s IT infrastructure, systems, networks, and end-user technology.

Company Details:
Wellspring University is a private university promoted by Management Science Centre and approved by the Federal Government. It operates on Christian ethics and principles.

The vision of the university is to mould the new Nigerian who will have the intellectual knowledge and moral strength for app...read morelying science and technology to the piloting of national development. 

In 1983, a group of academics and professionals came together in Lagos under the name, Management Science Centre, to render consultancy and training services to the teeming population of working men and women who had the common problem of inability to leave their employments to undertake full-time tertiary education.

The Centre commenced operations on a modest scale with the private coaching of students of the University of Lagos Correspondence and Open Studies Institute (COSIT), later renamed Distant Learning Institute (DLI).

By 1995, the modest foundation of 1983 had brought Management Science Centre into joint relationships with several institutions of higher learning in Nigeria, among which are the Auchi Polytechnic, Auchi, Edo State; University of Ibadan, Ibadan, Oyo State and Ambrose Alli University, Ekpoma, Edo State.

Our achievements in the programmes undertaken gave rise to a desire for expansion in order to contribute optimally to the development of education in Nigeria. The result was the establishment of Wisdom Gate High School in 2001 and Wellspring College in 2003, both secondary schools of international standard that placed great emphasis on moral upbringing. Then in 2006, the Centre established the Cornerstone College of Education in Lagos.

The motive of serving as a Centre of learning where Nigerian children, who are hungry for university education that is based on sound moral and spiritual principles, can accomplish their ambitions has always been the core of our vision. Thus, after more than twenty five years of serving the education sector, Management Science Centre considered itself strong enough to establish a full-fledged university.

To the glory of God, Wellspring University (WU) was licensed by the Federal Government of Nigeria in November 2009. WU is founded on Christian principles and ethics. WU is committed to providing quality education that will impact on the intellect and morals of its students.

The dream of the founders of WU is for it to become a world class institution, capable of delivering locally and globally relevant university education. This dream came to fruition in 2011 when WU joined the league of international universities offering cross border university education. In August 2011, WU signed an MOU with the famed Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Kumasi, Ghana, to run joint international degree programmes. WU's collaboration with KNUST is under the auspices of the National Universities Commission (NUC), through its Pilot Scheme on Cross Border University Education.

This landmark achievement makes WU one of the first Nigerian universities that will be awarding joint international degrees. We give glory to our Lord!

WU and KNUST are committed to using the latest and the best in technology and teaching principles and methods to produce God-fearing world leaders in science, technology, business and the arts.

Company Details:
Wellspring University is a private university promoted by Management Science Centre and approved by the Federal Government. It operates on Christian ethics and principles.

The vision of the university is to mould the new Nigerian who will have the intellectual knowledge and moral strength for app...read morelying science and technology to the piloting of national development. 

In 1983, a group of academics and professionals came together in Lagos under the name, Management Science Centre, to render consultancy and training services to the teeming population of working men and women who had the common problem of inability to leave their employments to undertake full-time tertiary education.

The Centre commenced operations on a modest scale with the private coaching of students of the University of Lagos Correspondence and Open Studies Institute (COSIT), later renamed Distant Learning Institute (DLI).

By 1995, the modest foundation of 1983 had brought Management Science Centre into joint relationships with several institutions of higher learning in Nigeria, among which are the Auchi Polytechnic, Auchi, Edo State; University of Ibadan, Ibadan, Oyo State and Ambrose Alli University, Ekpoma, Edo State.

Our achievements in the programmes undertaken gave rise to a desire for expansion in order to contribute optimally to the development of education in Nigeria. The result was the establishment of Wisdom Gate High School in 2001 and Wellspring College in 2003, both secondary schools of international standard that placed great emphasis on moral upbringing. Then in 2006, the Centre established the Cornerstone College of Education in Lagos.

The motive of serving as a Centre of learning where Nigerian children, who are hungry for university education that is based on sound moral and spiritual principles, can accomplish their ambitions has always been the core of our vision. Thus, after more than twenty five years of serving the education sector, Management Science Centre considered itself strong enough to establish a full-fledged university.

To the glory of God, Wellspring University (WU) was licensed by the Federal Government of Nigeria in November 2009. WU is founded on Christian principles and ethics. WU is committed to providing quality education that will impact on the intellect and morals of its students.

The dream of the founders of WU is for it to become a world class institution, capable of delivering locally and globally relevant university education. This dream came to fruition in 2011 when WU joined the league of international universities offering cross border university education. In August 2011, WU signed an MOU with the famed Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Kumasi, Ghana, to run joint international degree programmes. WU's collaboration with KNUST is under the auspices of the National Universities Commission (NUC), through its Pilot Scheme on Cross Border University Education.

This landmark achievement makes WU one of the first Nigerian universities that will be awarding joint international degrees. We give glory to our Lord!

WU and KNUST are committed to using the latest and the best in technology and teaching principles and methods to produce God-fearing world leaders in science, technology, business and the arts.

Job Description:
Role purpose
The Procurement Manager will lead and coordinate end-to-end procurement for Alaro City and related business operations.
The role will cover direct procurement for development and construction requirements and indirect procurement for corporate and operational needs, ensuring timely, compliant and cost-effective sourcing while protecting quality, budget, programme and commercial value.
Working across projects, corporate and operational functions, the role will support procurement strategy, category management, pipeline planning, competitive tendering, supplier performance, commercial governance and disciplined contract administration throughout the business and project lifecycle.
Key responsibilities
Category management and sourcing: Manage categories and sourcing activities across direct and indirect spend, developing fit-for-purpose strategies that reflect business priorities, project requirements and market conditions.
Procurement planning and pipeline management: Develop and maintain procurement plans, category strategies, sourcing pipelines and delivery schedules aligned with approved budgets, programmes and operational priorities.
Supplier market research and prequalification: Research supplier markets and lead prequalification and engagement activities to identify capable, competitive, compliant and suitably resilient sources of supply.
RFP and RFQ preparation and issuance: Prepare and issue requests for proposals and requests for quotations, ensuring clear scopes, specifications, commercial requirements, submission instructions and evaluation criteria.
Tender evaluations and award recommendations: Coordinate technical and commercial evaluations, prepare tender comparisons and develop well-supported award recommendations for approval.
Commercial negotiations: Lead or support negotiations on pricing, terms, service levels, delivery, risk allocation and other commercial matters to secure sustainable value.
Contracts and purchase orders: Support the preparation, administration, renewal and close-out of contracts and purchase orders, maintaining clear records of commitments, variations, approvals and obligations.
Supplier performance: Establish and monitor supplier performance, service levels, delivery and quality, escalating issues and agreeing corrective actions where required.
Spend analysis and cost optimisation: Analyse spend, identify savings and value opportunities, and support cost optimisation, value engineering and alternative-sourcing initiatives across categories.
Governance and compliance: Maintain complete, accurate and auditable procurement records and ensure compliance with approved procedures, delegated authorities, contracts, warranties, guarantees and supplier documentation requirements.
Direct procurement:Manage sourcing for construction materials, infrastructure works, MEP, finishing packages, FF&E, landscaping, facilities and other project-related goods and services.
Indirect procurement: Manage sourcing for marketing and communications services, professional and advisory services, information and communications technology (ICT), software and licences, office and facilities services, travel and accommodation, recruitment and HR-related services, insurance, training, events, printing and branded materials, and other corporate services as required.
Stakeholder engagement: Work closely with project, corporate and operational stakeholders, including Construction & Delivery, Quantity Surveying, Design, Finance, Legal, Human Resources, Information Technology, Marketing and business support teams.
Pricing basis and issue resolution: Ensure that pricing is requested on a CIF basis to Alaro City FZC, Lagos, where relevant to imported or project procurement packages, and support the resolution of delivery, quality, customs, logistics and commercial issues.
Procurement categories
Direct / Project Procurement:
Construction and finishing materials, including waterproofing, gypsum boards and acoustic ceilings
Civil and infrastructure works
Mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) packages
Furniture, fixtures and equipment (FF&E)
Landscaping, facilities and operational services supporting projects
Other project-related goods, services and subcontract packages
Indirect / Corporate and Operational Procurement:
Marketing and communications services, printing and branded materials
Professional, advisory, legal and other corporate services
Information and communications technology (ICT), software and licences
Office and facilities services
Travel and accommodation
Recruitment, training and other HR-related services
Insurance, events and other corporate and operational requirements
Requirements

Advanced proficiency with Excel and hands-on experience with procurement systems.
Proven experience leading tendering processes, commercial negotiations, and contract administration.
Experience with procurement for imported or project packages using CIF pricing terms.
Strong track record of managing procurement stakeholders across Construction & Delivery, Quantity Surveying, Design, Finance, Legal, and senior business leadership.

Department: Technology & Secure Solutions
Job Purpose
The Electronic Security Manager is responsible for planning, designing, scheduling, and controlling all electronic security technology activities to meet the strategic objectives of G4S Nigeria and its diverse corporate, industrial, and diplomatic clients.
The role combines technical expertise, project management, and commercial acumen to deploy and maintain cutting-edge security systems (CCTV, Access Control, Intrusion Alarms, and Fire Systems) while managing engineering teams and vendor SLAs.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Planning & Technology Leadership
Drive Technology Strategy: Develop, implement, and manage the G4S Nigeria
Electronic Security Systems policy and roadmap in alignment with regional and global group standards.
Market Trends & Innovation: Continuously benchmark local offerings against international security trends, introducing innovative hardware/software solutions to the Nigerian market.
Budgetary Control: Prepare, submit, and manage the annual hardware, software, and departmental technology budgets. Analyze monthly financial variances and optimize cost efficiency.
Project Management & Solution Design
System Design: Oversee the technical design, configuration, and engineering drawings for scalable electronic security solutions (specifically for high-rise commercial offices, residential estates, financial hubs, and transit facilities).
Project Delivery: Actively manage a portfolio of active installations, ensuring projects are delivered on time, within scope, and on budget.
Quality Assurance: Guarantee the technical quality of all project deliverables while proactively managing risks associated with system integration.
Operations & Maintenance Management
SLA & Vendor Management: Draft, implement, and monitor Service Level Agreements (SLAs) with technology providers, OEMs, and local outsource partners.
Control Room & Core Infrastructure: Oversee the technical operational efficiency of the G4S Monitoring and Response Center (Control Room), ensuring seamless functionality of panic alarms, fleet tracking, and client CCTV feeds.
Disaster Recovery: Establish and maintain robust IT data security principles, backup systems, and a functional business continuity plan for all electronic infrastructure.
Client Relations & Business Development
Technical Consulting: Support the sales team by attending high-level client meetings to present technical proposals, perform security audits, and deliver risk assessments.
Customer Success: Act as the primary technical point of escalation for premium corporate clients to resolve critical system failures or performance gaps.
Team Leadership & Governance
Line Management: Supervise, mentor, and allocate tasks to field technicians, control room operators, and project engineers.
Training & Compliance: Enforce strict health, safety, and environmental (HSE) standards on-site. Identify skills gaps in the technical team and organize routine OEM certifications.

Percentage of projects delivered on time and within budget.
Client SLA compliance rate for system maintenance and error resolution.
Minimal system downtime within the G4S central monitoring infrastructure.
Departmental profitability and accurate alignment with the approved technical budget.
Qualifications And Experience
Education: Bachelor’s degree or Higher National Diploma (HND) in Electrical/Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.
Experience: Minimum of 5-8 years of progressive experience in Electronic Security Systems, with at least 3 years in a managerial or supervisory role within Nigeria or West Africa.
Technical Certifications: Professional certifications in world-class enterprise security systems are highly preferred (e.g., Lenel, Gallagher, Milestone, Honeywell, Bosch, or Cisco CCNA). Project Management certification (PMP or PRINCE2) is a strong advantage.
Industry Portfolio: Proven track record of managing electronic security rollouts for multi-site corporate environments, oil & gas facilities, or high-end residential estates.
Competencies & Technical Skills
Deep knowledge of IP networking, fiber optics, wireless transmission, and cybersecurity integration for physical security.
Strong ability to read, interpret, and modify architectural blueprints, electrical schematics, and CAD designs.
Exceptional negotiation, contract management, and vendor liaison skills.
High emotional intelligence with the ability to manage complex project stress and lead technical teams under pressure.
Fluency in English (written and verbal) with excellent presentation and technical report-writing skills.

Quality Control Inspection.

Occupational Health & Safety (OHS).

Good time management and organizational skills.

Safety-conscious approach to workshop activities.
Quality-focused mindset.

Job Description:
Role Overview
The Executive Director/CEO will serve as the chief executive and strategic leader of Open Health Foundation, providing overall direction for the organization’s programmes, operations, people, partnerships, finances, and institutional development.
The role will work closely with the Board and senior leadership team to develop and execute the Foundation’s strategic priorities, build strong relationships with donors, government institutions, development partners, private-sector organizations, healthcare stakeholders, and other strategic partners.
The Executive Director/CEO will also serve as a principal ambassador for the Foundation, representing its interests and mission at high-level meetings, conferences, policy forums, donor engagements, and other relevant platforms.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Leadership & Organizational Direction:
Provide visionary and effective leadership in alignment with the Foundation’s mission, values, and long-term objectives.
Develop, implement, and periodically review the Foundation’s strategic plan and organizational priorities.
Translate strategic objectives into clear annual operational plans, targets, budgets, and measurable outcomes.
Identify emerging opportunities, risks, and trends within the health and development sectors and position the Foundation accordingly.
Foster a culture of excellence, accountability, innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Ensure that the Foundation remains responsive to the evolving needs of the communities and populations it serves.
Programme Leadership & Impact:
Provide strategic oversight of all Foundation programmes, projects, and interventions.
Ensure programmes are evidence-based, impactful, scalable, and aligned with the Foundation’s strategic priorities.
Establish appropriate systems for monitoring, evaluation, learning, and impact measurement.
Review programme performance and ensure timely corrective action where required.
Promote innovation and the adoption of effective approaches to healthcare delivery and health-system strengthening.
Ensure programme activities comply with relevant regulatory, ethical, contractual, and donor requirements.
Fundraising & Resource Mobilization:
Lead the development and implementation of a sustainable resource-mobilization strategy.
Build and maintain strong relationships with institutional donors, foundations, development agencies, government institutions, corporate organizations, philanthropists, and other funding partners.
Identify and pursue strategic funding opportunities, grants, partnerships, and investment opportunities.
Provide leadership in the development of high-quality proposals, concept notes, funding strategies, and partnership opportunities.
Diversify the Foundation’s funding base and reduce dependence on a limited number of funding sources.
Represent the Foundation in high-level donor and funding discussions.
Strategic Partnerships & Stakeholder Engagement:
Develop and maintain strategic partnerships that advance the Foundation’s mission and programmes.
Build strong relationships with government ministries, departments and agencies, development partners, healthcare organizations, academic institutions, NGOs, private-sector organizations, and community stakeholders.
Represent the Foundation at national and international conferences, policy engagements, sector meetings, and other strategic forums.
Identify opportunities for collaboration, co-investment, knowledge exchange, and programme expansion.
Position Open Health Foundation as a credible and respected organization within the health and development ecosystem.
Governance, Compliance & Risk Management:
Work closely with the Board to ensure effective organizational governance and accountability.
Provide the Board with accurate, timely, and strategic information to support informed decision-making.
Ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations, donor requirements, organizational policies, and governance standards.
Identify, assess, and manage organizational, financial, operational, reputational, and programme risks.
Maintain appropriate internal controls and accountability mechanisms.
Promote transparency and ethical conduct across the organization.
Financial & Operational Management:
Provide executive oversight of the Foundation’s financial sustainability and operational performance.
Work with the finance team and Board to develop and manage annual budgets and financial plans.
Ensure responsible stewardship of organizational and donor resources.
Monitor organizational financial performance and take appropriate action where necessary.
Ensure effective systems, processes, policies, and structures are in place to support organizational growth.
Oversee organizational efficiency and ensure resources are aligned with strategic priorities.
People & Leadership Development:
Provide strong leadership to the senior management team and promote effective cross-functional collaboration.
Build and retain a high-performing, diverse, and mission-driven workforce.
Establish clear performance expectations and accountability mechanisms for senior leadership.
Support staff development, succession planning, and leadership capacity building.
Promote a positive organizational culture built on professionalism, integrity, inclusion, accountability, and respect.
Ensure that the Foundation attracts and retains high-calibre talent.
Advocacy, Visibility & Thought Leadership:
Serve as a public ambassador and leading voice for Open Health Foundation.
Develop and strengthen the Foundation’s institutional profile and visibility within the health sector.
Contribute to health policy discussions, sector advocacy, and thought leadership initiatives.
Represent the Foundation in media engagements and public forums where appropriate.
Promote the Foundation’s achievements, evidence, lessons learned, and impact responsibly.
Monitoring, Reporting & Accountability:
Ensure the timely preparation and presentation of organizational, programme, financial, and strategic reports.
Track progress against organizational goals, key performance indicators, and strategic targets.
Provide regular performance updates to the Board and other relevant stakeholders.
Use data, evidence, and organizational learning to inform strategic decision-making.
Ensure accountability to beneficiaries, partners, donors, regulators, and the Board.
Key Performance Indicators
The successful Executive Director/CEOwill be expected to demonstrate measurable performance across areas including:
Achievement of the Foundation’s strategic objectives and annual targets.
Growth and diversification of funding and resource mobilization.
Quality, reach, and measurable impact of programmes.
Development and sustainability of strategic partnerships.
Financial sustainability and responsible resource management.
Organizational growth, efficiency, and institutional strengthening.
Staff engagement, retention, and leadership development.
Governance, compliance, and risk management.
Increased institutional visibility and sector influence.
Satisfaction and confidence of key stakeholders, partners, and the Board.
Qualifications & Experience
Essential
A Bachelor’s Degree in Public Health, Medicine, Health Sciences, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Business Administration, Management, or a related discipline.
A Master’s degree or relevant postgraduate qualification is highly desirable.
Minimum of 7years of progressive professional experience, with at least 3years in a senior management, executive, or organizational leadership position.
Demonstrated experience leading a nonprofit, foundation, NGO, development organization, healthcare organization, or comparable institution.
Proven experience in strategic planning, organizational leadership, programme management, and stakeholder engagement.
Demonstrable experience in fundraising, grant acquisition, donor management, and resource mobilization.
Strong understanding of the health, development, nonprofit, or social-impact ecosystem.
Demonstrated experience managing multidisciplinary teams and complex organizational operations.
Strong financial management, budgeting, and organizational oversight capabilities.
Excellent written, verbal, presentation, negotiation, and relationship-management skills.
Desirable:
Experience working with international development agencies, foundations, bilateral or multilateral organizations, or major institutional donors.
Experience working with government and public-sector stakeholders.
Experience in health systems strengthening, healthcare access, community health, public health, or related areas.
Experience developing and managing large-scale grants and multi-stakeholder programmes.
Professional membership or certification in a relevant field.
Experience serving on boards, committees, advisory groups, or sector-level initiatives.
Core Competencies:
The ideal candidate will demonstrate:
Visionary and strategic leadership
Exceptional stakeholder management
Fundraising and business development acumen
Strong understanding of the health and development sector
High-level communication and public speaking skills
Financial and commercial awareness
Strong governance and ethical judgement
Programme and project oversight
Negotiation and partnership-building skills
People leadership and talent development
Problem-solving and sound decision-making
Adaptability and innovation
High integrity, professionalism, and accountability
Commitment to equity, inclusion, and sustainable health impact
Leadership Profile:
We are looking for a leader who is strategic without losing sight of execution, commercially astute without compromising the Foundation’s social mission, and ambitious while remaining accountable to the communities it serves.
The ideal candidate should be able to move confidently between Board-level strategy, donor and government engagement, programme oversight, financial stewardship, and people leadership.
They should possess the credibility and relationship-building ability to establish Open Health Foundation as a trusted partner while creating the systems, culture, and resources required for long-term institutional sustainability.

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) will provide strategic financial leadership across Incel Group, ensuring sound financial management, effective internal controls, regulatory compliance, financial sustainability and informed business decision-making.
The CFO will oversee the Group's financial planning, accounting, treasury, budgeting, reporting, taxation, financial controls, risk management and investment-related financial activities.
The role will also serve as a key strategic adviser to Executive Management, providing timely financial insights to support growth, profitability, operational efficiency and long-term organisational sustainability.
Key Responsibilities
Financial Strategy & Leadership:
Develop and execute the Group's financial strategy in alignment with corporate objectives.
Provide strategic financial advice to the Executive Management and Board.
Lead financial planning, forecasting and long-term financial modelling.
Evaluate the financial implications of new business opportunities, investments and expansion initiatives.
Provide financial insights to support strategic and operational decision-making.
Financial Planning, Budgeting & Performance:
Lead the annual budgeting and periodic forecasting processes.
Monitor actual performance against approved budgets and financial targets.
Analyse revenue, expenditure, margins, cash flow and profitability across business units.
Develop and monitor financial KPIs and management dashboards.
Identify cost optimisation and revenue enhancement opportunities.
Provide regular management reports on financial performance.

Ensure accurate and timely preparation of management accounts and statutory financial statements.
Ensure proper maintenance of accounting records across the Group.
Oversee month-end, quarter-end and year-end financial closing processes.
Ensure appropriate reconciliation of bank accounts, receivables, payables and other balance sheet accounts.
Strengthen financial reporting standards, procedures and controls across all business units.

Provide strategic oversight of cash flow management and liquidity.
Monitor the Group's banking relationships and financing arrangements.
Ensure effective management of currency exposures and international payments.
Establish appropriate controls over cash, bank transactions and payment approvals.
Ensure timely settlement of critical business obligations and financial commitments.
Internal Controls, Risk & Compliance:
Establish and maintain robust financial controls across the Group.
Work closely with Internal Control, Internal Audit, HR, Operations and other functions to strengthen governance.
Identify financial, operational and compliance risks and recommend appropriate mitigation measures.
Ensure compliance with applicable Nigerian tax, financial reporting, regulatory and corporate requirements.
Support the continuous improvement of financial processes in line with the Company's QMS and governance framework.

Ensure timely and accurate tax filings and payments.
Liaise with tax advisers, auditors and relevant regulatory authorities where required.

Ensure timely resolution of audit findings and implementation of agreed recommendations.
Provide financial information and analysis required for Management and Board meetings.
Maintain appropriate documentation and financial records to support transparency and accountability.

Partner with business unit heads to improve financial performance and accountability.
Evaluate pricing, margins, contracts and commercial arrangements.
Provide financial analysis for new services, projects and business expansion.
Promote financial awareness and accountability across the organisation.
Challenge financial assumptions constructively and provide evidence-based recommendations to Management.
Team Leadership & Development:
Lead, develop and manage the Finance & Accounts function.
Establish clear performance objectives and accountability within the Finance team.
Build the team's technical capabilities and promote continuous professional development.
Foster collaboration between Finance and other departments.

Accuracy and timeliness of financial reporting.
Budget achievement and variance management.
Cash-flow and liquidity management.
Revenue and profitability performance.
Reduction of avoidable financial costs and leakages.
Timeliness of statutory and tax compliance.
Audit outcomes and closure of audit findings.
Effectiveness of financial controls.
Working-capital and receivables management.
Quality and timeliness of management financial information.
Finance team productivity and capability development.
Contribution to strategic business growth and financial sustainability.

Demonstrated experience managing Finance & Accounts at a senior/executive level.
Desirable:
MBA, MSc Finance, or another relevant postgraduate qualification.
Experience within a diversified group, tourism/travel, trading, investment, hospitality or other service-oriented business.
Experience managing multi-entity or international financial operations.
Strong knowledge of Nigerian taxation, financial reporting and corporate compliance.

Strategic financial leadership.
Strong commercial and business acumen.
Advanced financial analysis and modelling.
Budgeting and forecasting expertise.
