Job Description:
Purpose of the Role
The Head of Primary will lead the design, launch and ongoing management of Brighthouse Academy's Primary section. This is a start-up leadership role: the successful candidate will build the curriculum, systems, culture and team from an early stage, rather than inherit an existing operation. The role combines academic leadership, people leadership, and hands-on administrative and financial-administration responsibility.
Key Responsibilities
Curriculum Design & Educational Leadership
Design and set up the Primary section's structure (classes, streams, timetable, academic calendar) from scratch.
Develop an original, locally-grounded mixed curriculum — not an unmodified 'out of the box' import — that blends best practice from national/international frameworks with Kogi State and Nigerian local content, culture, and context.
Build variety and creativity into curriculum delivery: project-based learning, local-content modules, literacy and numeracy foundations, and enrichment activities.
Set and monitor academic standards, schemes of work, and assessment frameworks across all Primary year groups.
Continuously review and improve curriculum and pedagogy based on learner outcomes and community context.
People Leadership & Capacity Building
Join in the recruitment, induction, and training of Primary teaching and support staff.
Supervise and manage the performance of Primary teaching and support staff.
Design and deliver ongoing teacher training and professional development, particularly in curriculum delivery methods that are new to staff.
Coach, mentor and inspire teachers to adopt creative, learner-centred teaching practices.
Model strong classroom practice and lead by example in teaching quality.
Build a positive, high-expectation, child-safe school culture within the Primary section.
Operations, Administration & Resource Management
Oversee day-to-day administration of the Primary section: pupil records, attendance, timetabling, reporting to parents/guardians.
Manage basic financial administration for the section — budgeting input, expenditure tracking, procurement requests, and accountability for funds/resources allocated, in line with Brighthouse Academy's non-profit financial policies.
Manage school assets relevant to the Primary section (furniture, learning materials, equipment) — maintaining inventories and ensuring proper use and upkeep.
Ensure compliance with relevant Nigerian basic-education regulations and Kogi State education requirements.
Community & Stakeholder Engagement
Act as the main point of contact for Primary parents/guardians and the local community.
Represent the Primary section to the Head of School, Board/Trustees, donors and external partners as required.
Build relationships with the local community to source and validate local content for the curriculum.
Person Specification
Essential
B.Ed (Primary Education), B.A/B.Sc + PGDE, or equivalent; a Master's degree is gives you a high advantage.
TRCN certificate if required; additional certifications give you an added advantage.
Proven experience setting up or launching a school, department or section from the ground up.
Demonstrated curriculum development experience, including incorporating local/community content into formal curricula.
Strong record as a school leader/manager — staff supervision, performance management, and team development.
Working knowledge of basic financial administration (budgeting, expenditure tracking, accountability) and asset management.
Experience training, coaching and developing teachers.
Excellent administrative and organisational skills.
Genuine commitment to inclusive, tuition-free, community-focused education.
A recognized teaching qualification and relevant experience at primary level.
Desirable
Experience working within a non-profit or NGO-run school.
Familiarity with Nigerian basic education standards and Kogi State education context.
Postgraduate qualification in education leadership/management, curriculum studies, or related field.
Experience designing original teaching materials rather than relying on standard published schemes.

Main Purpose of the job

The role is responsible for translating the agreed demand plan into detailed supply and production requirements, identifying risks and constraints early, and driving cross-functional actions to ensure high customer service while optimizing inventory and working capital.
The Supply Planning Executive will work closely with Demand Planning, Manufacturing, Procurement, Logistics, Sales, Finance and Customer Service to ensure end-to-end supply continuity across Godrej Nigeria's portfolio.

Drive reduction of excess and obsolete inventory.

Experience working with Sales and Marketing to incorporate commercial intelligence, promotions, launches and market events into the demand plan.
Experience participating in S&OP/IBP and consensus demand planning processes.
Experience analysing demand deviations and converting learning into forecast improvements.
Experience working with ERP/demand planning systems and large datasetsKey Responsiblities
Skills & Competencies
Technical Skills:
Strong knowledge of demand planning, forecasting, statistical forecasting and demand management principles.
Strong understanding of FMCG demand drivers including seasonality, promotions, pricing, distribution, product lifecycle and customer behaviour.
Proficiency in ERP/Demand Planning systems (e.g. SAP) and advanced Excel.
Experience with data analytics, forecasting and reporting tools, preferably Power BI or equivalent.
Understanding of Demand Plan Accuracy, Forecast Bias, Forecast Value Added and forecast error analysis.
Understanding of IBP/S&OP, Consensus Demand Planning and cross-functional alignment processes.
Soft Skills:
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Effective communication and collaboration skills.
Ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
Attention to detail and proactive decision-making.
To develop and maintain an accurate, unbiased and commercially realistic demand plan for the assigned portfolio by combining statistical forecasting with customer, consumer, market and commercial insights.
The role is responsible for translating market and business intelligence into a reliable demand signal, driving consensus across Sales, Marketing, Finance and Supply Chain, and proactively identifying and managing demand risks and exceptions.
The role will contribute to the IBP/S&OP process and continuously improve forecast accuracy, forecast stability and value-added planning across the business.
Maintain Data and Systems
Create and maintain the appropriate master data in the planning systems in use, minimising errors, and avoiding duplication and obsolescence.
Maintain system hygiene and health to ensure demand signals are not polluted, in close collaboration with Customer Services.
Collate Information and Assumptions
Ensure commitment from all functions, build and maintain good communication and collaboration both within Supply Chain and with Sales and Marketing, Manufacturing and Finance, according to the Integrated Business Planning (IBP) best practices.
Capture, prioritize, analyze and input Marketing and Sales events; customer, consumer & competitor information; other external / internal trends and influences which impact demand.
Manage Portfolio and Lifecycle
Effectively use all Demand Planning system functionality to enable an exception based management approach.
Maintain the systems to reflect the lifecycle of products (predecessors, successors, temporary promotional variants.
Collaborate with Marketing and Sales by providing input on a regular basis regarding product launches, portfolio optimization, rationale of commercial decisions, promotions and customer behavior.
Develop and Maintain the Forecast
Use appropriate statistical models and parameters, and enrich statistical forecasts to generate accurate base demand forecasts.
Generate and maintain a demand plan for a given portfolio of products, locations and/or customers, at the levels (product hierarchy and time) at which business decisions are taken.
Focus on and deliver a stable demand plan, but taking into account appropriately recent events, along with achievement of Demand Plan Accuracy (DPA), controlled variability of accuracy and no systematic bias.
Ensure that business planning is operated at the correct level of aggregation (product hierarchy and time).
Reach Consensus through Alignment
Contribute to cross functional planning activities such as IBP and the Consesus Demand Planning Framework (CDP) according to Best Practice.
Contribute to Customer Facing activities such as Collaborative Planning, Promotional Forecasting, ad hoc joint Supply Chain improvement projects as appropriate.
Share and Publish the Forecast
Through systematic reporting, provision of links or ad-hoc reports and communications, ensure that Demand Plan information is available to internal business partners as required.
Cascade knowledge of Best Practices and tools to other Demand Planners.
Track and Manage Demand
Actively follow-up actual sales to customers and sell-out (POS) data to identify exceptional or unforecasted activities.
Drive fast, appropriate actions to minimize the impact of deviations from the Demand Plan. Communicate these actions to stakeholders.

Strong analytical skills to adequately anticipate demand and make investment decisions

Job Description:
Location: Ede, Osun
Reports To: Head Accountant
Position Type: Contract, renewable annually
About the Programme
STRIDE (Scientific Training and Research in Infectious Disease Genomics and Entrepreneurship) is a six-year, pan-African workforce development program designed to strengthen Africa’s health systems by building a new generation of genomics and bioinformatics professionals.
Led by the Institute of Genomics and Global Health (IGH) at Redeemer’s University in partnership with the University of Cape Town, University of Yaoundé I, and Villgro Africa, STRIDE aims to train and equip approximately 5,100 young African scientists and health professionals to transition into dignified, sustainable careers across disease surveillance, research, diagnostics, and biotech innovation.
The program addresses Africa’s critical shortage of genomics expertise through three integrated pathways: internationally accredited MSc and PhD training with guaranteed professional placements, intensive skills and upskilling programs for early- and mid-career professionals, and bioentrepreneurship education supporting the development of locally driven health innovations.
By strengthening faculty capacity at emerging universities and building employment pipelines with national public health institutions, STRIDE contributes to an Africa-led genomics ecosystem that advances health sovereignty, innovation, and improved health outcomes across the continent.
About the Job
STRIDE is seeking an experienced Accounting Officer to manage day-to-day financial operations, ensuring accurate tracking, reporting, and compliance of program expenditures across this multi-country initiative.
The Accounting Officer will work closely with IGH’s Head Accountant, STRIDE program staff, and partners to maintain financial records, process expenses, and prepare reports that meet organisational and donor requirements.
This role is central to maintaining transparency, accountability, and effective resource management, enabling STRIDE to deliver on its objectives in workforce development, institutional capacity strengthening, and the growth of an Africa-led genomics and surveillance ecosystem.
Key Responsibilities
Maintain accurate and up-to-date financial records for the STRIDE program, including expense tracking, ledger entries, and reconciliations.
Process and record approved program expenditures in compliance with organisational policies, donor regulations, and accounting standards.
Prepare regular financial reports, summaries, and analyses for internal management, the Head Accountant, and donor reporting requirements.
Monitor budgets, flag discrepancies, and provide timely updates on actual versus planned expenditures.
Assist in preparing financial documentation and supporting materials for audits and donor reviews.
Coordinate with program staff to ensure proper documentation, approvals, and classification of expenses.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
3–5 years of professional experience in accounting, preferably in NGOs, research programs, or donor-funded projects.
Strong knowledge of accounting principles, financial reporting, and budget monitoring.
Experience with ERP/Accounting software and Microsoft Excel.
Familiarity with donor financial rules and regulations, particularly those of international foundations, development agencies, and research funders, is an advantage.
Preferred Skills:
Attention to detail and strong organisational skills to manage multiple tasks and deadlines independently.
Ability to analyse financial data and produce clear, accurate reports.
Strong communication skills for liaising with program staff, finance team members, and external stakeholders.
Integrity, discretion, and adherence to ethical financial practices.
Proactive problem-solving skills and ability to suggest process improvements.
Familiarity with multi-country or multi-partner program finance is an advantage.

Company Address: Cedarcrest Hospitals Abuja, Plot 195 Apo Dutse Road Off Oladipo Diya Way, Gudu District, Abuja.
Company Details:
Cedarcrest Hospitals / Cedarcrest Orthopaedic Clinics Ltd is a modern specialist medical care centre located in the heart of Abuja, Nigeria’s blossoming capital. It was established in January 2008 with the aim of providing a high standard of local healthcare that is comparable with what obtain...read mores in other more developed parts of the world.
The centre started off as a highly specialized orthopaedic facility, registered as Cedarcrest Orthopaedic Clinics Ltd. Before long, it became obvious that other specialties had to be incorporated partly due to the success of the centre and partly due to the lack of local specialist services in those specialties that relate directly with orthopaedic and trauma surgery.
Its core specialty areas have now been expanded to include neuro/spine surgery, plastic/reconstructive surgery and dermatology. Thus was Cedarcrest Hospitals born in early 2009. The hospital also renders non-core specialist services covering internal medicine, obstetrics and gynaecology, radiology, rheumatology, ear nose and throat surgery, dietetics, physiotherapy and general practice.
These key specialists are supported by highly trained and courteous doctors, nurses, imaging scientists, laboratory scientists, administrative and ancillary staff who strive to make patients’ experience at Cedarcrest is as pleasant as possible. We work in liaison with centres in the United Kingdom and the United States and frequently have visiting surgeons from these foreign hospitals, as well as sending patients to these centres where specific facilities for their care are not optimal here.
We are also supported by a wide range of related specialties and specialist services. With adequate facilities and highly skilled manpower, Cedarcrest Hospitals has over several years, provided specialized treatment to a large number of patients from the federal capital and the rest of Nigeria. This has made it possible for patients to get timely highly specialized surgical treatment without the need to travel abroad.

Job Description:
What this looks like in practice:
You work with the financial records. You process or review transactions, invoices, bills, postings, and other accounting information, and ensure the records are properly maintained.
You reconcile the figures. You perform bank and other relevant reconciliations, investigate differences, and follow through on outstanding items.
You check the work. You run preliminary checks on client financial information, including trial balances, reconciliations, and previous correction directives, and flag anything that requires further attention.
You support month-end close. You assist with accruals, prepayments, and other required month-end entries and prepare the schedules and supporting information needed for the close.
You support tax and payroll work. You prepare tax computations and draft VAT, WHT, PAYE, and other relevant statutory work from the available information for further review. Where applicable, you also support payroll checks, including PAYE, pension, and other statutory deductions.
You maintain engagement records. You keep engagement trackers and workpapers updated on Zoho Projects.
You investigate discrepancies. When figures do not agree, or something looks unusual, you look into the underlying records, identify what is causing the issue where possible, and provide the relevant information for further review.
You follow things through. You track previous correction directives, follow up on missing documents and information, and make sure outstanding items do not get lost.
You work across teams. You communicate with associates, other finance team members, clients, and other relevant teams to obtain information, clarify issues, resolve outstanding items, and keep work moving.
You improve as you go. You apply feedback to your work, build your accounting and analytical skills, and improve the standard, accuracy, and independence of your work over time.
What Good Looks Like After 3–6 Months
At this stage, we are not expecting you to know everything or be fully proficient in every part of the role. We expect to see clear progress from where you started and a stronger understanding of how the firm's work is done.
You understand the firm's systems, processes, and expectations for client work.
You are becoming more confident and consistent with financial checks, and reconciliations.
You can identify common discrepancies, understand when further investigation is needed, and know when to seek guidance.
You have developed a stronger working understanding of the tax, payroll, and statutory requirements relevant to your work.
You understand how correction directives and outstanding items are tracked and followed through.
You communicate effectively across teams and with clients when requesting information, clarifying issues, or following up on outstanding work.
You are applying feedback and showing improvement in the accuracy, organization, and overall standard of your work.
You are becoming more confident with the accounting systems, Excel/Google Sheets, and other tools required for your work.
Requirements
A Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
1–2 years of relevant practical accounting experience.
Basic working knowledge of tax and statutory requirements, including VAT, WHT, PAYE, and related deductions.
Ability to work with financial information, identify discrepancies, and investigate issues within your level of responsibility.
Good knowledge of Excel or Google Sheets.
Basic knowledge of accounting software. Zoho Books or QuickBooks experience is an advantage.
Careful and accurate in your own work, with the ability to notice when something in the records does not look right.
Able to organize your work, manage several tasks, and follow through on outstanding items.
Able to communicate clearly and professionally across teams and with clients.
Willing to learn, receive feedback, ask questions when necessary, and improve the standard of your work.

.

Proper organization, completeness, and availability of financial documentation for audits and reviews.

1–3 years of relevant experience
in accounting, finance, or related functions.

Good understanding of basic accounting principles, financial reporting, and bookkeeping practices.
Basic knowledge of bank reconciliation, invoice processing, and payroll processes.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities.
Proficiency in accounting software, Microsoft Excel, and other financial management tools.
Strong attention to detail and accuracy, particularly when handling financial information and documentation.
Effective communication and reporting skills.
Ability to collaborate, coordinate, and work effectively with team members.
High level of integrity, accountability, and confidentiality when handling financial information.

Track and oversee the preparation of visiting missions/trips to the country

Master’s degree, in finance, business administration, management, economics, or a similar field.

Job Description:
About the Role
We are hiring Marketing Officers to own marketing for an assigned cluster of our stores, on the ground and online. You will be the face of our brand in your territory: running promotions and activations, keeping our products beautifully presented, partnering with our content team, and bringing back the customer and market insight that shapes what we do next.
You will spend most of your working days in stores, so you must live within easy reach of your assigned cluster.
What You Will Do
Own your territory: Visit your branches regularly, build strong relationships with branch teams, and spot opportunities and gaps before anyone asks.
Run promotions and activations: Plan and execute in-store promotions, seasonal campaigns, product sampling, and makeup demo days. Make sure banners, flyers, shelf talkers, and other campaign materials are produced, delivered, and displayed correctly and on time.
Keep our products visible and irresistible: Monitor displays, shelf presentation, and branding standards across your stores. Flag slow movers that need repositioning or a promotional push, and make sure new launches get prime placement and attention.
Take the brand into the community: Represent Kuddy at local events, markets, salons, and beauty schools in your territory. Build relationships with makeup artists and beauty professionals who can champion our products, and find local partnership opportunities that bring new customers through our doors.
Co-create content and campaign ideas: Work closely with our content creators, designers, and photographers. Spot the moments worth capturing in your stores, from a new launch to a loyal customer’s story, line up products and people for shoots, and bring your own ideas for campaigns, promos, and content to the table. We expect you to contribute ideas, not just execute instructions.
Support our digital channels: Assist with social media, email, and WhatsApp marketing, help push your territory’s promos online, and keep brand messaging consistent between our shelves and our screens.
Bring back insight: Track what is selling and what is sitting, gather customer feedback, watch competitor pricing and promotions in your area, and share what you learn so the team plans with real information.
Who Fits
1 - 3 years’ experience in marketing, retail, field marketing, digital marketing, or brand activation.
Degree in a related field.
Organized, proactive, and strong on follow-through
Comfortable on the move between stores and talking directly with customers
Full of ideas and confident enough to share them
Good eye for product presentation, beauty trends, and what makes a display sell
Working knowledge of social media and basic digital marketing tools
Genuine passion for makeup, beauty, and retail

Job Summary

Strong knowledge of IFRS and Nigerian accounting/tax regulations.

Job Description:
Job Summary
We are seeking an experienced, independent, and highly analytical Chief Internal Auditor to lead the hotel’s internal audit function and provide objective assurance on financial, operational, and internal control processes.
The Chief Internal Auditor will be responsible for reviewing the effectiveness of financial and operational controls, safeguarding hotel assets, identifying financial and operational risks, detecting irregularities, and ensuring compliance with approved policies and procedures.
The role will cover key hotel operations including revenue, cash management, procurement, inventory, payroll, Food & Beverage, Front Office, stores, fixed assets, and general administration.
The successful candidate will work closely with management while maintaining sufficient independence to objectively review and report on the hotel’s operations and control environment.
Key Responsibilities
Internal Audit Planning & Leadership:
Develop and implement a risk-based internal audit programme for the hotel.
Lead and supervise the internal audit function and audit activities.
Conduct periodic reviews of financial, operational, and administrative processes.
Identify key business and operational risks and recommend appropriate controls.
Ensure audit activities are conducted objectively, professionally, and in accordance with approved procedures.
Financial & Revenue Audit:
Review daily hotel revenue generated from rooms, Food & Beverage, events, banquets, and other income streams.
Audit daily revenue reports from the Front Office, POS, PMS, restaurant, bar, and other revenue centres.
Verify that all sales are properly recorded and accounted for.
Review discounts, complimentary services, refunds, voids, allowances, and adjustments for proper authorization.
Perform revenue reconciliations between PMS, POS, cash collections, bank settlements, and accounting records.
Investigate unexplained revenue variances and report findings to management.
Cash & Banking Controls:
Review daily cash collections, deposits, cash counts, and banking records.
Conduct surprise cash counts where necessary.
Verify cashiers’ reports and identify shortages, overages, or irregular transactions.
Review bank reconciliations and investigate unusual or outstanding items.
Assess the effectiveness of cash-handling and cash-security procedures.
Procurement & Expenditure Audit:
Review purchasing activities to ensure compliance with approved procurement procedures.
Examine purchase requisitions, purchase orders, quotations, invoices, delivery notes, and payment documentation.
Verify that purchases are properly authorized and supported by appropriate documentation.
Review supplier transactions for unusual pricing, duplicate payments, conflicts of interest, or other irregularities.
Assess expenditure controls and identify opportunities to reduce unnecessary costs and losses.
Inventory & Stores Audit:
Conduct periodic and surprise audits of food, beverages, housekeeping supplies, engineering materials, and general hotel inventory.
Review stock receipts, issues, transfers, adjustments, and wastage.
Reconcile physical stock counts with inventory records.
Investigate stock variances, shortages, excessive wastage, and unexplained losses.
Review controls over high-value and sensitive items.
Recommend improvements to stores and inventory management procedures.
Food & Beverage Audit:
Review restaurant, bar, banquet, room service, and other Food & Beverage transactions.
Verify food and beverage sales against POS records and stock consumption.
Review portion control, wastage, complimentary items, discounts, and staff meals.
Conduct periodic checks on beverage and kitchen inventory.
Investigate unusual variances between purchases, consumption, production, and sales.
Payroll & Staff Cost Audit:
Review payroll records to ensure payments are made only to authorized employees.
Verify new employees, resignations, promotions, salary adjustments, allowances, overtime, and deductions.
Identify duplicate, inactive, unauthorized, or unusual payroll entries.
Reconcile payroll records with approved staff lists and attendance records.
Review controls over staff advances, loans, and other employee-related payments.
Asset Protection & Fixed Asset Audit:
Review controls over hotel property, equipment, furniture, vehicles, and other fixed assets.
Conduct periodic physical verification of fixed assets.
Review asset registers and investigate missing, damaged, or unrecorded assets.
Ensure disposals and transfers are properly authorized and documented.
Recommend measures to reduce theft, misuse, damage, and loss of hotel assets.
Compliance & Policy Review:
Assess compliance with hotel policies, financial procedures, approval limits, and operating standards.
Review compliance with applicable statutory and regulatory requirements.
Identify control weaknesses and instances of non-compliance.
Recommend corrective actions and monitor implementation.
Keep management informed of significant compliance and control risks.
Fraud & Irregularity Investigation:
Investigate suspected fraud, theft, financial irregularities, unauthorized transactions, and control breaches when assigned.
Review supporting documentation and relevant transaction records.
Analyze available CCTV, POS, PMS, accounting, inventory, and other records where appropriate and authorized.
Maintain confidentiality throughout investigations.
Prepare clear investigation reports and communicate significant findings to authorized management.
Internal Control Improvement:
Evaluate the adequacy and effectiveness of existing internal controls.
Identify control gaps, weaknesses, duplication of processes, and potential areas of financial leakage.
Recommend practical measures to strengthen controls and improve operational efficiency.
Follow up on previously identified audit issues to confirm that corrective actions have been implemented.
Audit Reporting & Management Advisory:
Prepare clear, accurate, and timely internal audit reports.
Present significant audit findings and recommendations to the General Manager and relevant management personnel.
Highlight material risks, control weaknesses, financial exposures, and areas requiring immediate attention.
Maintain proper audit working papers and supporting documentation.
Provide advisory input on new processes, systems, policies, and business initiatives where appropriate without compromising audit independence.
Qualifications & Experience
Bachelor’s degree or HND in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
Professional accounting or internal audit qualification such as ACA, ACCA, ANAN, CIA, or equivalent is strongly preferred.
4–7years of relevant experience in internal audit, external audit, financial control, or risk management.
Previous experience in a hotel, hospitality group, restaurant, corporate organization, or similar environment is an advantage.
Strong knowledge of accounting principles, internal controls, audit procedures, and financial reporting.
Experience auditing hotel revenue, cash, inventory, procurement, payroll, and operational processes is highly desirable.
Good knowledge of Nigerian tax, statutory, regulatory, and financial control requirements.
Experience with accounting software, hotel PMS, POS systems, and Microsoft Excel.
Demonstrable experience preparing audit reports and presenting findings to senior management.
Required Skills & Competencies:
Strong knowledge of internal auditing and internal control systems.
Excellent accounting and financial analysis skills.
Strong understanding of hotel revenue and operational controls.
Good knowledge of audit methodologies and risk-based auditing.
Strong analytical and investigative skills.
Excellent knowledge of Microsoft Excel and accounting systems.
Familiarity with hotel PMS and POS systems.
Strong report-writing and presentation skills.
Excellent attention to detail.
Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
Ability to identify financial leakages and control weaknesses.
Strong knowledge of inventory, procurement, payroll, and cash controls.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Ability to maintain confidentiality.
Strong leadership and team-management skills.
Ability to work independently and objectively.

Your job is to turn what already sells into complete, cohesive collections, and to design the pieces that are missing. That means reading our bestseller data, spotting the gaps (a heart necklace with no matching stud, a collection with no classic base chains), and designing the pieces that fill them, down to the millimeter, in CAD that a supplier can turn into a mold.
It also means styling. You will build necklace, bracelet, ring and earring stacks from our existing catalogue and your new designs, photograph them with the Co-Founder (you will both be the mannequin at times), and make sure every combination looks right with the ÌTURA wardrobe.
This is an execution role with real ownership. Nobody will chase you. You will be the one chasing the Co-Founder to get decisions made, samples reviewed and suppliers briefed. We are hiring someone who wants to own the design pipeline, not someone who wants to be handed a brief.
What You'll Own
Original Piece Design and CAD:
Design new pieces that complement our top 20 to 50 bestsellers, so each bestseller becomes a complete set (necklace, studs, bracelet, ring where it makes sense)
Produce production-ready CAD files (MatrixGold preferred; Rhino, Blender or equivalent accepted as long as the output is a manufacturable file) with every dimension specified in millimeters
Design the classic base pieces the collection is missing: bare chains (rolo, paperclip, satellite, curb, Figaro, box, cable), classic studs and huggies that anchor a stack
Work within our materials system: 316L stainless steel, sterling silver and 18k gold vermeil, moissanite and lab stones, gemstones and freshwater pearls
Supplier Spec Sheets and Sample Review:
Write the technical spec sheet for every new design: dimensions, metal, plating thickness, stone type and cut, findings, finish, tolerances, target unit cost and MOQ
Brief our existing suppliers (all of whom do customization), get mold fee, unit cost and lead-time quotes, and compare them
Review samples against the spec, log defects and drive corrections until the piece is right
Collection Cohesiveness and Stacks:
Build and document necklace, bracelet, ring and earring stacks from existing pieces and new designs, with layer lengths and sizing so they can be reproduced for photography and for customers
Build full combinations (necklace stack plus bracelet stack plus earring stack plus ring stack) that work with the ÌTURA wardrobe and stylescape
Own the men's stack: define what the ÌTURA man wears and which pieces are missing
Collection Planning and Trend Research:
Maintain the design pipeline in Notion: what is being designed, why (which bestseller it serves), where it is with suppliers, and what it will cost
Track competitor collections and the stacking trends our customers are already following, and translate them into pieces that fit ÌTURA
Recommend what to design next, backed by what is selling
What Success Looks Like
Every top-20 bestseller has a designed set around it, with CAD, spec sheets and supplier quotes
The collection has the classic base chains and studs it is missing today, in production
Necklace, bracelet, ring and earring stacks are documented and photographed, and customers can buy a stack that works
The men's collection has a clear stacking logic and the pieces to support it
The Co-Founder is reviewing your designs and approving suppliers, not drawing or chasing
Suppliers receive spec sheets they can manufacture from without a second round of questions
Who You'll Work With
You will report directly to Kanma, Co-Founder, and work alongside her every day.
You will work closely with:
Paul, Co-Founder (marketing, ads, website, best-seller data)
Procurement and Inventory (purchase orders, supplier relationships, stock)
Head of Content and the content team (product photography, styling content, launch assets)
Who You Are
You are a jewelry designer who loves the technical side as much as the creative side, and who has taken a design from sketch to CAD to sample to production before.
You are likely someone who:
Has designed jewelry professionally and can show CAD work with real dimensions
Understands how a piece is actually made: casting, stone setting, plating, chain construction, findings
Thinks in sets and stacks, not single pieces
Reads sales data and lets it shape what you design, rather than designing what you personally like
Chases decisions and answers rather than waiting for them
Is comfortable being on camera, styling pieces on yourself and others, and shooting product with a phone
Is organized enough to run a design pipeline in Notion without being asked
Cares about materials being what we say they are
What We're Looking For
We would love to hear from you if you have:
A jewelry-specific background: jewelry design, goldsmithing, product design for jewelry, or design work inside a jewelry brand or manufacturer
A portfolio with clear CAD designs (MatrixGold, Rhino, RhinoGold, Blender, ZBrush, or similar) that were produced or that show production-ready dimensioning
Experience taking a design through the full process: CAD, spec sheet, supplier brief, sample review, production
Working knowledge of stainless steel, sterling silver, vermeil, plating and lab stones
Experience building or styling jewelry stacks and sets
Comfort using Notion, Figma, or similar tools, or the ability to learn them fast
Experience working with Chinese jewelry manufacturers is a strong advantage
Years of experience matter less to us than the quality of the work and your ownership of it
This Role Is Not For You If:
You can sketch beautifully but cannot produce a manufacturable CAD file with dimensions
You design from taste alone and are not interested in what is actually selling
You need a brief and a deadline from someone else to start work
You wait to be followed up with rather than following up yourself
You are not comfortable being in the studio, styling pieces on yourself, and shooting them
You treat spec sheets and supplier back-and-forth as someone else's job
You want to design a collection from scratch rather than build around what already works

Job Title: Senior Store and Financial Operations Manager
Job Description:
Job Description
Responsible for the strategic oversight of store/inventory operations and financial management, ensuring robust internal controls, accurate reporting, and alignment of stock and financial processes with organizational goals across the business.
Responsibilities
Oversee end-to-end store/inventory operations including procurement coordination, receiving, storage, and stock control
Lead financial operations related to store activities — budgeting, cost analysis, and expense management
Develop and enforce internal controls to prevent stock loss, fraud, and financial discrepancies
Review and approve stock requisitions, purchase orders, and financial vouchers
Prepare comprehensive financial and inventory reports for senior management/board
Conduct variance analysis on stock consumption vs. financial expenditure
Lead periodic audits and reconciliations of stock and financial records
Supervise and mentor store and junior finance/store staff
Drive process improvements and cost optimization strategies
Ensure full compliance with financial regulations, tax obligations, and company policy
Liaise with auditors, senior management, and other departments on store-finance matters
Education
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or related field (required)
Professional certification strongly preferred (ICAN, ACCA, CPA, or equivalent)
A Master's degree (MBA or related) is an added advantage
Experience:
Minimum of 6–8 years' progressive experience in store/inventory and financial operations, with at least 3 years in a senior/managerial capacity
Proven track record of managing multi-unit or multi-branch stock and financial operations preferred
Skills:
Advanced financial management and analytical skills
Strong inventory/supply chain management expertise
Proficiency in accounting/ERP systems (e.g., Sage, QuickBooks, SAP) and advanced Excel
Strategic thinking and decision-making
Strong leadership and people management
High-level reporting and presentation skills
Risk management and internal controls expertise
Other Requirements:
Exceptional integrity, discretion, and accountability at a senior level
Strong stakeholder management and cross-departmental collaboration skills
Ability to work independently, make high-stakes decisions, and manage pressure
Familiarity with regulatory/tax compliance frameworks

The history of the Nigerian Army dates to 1863, when Lt Glover of the Royal Navy selected 18 indigenes from the Northern part of the country and organized them into a local force, known as the "Glover Hausas". The small force was used by Glover as governor of Lagos to mount punitive expedi...read moretion in the Lagos hinterland and to protect British trade routes around Lagos. In 1865, the "Glover Hausa" became a regular force with the name "Hausa Constabulary". It performed both police and military duties for the Lagos colonial government. It later became "Lagos Constabulary". On incorporation into the West Africa Frontier Force (WAFF) in 1901, it became "Lagos Battalion". In addition to this force, the British Government included the Royal Niger Company (RNC), Constabulary Force in Northern Nigeria in 1886 and the Oil Rivers irregular in 1891. In 1889, Lord Fredrick Lugard had formed the incipient body of what was to be known in 1890, as the West Africa Frontier Force, (WAFF), in Jebba, Northern Nigeria. The new unit expanded by absorbing the Northern Nigeria-based elements of the Royal Niger Company (RNC) Constabulary. By the end of 1901, it had incorporated all paramilitary units in the other British dependencies into its command, thus fully meriting its designation "WAFF". The establishment of West Africa Frontier Force (WAFF) led to the merger of all units into regiment in each of the dependencies. The merger in Nigeria produced the Northern Nigerian Regiment and Southern Nigerian Regiment. The First commanders of the Southern Regiments of WAFF were Lt CHP Carter (1899-1901) and Col J Wilcox (1900-1909) respectively. The two regiments were later used for expeditions during the annexation of Nigeria by Lord Lugard between 1901 and 1903.

Collaborate with production and quality control teams to confirm designs are manufacturable within current machine capabilities
Review prototypes/first-run samples against design intent and flag deviations
Update designs based on production feedback (material waste, assembly difficulty, structural issues)
Maintain a library of standard cabinet modules, templates, and reusable design components to improve production efficiency.
Cross-Functional & Administrative:
Work with the sales/CRM team to convert approved quotes into finalized production-ready designs
Maintain accurate design documentation and revision history in the company's project management/ERP system
Support costing/estimation teams with accurate material takeoffs
Stay current on design trends, hardware innovations, and manufacturing techniques relevant to cabinetry
Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree / HND in Architecture, Interior Design, Industrial Design, or related field (or equivalent practical experience)
3+ years experience in cabinet/furniture design, millwork, or joinery — CNC manufacturing environment preferred
Proficiency in CAD software; cabinet-specific design software strongly preferred
Strong understanding of wood-based panel materials (MDF, plywood, particleboard) and their manufacturing tolerances
Excellent spatial reasoning and attention to detail
Ability to read and interpret architectural/interior design drawings.

Client-facing communication skills
Collaborative — comfortable working across design, sales, and shop-floor teams

The Area Business Manager is ultimately accountable for generating sales, ensuring collections are timely and accurate and keeping the entire Direct Distribution growing rapidly in a sustainable manager.

Hire & retain Energy Officers: Hire, train and maintain a team of at least 40 Sun King Energy Officers in the area. Create a reputation and goodwill for the mission of Sun King to provide clean, affordable and reliable source of energy in their areas.
Training of Energy Officers: Provide training to the Energy Officers on several aspects of the business such as sales, collections, product, technical, inventory and logistics related. Ensure that they are fully supervised in the best professional manner demonstrating highest levels of integrity, ethics and professionalism while dealing with customers.
Provide role clarity to Energy Officers: Provide complete clarity to Energy Officers related to their day to day tasks, sales & collections plans, routes and targets. This includes, ensuring Energy Officers have sales route/area to sell in, they know on how to demonstrate and sell Sun King products, they have the confidence to be able to present and resolve basic customer queries on the spot and they have access to Area Business Manager at all times in case of questions and concerns.
Daily field visits: Have a weekly touchpoint with every Energy Officer in your area – either through in-person meetings, making a sale to the customer in your area or having a call. Resolve all possible issues faced by the Energy Officers and report them to your Regional Business Manager, every week. Ensure that first 5 sales of each Energy Officer is done along with the Area Business Manager in the area, by each Energy Officer to ensure that the core sales and collection process is fully understood by each Energy Officer.
Work with Energy Officers: Conduct joint field work with a group of Energy Officers to provide sales and collection training on a weekly basis and drive EO engagement. This includes doing night activations, market activations, visiting local communities and gatherings such as SACCOs, Self Help groups, retail centers and markets to make group sales.
Exceed your sales & collections targets: Meet or exceed sales and collection targets established on 2nd of every month by your Regional Business Manager. Provide daily, weekly updates on sales, EO recruitments, Customer issues and resolutions, in alignment with your Regional Business Manager.
Drive robust field sales processes: Review collection progress with your Energy Officers daily and provide adequate training to them on driving better collections in your areas. This includes, customer and area profiling, ensuring regular and timely collection follow-ups, resolving customer issues to ensure they make payments and ultimately repossessing the systems as a last recourse in case the customer defaults.
Remain externally focused: Keep an eye on companies selling similar products within your area and ensure you take adequate measures to protect and grow our business from pressures. Pre-inform your management team and take measures to ensure Sun King remains a paramount brand name in Solar products for your area.

Company Details: Aldelia’s global management strategy delivers specialised services to the Oil & Gas sector from dedicated teams in each key strategic region. From these centres we can support our clients locally by being able to take advantage of the local labour markets whilst also having the ability...read moreto resource candidates internationally for technical, engineering and higher level positions which require industry leading professionals with international profiles. Each regional team is guided by a common set of processes and working practices within a robust operational structure to ensure a consistent high quality of delivery which our clients can depend on in any market. The origin of Aldelia gives a good indication of what the company was meant to be. Cedric Filet, whilst recovering from a rugby injury, established the company from his bedroom. The dream was to set up a recruitment consultancy which would compete with the top 5 Oil & Gas Recruitment Specialists in a matter of 5 years. To achieve that, Cedric focused on a gap he identified in the Oil & Gas industry: local content. Local content had long been considered a pain for international Oil & Gas firms. These firms understood the necessity of developing local content programs but struggled to implement them. Job Description:
Job Summary
To design, implement and continuously improve the technical security controls that protect the organization's AWS cloud estate, Kubernetes (EKS) platform, software delivery pipelines and data stores; and to provide expert detection, response and assurance capability that keeps the organization's digital services resilient, auditable and compliant with CBN, PCI DSS, ISO 27001 and NDPR requirements.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Cloud and Security Engineering:
Design, implement and maintain preventive and detective security controls across all AWS accounts, including AWS Organizations service control policies, AWS Config rules and conformance packs, AWS WAF and AWS Shield.
Enforce least privilege through IAM roles, permission boundaries, IAM Identity Center and IAM Access Analyzer; drive the elimination of long-lived access keys in favour of federated and role-based access.
Own AWS Secrets Manager end to end — secret lifecycle, automatic rotation, resource and cross-account policies — and lead the removal of hard-coded credentials from application code, manifests and pipelines.
Configure and maintain organization-wide AWS CloudTrail (including data and management events), CloudWatch log groups, metric filters, alarms and retention aligned to regulatory record-keeping requirements.
Implement AWS Config baselines with automated drift detection and remediation against CIS AWS Foundations and PCI DSS benchmarks.
Manage AWS WAF rule sets, rate limiting, bot control and geo restrictions for internet-facing applications behind CloudFront and ALB, and tune rules to minimise false positives without weakening protection.
Operate Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub, Amazon Inspector and Amazon Detective as a single triage workflow — from finding, to enrichment and root-cause investigation, to verified closure.
Define and review secure landing zone and VPC network patterns (segmentation, private subnets, VPC endpoints, security groups, managed prefix lists) and assess new architectures against them.
Kubernetes & Container Security (Amazon EKS):
Harden EKS clusters: private API endpoints, control plane audit logging to CloudWatch, node group hardening, and timely patching of cluster versions and node AMIs.
Design, implement and periodically review Kubernetes RBAC, namespace isolation, service accounts and IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA) / EKS Pod Identity.
Enforce Pod Security Standards, admission control policy (OPA Gatekeeper or Kyverno) and Kubernetes network policies to restrict east-west traffic.
Secure the container supply chain — approved base images, ECR and Amazon Inspector image scanning, image signing and admission-time signature verification.
Deploy and tune runtime threat detection for containers (GuardDuty EKS Runtime Monitoring, Datadog Cloud Security Management) and investigate detections through to resolution.
Secure secret delivery into workloads using the External Secrets Operator or Secrets Store CSI driver backed by AWS Secrets Manager, removing plaintext secrets from manifests and Helm values.
Security Monitoring, Detection & Incident Response (Datadog):
Build and maintain detection coverage in Datadog Cloud SIEM — log pipelines, detection rules, signal correlation, suppression tuning and security dashboards.
Operate Datadog Cloud Security Management (misconfiguration, identity and workload risk) and Application Security Management (runtime protection and vulnerability detection) alongside native AWS security services.
Configure Datadog Sensitive Data Scanner to detect and redact PII and cardholder data in logs and telemetry.
Ensure complete, tamper-evident log coverage across AWS, EKS, applications and databases, with defined retention, archiving and log integrity controls.
Lead technical security incident response — triage, containment, eradication, recovery and post-incident review — and maintain runbooks, escalation paths and tabletop exercises.
Define, track and report security metrics and posture trends to management and risk committees.
Data & Database Security:
Enforce encryption at rest and in transit across RDS, Aurora, DocumentDB, DynamoDB, S3, EBS and EFS using AWS KMS, with defined key policies, rotation and separation of duties.
Implement IAM database authentication and Secrets Manager-driven credential rotation; remove shared, static and over-privileged database accounts in favour of least-privilege roles.
Enable, centralise and monitor database audit logging (RDS and Aurora audit logs, DocumentDB auditing, SQL Server audit, CloudTrail data events) within the central log platform.
Apply data classification, masking or tokenisation and access controls for sensitive and regulated data, and support data loss prevention requirements.
Eliminate public database exposure — private subnets, restrictive security groups, no public accessibility — and validate backup and snapshot encryption, snapshot sharing controls and restore testing.
Review database migrations, schema changes and access grants for security impact before approval.
Governance, Risk & Compliance:
Translate CBN cybersecurity framework, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, NIST CSF and NDPR requirements into enforceable technical controls and repeatable evidence.
Maintain security standards, secure configuration baselines and control documentation, and support internal and external audits with automated evidence collection.
Conduct security assessments, vulnerability management cycles and configuration reviews; coordinate penetration testing and track remediation to closure.
Perform security reviews of third-party vendors, SaaS integrations and exposed APIs
Contribute to risk register maintenance, security exception management and management reporting.
Collaboration, Enablement & Technical Leadership:
Act as senior security advisor to infrastructure, platform, DevOps and application teams during architecture, design and change reviews.
Mentor junior security and platform engineers, and raise the standard of security code and configuration review across engineering.
Automate recurring security operations using Python, Bash, Terraform and AWS-native tooling to reduce manual effort and human error.
Deliver targeted, role-relevant security training for engineering teams covering secure coding, secrets handling and incident escalation.
COMPETENCIES REQUIREMENTS:
Technical:
Deep, hands-on AWS security expertise: IAM, KMS, Secrets Manager, CloudTrail, CloudWatch, AWS Config, WAF and Shield, GuardDuty, Security Hub, Inspector, Detective and VPC network security.
Strong Kubernetes and Amazon EKS security skills: RBAC, IRSA, Pod Security Standards, admission controllers (OPA Gatekeeper or Kyverno), network policies, image scanning, image signing and runtime security.
Practical experience implementing SCA, SAST, DAST, secret scanning and IaC scanning within GitHub Actions, and enforcing branch protection rules, rulesets and OIDC-based pipeline authentication.
Working knowledge of Datadog security capabilities: Cloud SIEM, Cloud Security Management, Application Security Management, Sensitive Data Scanner, log pipelines and dashboards.
Database security across RDS, Aurora, DocumentDB, SQL Server and NoSQL stores: encryption and key management, IAM authentication, audit logging, masking and least-privilege access.
Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform, Helm and GitOps workflows, with proficient scripting in Python and Bash.
Solid grounding in security frameworks and regulation: CBN cybersecurity guidelines, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, NDPR and GDPR; threat modelling (STRIDE) and MITRE ATT&CK.
Vulnerability management, incident response and digital forensics fundamentals.
Behavioural:
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with sound risk judgement and the ability to prioritise what matters most.
Excellent written and verbal communication; able to explain technical risk to non-technical stakeholders and influence engineering teams without direct authority.
Ownership mindset — detail-oriented, proactive and persistent in identifying and closing control gaps.
Pragmatic and collaborative; balances security rigour against delivery velocity.
Calm, structured and decisive under incident pressure.
Coaching and knowledge-sharing orientation, with a commitment to raising security capability across the organization.
Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Engineering or a related discipline.
Professional certification is strongly preferred, for example: AWS Certified Security – Specialty, Certified Kubernetes Security Specialist (CKS), CISSP, CISM, CCSP, OSCP, or GIAC certifications (GCSA, GCIH, GWAPT, GCLD).
Minimum of 6–8 years' experience in cybersecurity or security engineering, including at least 4 years securing production AWS workloads and at least 2 years securing Kubernetes (preferably Amazon EKS) and CI/CD pipelines.
Demonstrable, hands-on experience implementing cloud, container, pipeline and database security controls in a regulated environment; financial services experience is an advantage.
Proven track record of leading security incident investigations and remediation in production environments

Job Summary
The School Driver at Discovering Talents Academy (DTA) is responsible for providing safe, reliable, and efficient transportation services for students, staff, and school-related activities.
This role is paramount in ensuring the well-being of our pupils during transit and maintaining the school's commitment to safety and operational excellence.
The Driver will adhere strictly to all DTA transportation policies and procedures, contributing to a secure and positive environment for everyone.
Key Responsibilities
Safe Vehicle Operation & Transportation:
Operate school vehicles (buses, cars) safely and responsibly, adhering strictly to all traffic regulations, speed limits (e.g., maximum 60 km/h in residential areas), and road safety rules.
Prioritize the safety of all passengers (students and staff) during every trip.
Conduct morning pick-ups and afternoon drop-offs according to designated routes and schedules.
Assist pupils in safely boarding and alighting the vehicle, ensuring no hurrying or pushing.
Collaborate effectively with the Bus Attendant to monitor student behavior and ensure an orderly environment on the bus.
Refrain from answering phone calls while driving and maintain respect towards other road users.
Ensure the bus adheres strictly to scheduled pupil pick-up and drop-off points; no unauthorized halts or picking up of unassigned individuals.
Vehicle Maintenance & Care:
Perform daily pre-trip checks, including fluid levels (engine oil, water/coolant, steering oil), tire pressure, battery, lighting systems (headlights, brake lights, indicators), and window/door functionality.
Warm up the vehicle's engine for 5-10 minutes before take-off.
Maintain the cleanliness of the vehicle, both interior and exterior, on a daily basis (washing exterior after morning pick-up, cleaning interior after evening drop-off, general cleaning on Saturdays).
Conduct continuous and diligent checks to ensure the ongoing roadworthiness of the vehicle.
Report any fault or anomaly discovered on the vehicle immediately in the designated vehicle maintenance update book.
Ensure vehicles are fueled every Wednesday and Saturday, or as needed.
Ensure vehicles are serviced strictly as and when due, following the maintenance schedule.
Oversee mechanical repairs by taking the vehicle to the authorized mechanic, explaining the fault, staying during the repair, and test-running the vehicle afterward.
Security & Compliance:
Ensure the school bus is properly secured at all times, including winding up windows and locking doors after use.
Maintain a valid driver's license and ensure timely renewal.
Ensure all vehicle documents (registration, insurance) are complete, intact, and readily available.
Adhere to all DTA Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for School Drivers.
Submit vehicle keys and bus phone to the Admin Officer after morning pick-up and evening drop-off.
Be available for Saturday duties as assigned, including general cleaning and maintenance.
Communication & Reporting:
Communicate effectively with the Bus Attendant regarding student behavior, safety, and operational matters.
Report any delays in pupil pick-up/drop-off to the Admin Officer immediately.
Document observations regarding driving habits, vehicle issues, and pupil behavior in daily reports.
Communicate using the English language while on duty.
Qualifications
Education: Minimum of a Secondary School Leaving Certificate.
License: Valid and current professional driver's license.
Experience: 3-5 years of proven experience as a professional driver, preferably in a school or passenger transport setting.
Knowledge:Thorough knowledge of local traffic laws, road safety regulations, and basic vehicle maintenance. Familiarity with DTA's routes is an advantage.
Skills:Excellent driving skills, strong observational skills, and ability to manage time efficiently.
Personal Attributes:Patient, responsible, reliable, punctual, and a calm demeanor, especially when interacting with children.
Key Competencies:
Safe Driving Practices
Vehicle Maintenance & Care
Punctuality & Reliability
Adherence to Regulations & SOPs
Customer Service (with students & parents)
Problem-Solving (minor vehicle issues, route challenges)
Communication & Reporting
Responsibility & Accountability
Commitment to Child Safety.

Job Title: Program Officer, Health Systems Strengthening and Primary Healthcare (PHC)
Job Description:
Your Role
The Program Officer (PO) Will
Support the design, development and implementation of Primary Health Care (PHC) reforms across both foundational reforms and innovation agenda pillars at the country level (federal and sub-nationals) including the Nigeria Integrated Health (NIH) Model and State Delivery and Intelligence Units (SDIU)
Support PHC reforms that help Nigeria and other countries “spend well” on PHC by reforming financing fundamentals, delivery platforms, getting funds more directly to facilities or ‘local’ levels, enabling autonomy over the use of these funds and extending recourse and decision making over supplies and human resources
Support the operationalization and institutionalization of PHC functionality and use of data for decision-making and accountability
Strategically develop and manage one or more portfolios of grants and contracts requiring high-level grant management skills, monitoring and evaluation to ensure that the outcomes are achieved
Develop key partnerships to expand and scale health impact at the country level
Have a very strong country led focus and will engage with our country teams to ensure excellent partnerships, shared goals and joint vision
Foster exceptional relationships with key Government stake holders at Ministerial level in Nigeria, using excellent communication skills with deep technical knowledge to support Ministries of Health (MoH) etc, to embrace the PHC strategy and create impact and better utilization of PHC services in Nigeria.
This position reports to the Deputy Director – HSS and PHC, in the Nigeria Country Office.
What You'll Do
This is a significant role in championing the PHC strategy across both Innovation and Foundational pillars and fostering unparalleled levels of support and partnership from the Nigeria Country Office (NCO). The PO will work closely with all health sub-teams and NCO to support health and PHC systems reforms.
Ensure that the results framework is embedded across our HSS and PHC pillars and is fostered and jointly owned by relevant sub-teams and Program Support Teams (PSTs).
Facilitate development of annual investment plans and budgets, develop, modify, and implement strategy at the national and sub-national levels. Work with NCO leadership, sub-teams and PSTs as requested to address cross-cutting issues and improve functions and performance.
Accountable for the identification and assessment of key portfolio risks, and the development and management of mitigation/contingency plans at the portfolio level.
Manage partnerships and grantee relationships to achieve impact, for example, by conducting site visits, convening meetings of key partners, monitoring, and evaluating components of grants.
Support and coordinate with non-Gates Foundation partners to increase/scale the health impact at the country level.
Provide technical support in the areas of innovation in Primary Health Care (PHC) systems strengthening and service delivery with a focus on leveraging innovations and using digital technologies to improve outcomes.
Measure results and return on investments, pivot and learn from findings to create impact, and contribute to the nascent knowledge base on PHC systems strengthening.
Negotiate, implement, and manage complex portfolio of grants on PHC systems and delivery innovation and foundational reforms that will improve PHC functionality, service delivery and efficiency at population levels of scale.
Advise and support deep and moderate NCO efforts to accelerate foundational reforms by enabling federal and sub-national governments to effectively disburse funds/purchase high-priority services from PHC facilities, while enabling PHC facilities to receive and use these funds.
Provide technical support, facilitation, technical assistance, mentoring and coaching in the design and implementation of health systems strengthening activities, tailored to the specific needs of the country.
Advice and support the strengthening of platforms to improve subnational technical capacity to analyze & use data for PHC performance management.
Success Criteria
Demonstrated abilities to work with multiple partners in Nigeria, including government, other donors, grantees to create a common vision and visualize simple and effective but implementable solutions to complex problems that lead to sustainable impact.
Strong strategic thinker with experience developing evidence-based strategic or operational plans as well as shaping and managing sustainable and scalable ventures.
Experienced coalition builder and background of creating effective partnerships and establishing cross-sectoral linkages at the different levels of government.
Comfortable in a wide range of political, cultural, geographic and operational situations, demonstrating culturally sensitive behavior with a diverse range of partners.
Deep understanding of systems strengthening and PHC service delivery to improve outcomes.
Demonstrated working experience in health systems strengthening and PHC in developing economies, experience in Nigeria and Sub-Saharan Africa is highly preferred.
Demonstrates a growth mindset with curiosity about new approaches, ability to change direction when needed, and willingness to seek feedback and course correct based on it.
Excellent program and project management capabilities – always driving towards clear results within a timeline.
Clear, consistent communication in both writing and speaking.
Demonstrates excellent individual judgement and can act independently but also knows when to pull in additional resources or solicit others for assistance.
Capability to understand the challenges and complexity of introducing and scaling innovations in service delivery in Low and Middle Income Countries (LMIC) and how to work with partners and key collaborators, especially public sector entities, to overcome these challenges. Experience in developing public-private partnerships is desired.
Degree in Public Health, Health Systems and Administration, Health Financing, or other relevant field.
Your Experience
Minimum of 6 years of relevant work experience in health systems strengthening, PHC or public health in African settings
Ideally, 5+ years of experience in a low-income country context, or equivalent experience, in working directly with ministries of health, donors and implementing agencies in shaping the health systems strengthening, PHC reforms and innovation agendas.
Established track record of carrying out analytical/diagnostic work and preparing high-quality technical reports, policy briefing materials, and presentations to influence health and PHC systems policy decision making and implementation at national and subnational levels.
Experience in the use of diagnostics and other decision tools to improve quality, effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of care.
Track record of building strong relationships with implementing partners, donors, and officials at all levels of government
In-depth understanding of the Nigerian health system and of federal and state health policy, with on-the-ground experience in northern Nigeria in particular.
Other Attributes
Must be able to legally work in the country where this position is located without visa sponsorship.
Ability to travel up to 30%, domestically and internationally.

Job Summary
We are seeking an experienced
Odoo Techno-Functional Consultant
to support the end-to-end delivery of Odoo ERP implementations by combining strong business and functional consulting capability with hands-on technical knowledge of the Odoo platform.
The successful candidate will work directly with clients to understand business processes, gather and analyse requirements, configure Odoo, conduct fit-gap analysis and translate approved requirements into effective Odoo solutions.
Unlike a purely Functional Consultant, the Techno-Functional Consultant should also be capable of handling
controlled technical activities and minor customisations
, troubleshooting technical issues, understanding integrations and working effectively with Odoo Developers on requirements that require more substantial development.

standard-first approach

Business Analysis & Requirements Gathering
Lead and participate in client discovery and requirements workshops.
Understand the client's existing business processes, challenges and objectives.
Gather, analyse and document functional and business requirements.
Map client processes against Odoo capabilities.
Develop process flows, user stories, functional specifications and acceptance criteria.
Challenge unclear or unnecessary requirements and help clients simplify processes where appropriate.
Ensure requirements are validated and approved before configuration or development begins.
Maintain traceability between business requirements, solution design and delivered functionality.
Fit-Gap Analysis & Solution Design
Assess each requirement to determine whether it can be delivered through:
Standard Odoo functionality
Odoo configuration
A controlled business-process change or workaround
Minor technical extension
Custom development
The Techno-Functional Consultant should recommend customisation only where the approved requirement cannot reasonably be achieved using standard Odoo functionality.
Where significant development is required, produce a clear functional and technical handover for the Odoo Developer.
Odoo Functional Configuration
Configure Odoo applications based on approved requirements.
Configure workflows, application settings, user roles and access rights.

Set up multi-company and intercompany processes where required.
Ensure configuration follows agreed Odoo implementation standards.
Maintain appropriate configuration documentation.
Odoo Technical Activities
The Techno-Functional Consultant should be capable of undertaking controlled technical activities including:
Understanding and working with Odoo models, fields, views and relationships.
Creating or modifying views where appropriate.
Working with XML and QWeb templates.
Understanding Odoo ORM and Python-based business logic.
Creating or supporting automated and scheduled actions.
Troubleshooting functional and technical issues.
Analysing Odoo logs and errors.
Understanding PostgreSQL sufficiently to support investigation and data analysis.
Supporting API and integration troubleshooting.
Reviewing existing custom modules to understand their purpose and impact.
Implementing minor technical changes where these fall within the agreed responsibilities of the role.
Complex module development, major integrations, significant architectural changes and substantial customisation should be assigned to an
Odoo Developer
.
Integration Support
Gather and document functional integration requirements.
Define required data flows between Odoo and third-party systems.
Support field mapping and interface specifications.
Understand REST APIs, webhooks and authentication concepts.
Test integrations from a functional and business perspective.
Troubleshoot integration issues and determine whether problems originate from configuration, data, Odoo customisation or the external system.
Work with Odoo Developers and third-party technical teams on complex integrations.

Job Summary
The Asset Performance Manager (APM) is a senior leadership role within HEOSL, reporting functionally to the General Manager Reservoir Development and Strategic Integration and working closely with the COO, accountable for maximising asset value through integrated planning, disciplined execution and performance optimisation across the full production value chain, while acting as the single point of integration to ensure plans are delivered, deviations are actively managed, and performance excellence is achieved.
Key Accountabilities
Asset Value Delivery & Ownership:
The APM is accountable for influencing and driving the delivery of safe, reliable, efficient production, providing clear leadership and integration across the full value chain to ensure that asset performance meets or exceeds business expectations.
The role drives disciplined execution and sustained performance improvement by aligning operational delivery with strategic objectives and ensuring that value is consistently realised from the asset.
The APM leads the optimisation of production and uptime, reduction of deferment, improvement in operating cost per barrel, and enhancement of asset recovery and lifecycle performance.
The role drives economic decision-making and prioritisation across all activities within the Asset, ensuring that resources are deployed to maximise value and that trade-offs are understood and actively managed.
The APM ensures that asset performance remains fully aligned with HEOSL strategic objectives and JV partner expectations, providing clear visibility of performance, risks and opportunities.
Integrated Planning & Delivery (ADP Ownership):
The APM owns the development, integration and delivery of the Asset Development Plan (ADP) across all disciplines, ensuring it represents a ‘single source of truth’ perspective of the asset. The role ensures full alignment between long-term (20Q), mid-term (8Q) and Annual Operating Plan (AOP) horizons, maintaining consistency between strategic intent and executable plans.
The Asset Performance Manager supports the translation of strategy into prioritised, deliverable work programmes with clearly defined value outcomes, ensuring that plans are realistic, integrated and aligned with cross-functional resources and constraints.
The APM actively manages the ADP with a dynamic approach, evolving in response to changes in reservoir performance, operational conditions and commercial drivers, while maintaining focus on delivering sustained asset value.
Performance Management & Intervention:
The APM is accountable for defining and governing a robust asset-wide framework for performance management and intervening when performance is (observed as potentially) degrading. The framework covers production delivery, capital efficiency, risk exposure and plan adherence.
The Asset Performance Manager supports regular COO-chaired performance reviews, providing clear visibility of performance against plan and identifying gaps and emerging risks.
Through active engagement, the role challenges stakeholders on delivery performance and drives corrective action where required, escalating to the COO as necessary, and ensuring that underperformance is addressed.
Critical delivery risks are escalated appropriately, with the APM supporting and driving resolution.
Portfolio Optimisation, Functional Alignment & Decision Support:
