Key Accountabilities/Responsibilities
Strategic Leadership & Departmental Management
Develop and implement the strategic vision for the Molecular Genetics Department in alignment with the hospital’s mission and goals.
Provide executive leadership to the department, overseeing all operational, clinical, and research activities.
Manage departmental resources, including budget planning, staffing, and procurement of advanced laboratory equipment and technologies.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) for quality, turnaround time, and service efficiency.
Clinical Diagnostic Services:
Oversee the delivery of high-complexity molecular genetic testing, including next-generation sequencing (NGS), PCR-based assays, Sanger sequencing, and cytogenetic/molecular cytogenetic analyses.
Ensure accurate interpretation and reporting of genetic test results, including variant classification and clinical correlation.
Implement and maintain rigorous quality control, proficiency testing, and validation protocols for all assays.
Serve as the primary consultant for clinicians regarding test selection, result interpretation, and patient management implications.
Research & Innovation:
Lead and foster a robust research program in molecular genetics and genomics, focusing on translational and clinical research.
Secure competitive research grants and collaborate with national and international research consortia.
Drive innovation in genomic technologies, bioinformatics pipelines, and data integration for precision medicine.
Publish findings in high-impact journals and present at scientific conferences.
Bioinformatics & Data Science Oversight:
Supervise the development, validation, and maintenance of bioinformatics pipelines for genomic data analysis.
Ensure secure management, storage, and interpretation of large-scale genomic data in compliance with ethical and data protection standards.
Integrate genomic data with electronic health records (EHR) to support clinical decision-making and personalized treatment plans.
Compliance, Accreditation & Quality Assurance:
Ensure compliance with national (MLSCN, NAFDAC) and international (ISO 15189, CAP, CLIA) accreditation standards.
Prepare for and lead external audits and inspections.
Maintain comprehensive documentation for all laboratory processes, validations, and quality management systems.
Implement and oversee continuous quality improvement initiatives.
Education & Collaboration:
Foster interdisciplinary collaboration with departments such as Oncology, Pediatrics, Neurology, and Pathology.
Serve as a key representative in hospital committees related to genetics, precision medicine, and ethics.
Team Leadership & Development:
Support to develop a high-performing team of geneticists, laboratory scientists, bioinformaticians, and support staff.
Promote a culture of scientific excellence, continuous learning, and professional development.
Manage staff scheduling, performance evaluations, and career progression pathways.
Qualifications
MD / PhD in Genetics, Molecular Biology, Genomics, or a closely related field.
An MD/PhD or equivalent clinical genetics qualification is highly advantageous.
Certification or fellowship in Clinical Molecular Genetics, Laboratory Genetics, or a relevant specialty board is preferred.
Demonstrated experience with NGS technologies, bioinformatics, and genomic data interpretation.
Minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in a molecular genetics or genomics laboratory, with at least 3 years in a leadership role.
Proven track record in managing a high-complexity clinical genetics laboratory.
Strong publication record and success in securing competitive research funding.
Expertise in genetic variant interpretation, classification, and reporting standards (ACMG/AMP guidelines).
Experience with laboratory information management systems (LIMS) and bioinformatics tools.
Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills.
Knowledge of ethical, legal, and social implications (ELSI) of genetic testing and data sharing.

Relevant certifications such as CompTIA Network+ (N10 series), Security+, or equivalent networking credentials are highly beneficial.
Ability to work on-site in Ikeja on a short time training and collaborate effectively with the wider education and operations teams.

Job Description:
Duties
Three-Country Financial Coordination and Oversight:
Coordinate the financial management and reporting requirements of I-Youth 2.0 across Nigeria, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.
Serve as the central finance focal point for coordination between the project management team and country-level finance/admin personnel.
Establish and maintain mechanisms for the timely collection, review, consolidation, and submission of financial information from the three countries.
Ensure consistency in the application of project financial procedures, reporting requirements, and financial controls across country operations.
Coordinate country-level financial reporting calendars and ensure timely submission of financial information required for project management and donor reporting.
Review country-level financial information and identify discrepancies, unusual expenditure patterns, budget pressures, unsupported costs or other financial management issues requiring corrective action.
Consolidate country-level financial information for program-wide management reporting and financial analysis.
Facilitate cross-country learning and consistency in financial management practices while recognizing applicable country-specific regulatory and institutional requirements.
Budget Management and Financial Analysis:
Monitor project budgets and expenditure across the three countries against approved work plans, budgets, and implementation schedules.
Prepare regular budget-versus-actual analyses and identify significant variances, emerging budget pressures, and under-utilization of funds.
Provide financial analysis to support project management decision-making, work planning, reprogramming, and resource allocation.
Monitor project commitments, obligations, expenditure trends, and available balances across countries and project components.
Prepare cash-flow projections and funding requirements based on approved implementation plans and projected expenditures.
Advise project management on the financial implications of planned activities and proposed changes to implementation schedules or resource allocation.
Support budget revisions and reprogramming exercises by providing accurate financial analysis and supporting information.
Financial Reporting and Donor Accountability:
Lead the consolidation and preparation of periodic project financial reports for management review and submission to the relevant institutional and donor platforms.
Coordinate financial inputs from Nigeria, Liberia, and Sierra Leone to ensure completeness, accuracy, consistency, and timely reporting.
Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports, including expenditure summaries, budget-versus-actual analyses, cash-flow projections, and other management reports.
Coordinate preparation of financial information required for MasterCard Foundation reporting in accordance with approved reporting formats and timelines.
Ensure alignment between financial reports, approved work plans, implementation progress, and narrative reporting.
Review financial data for accuracy and completeness before submission for management review and approval.
Provide financial information and analysis required for project reviews, management meetings, donor engagements, and other strategic discussions.
Financial Controls and Compliance:
Monitor compliance with IITA financial policies, donor financial requirements, applicable country regulations, and approved project procedures across the three countries.
Review country-level financial submissions, expenditure returns, imprest retirements, and supporting documentation to ensure compliance with applicable requirements.
Identify control weaknesses, financial risks, and compliance gaps and recommend appropriate corrective measures.
Follow up on outstanding financial documentation, unsupported expenditure, and other compliance issues with relevant country teams.
Ensure appropriate segregation of duties and adherence to established financial controls within project operations.
Maintain oversight of project financial documentation and ensure that financial records are complete, accurate, properly authorized, and audit-ready.
Keep abreast of relevant donor and country-specific financial and regulatory requirements affecting project implementation and communicate implications to relevant project personnel.
Fund Management and Disbursement Coordination:
Coordinate timely disbursement of project funds to country teams, implementation locations, and approved project partners in accordance with approved work plans and financial procedures.
Monitor utilization of disbursed funds against approved activities, budgets, and implementation schedules.
Coordinate cash-flow requirements from the three countries and consolidate funding requirements for project management and Finance.
Monitor outstanding advances, imprests, retirements, and financial obligations and ensure timely resolution.
Identify potential cash-flow constraints and communicate them proactively to the Finance Manager and project management.
Ensure that project funding is aligned with implementation priorities and approved financial plans.
Country Finance Coordination:
Provide technical coordination and guidance to country-level finance and finance-facing personnel on project financial procedures and reporting requirements.
Establish clear timelines and reporting expectations for country-level financial submissions.
Review and provide feedback on country financial reports and supporting schedules before consolidation.
Coordinate resolution of financial queries arising from country operations.
Facilitate communication between country teams and the central Finance function on project-specific financial matters.
Support orientation and capacity strengthening of country-level staff on project financial management, donor requirements, and financial controls.
Promote consistent application of project financial procedures across Nigeria, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.
Procurement and Contract Financial Interface:
Work closely with the Procurement Officer to ensure that procurement and contracting activities have appropriate budgetary and financial coverage.
Review financial implications of procurement and contractual commitments within the scope of the accountant’s responsibilities.
Monitor financial commitments arising from major project contracts and procurement activities and ensure appropriate recording and reporting.
Coordinate with Procurement and project teams to ensure that financial documentation required for payment and accountability is complete.
Provide financial information required for procurement planning and project implementation without assuming the procurement function or procurement decision-making authority.
Audit, Assurance and Risk Management:
Coordinate project financial preparations for internal, external and donor audits across the three countries.
Prepare financial schedules, supporting documentation, and responses to audit queries.
Coordinate with country teams to ensure the timely provision of documentation requested during audits and financial reviews.
Track implementation of financial audit recommendations and report outstanding issues to the Finance Manager and project management.
Identify emerging financial risks and recommend measures to strengthen financial controls and accountability.
Maintain an organized and audit-ready financial documentation system for the overall project.
Management Advisory and Decision Support:
Provide the Finance Manager and project management team with timely analysis of the project's financial position and implementation performance.
Highlight significant financial risks, variances, funding gaps, under-utilization, and emerging financial pressures requiring management attention.
Provide financial inputs to annual work planning, project reviews, forecasts, and implementation decisions.
Participate in project management and planning meetings and provide professional financial advice on proposed activities and operational decisions.
Support management in assessing the financial implications of changes in implementation priorities, activity schedules, and resource allocation.
Contribute to the continuous improvement of financial management systems, processes, and controls across the program.
Financial Systems, Records and Data Management:
Maintain accurate and up-to-date project financial records and supporting documentation in accordance with IITA requirements.
Ensure appropriate electronic and physical filing of financial records, contracts, payment documentation, financial reports, and other accountability documents.
Develop and maintain financial tracking tools, reporting templates, and analytical schedules required for effective program-wide financial management.
Promote accurate, timely, and consistent financial data across the three countries.
Support the effective use of financial management and reporting systems for project monitoring and decision-making.
Perform any other duties assigned by the Financial Manager or Program Manager.
Requirements
Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration or a related field.
A professional accounting qualification (ICAN, ACCA or equivalent) is an added advantage.
3-5 years of relevant accounting/finance experience, preferably on donor-funded development or agriculture projects is required.
Competencies
The ideal candidate must have:
Working knowledge of accounting software (e.g., Oracle, SAP, QuickBooks, or similar ERP systems) and advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
Familiarity with donor financial compliance requirements.
Strong attention to detail, integrity, and ability to manage confidential financial information.
Good organizational and time management skills, with the ability to meet reporting deadlines across multiple locations.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Strong financial management and accounting skills.
Sound knowledge of budgeting, financial reporting, and grant management.
Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities.
High attention to detail and accuracy.
Strong organizational and time management skills.
Ability to interpret financial data and prepare management reports.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
High level of integrity, confidentiality, and professional ethics.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other financial management software.

Job Description:
About the Role
The Community Engagement / Advocacy, Communication and Social Mobilisation (ACSM) Officer will lead community-level implementation of farmer-led advocacy, communication and social mobilisation activities within the assigned state. The position is responsible for mobilizing and strengthening Farmer Organizations (FOs), facilitating community dialogue, supporting farmer champions, promoting evidence-based advocacy, and strengthening trust in priority agricultural innovations. Working closely with the State Team Lead and technical specialists, the Officer will facilitate sustained engagement between farmers, government institutions, private-sector actors and other stakeholders to strengthen market responsiveness, generate credible farmer demand and improve accountability within agricultural market systems.
Key Responsibilities
Community Mobilisation and Farmer Organization Engagement
Mobilize, engage and strengthen Farmer Organizations, producer groups and community structures to participate actively in programme interventions.
Support Farmer Organizations to function as advocacy, learning and market coordination platforms.
Facilitate community meetings, Farmer Organization forums and stakeholder consultations.
Maintain regular engagement with participating communities and beneficiary groups.
Farmer-led Advocacy
Support Farmer Organizations to identify, prioritize and articulate farmer concerns affecting market access, technology adoption and service delivery.
Facilitate evidence-based advocacy engagements between farmers and public and private sector actors.
Support implementation of advocacy campaigns, policy dialogues and accountability initiatives.
Track advocacy issues and document stakeholder commitments and responses.
Communication and Social Mobilisation
Implement community communication and awareness campaigns using appropriate local communication channels.
Promote farmer-to-farmer learning through Farmer Champions, Women Champions and Youth Innovation Ambassadors.
Facilitate peer learning events, demonstration plot activities and farmer validation exercises.
Support communication initiatives that counter misinformation and promote trusted farmer-led narratives.
Stakeholder Engagement
Maintain productive relationships with community leaders, extension agents, local government authorities, Farmer Organizations, agro-dealers, processors, financial institutions and civil society organizations.
Support state-level stakeholder engagement activities and community consultations.
Facilitate linkages between Farmer Organizations and market actors.
Gender and Social Inclusion
Promote active participation of women, youth and other underserved groups in programme activities.
Support women-led advocacy groups and encourage equitable participation in leadership and decision-making.
Ensure community engagement activities are inclusive and responsive to local social dynamics.
Monitoring, Evidence and Reporting
Collect and report high-quality field data using approved monitoring tools.
Document farmer feedback, adoption trends, advocacy outcomes and community priorities.
Prepare activity reports, success stories, case studies and field updates.
Support implementation of surveys, assessments and learning activities.
Operational Support
Coordinate logistics for community meetings, trainings, demonstrations and advocacy events.
Maintain accurate records of programme participants, activities and community engagements.
Required Qualifications & Experience
Bachelor's degree in Agricultural Extension, Rural Development, Development Studies, Agricultural Economics, Mass Communication, Sociology, Community Development, Public Administration or a related field.
Professional training in community mobilisation, advocacy, communication or facilitation will be an added advantage.
Minimum of 5 years of relevant experience implementing community-based agriculture, rural development or market systems programmes.
Demonstrated experience working with Farmer Organizations, cooperatives or community-based organizations.
Experience facilitating community mobilisation, stakeholder engagement and farmer training.
Knowledge of agricultural value chains, advocacy and participatory development approaches.
Experience with donor-funded projects and field data collection is an advantage.
Strong facilitation, communication, report-writing and interpersonal skills.
Language & Location Requirements
Fluency in spoken and written English with excellent report writing skills.
Applicants must be a resident of choice of state or be willing to relocate immediately upon employment.
Ability to communicate effectively in the dominant local language of the assigned state is required.
Ability to facilitate community meetings, advocacy dialogues and Farmer Organization engagements in both English and the relevant local language.

Job Description:
About the Role
The Project Manager will provide strategic oversight and day-to-day leadership, coordination and operational management of the programme across all target states, ensuring timely delivery of project activities, outputs and results. With oversight from the Programme Director, the Project Manager will coordinate multidisciplinary technical teams, oversee state-level implementation, monitor workplan execution, manage operational risks, and ensure effective collaboration among consortium partners, government institutions, Farmer Organizations (FOs) and private-sector stakeholders. The position will ensure that programme implementation is well-coordinated, results-oriented and compliant with donor requirements while supporting adaptive management and high-quality delivery.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Management
Lead in translating high-level Project objectives to actionable project scopes, roadmaps, and annual workplans.
Lead the team in executing programme activities across all target States, in alignment with consortium partners and field partners, complying with workplan schedules, quality delivery and at the desired costs.
Establish an adaptive management system of delivery, incorporating the needed flexibility and decision points for prioritisation of clients interest and changing realities and emerging opportunities for better influencing policies and institutions.
Ensure integration of organizational development, advocacy, gender, evidence generation and communication activities.
Represent the Project in high-level forum and stakeholder meetings.
Provide periodic project reports to consortium lead, ensuring compliance to reporting requirements.
Monitor programme performance against approved targets and indicators and report in compliance with clients expectations.
Establish and utilize reporting dashboards to track progress and changes at various levels of the chain.
Team Leadership and Performance Management
Supervise State Team Leads and support effective management of field teams.
Design and implement professional development support plans, keeping team motivated and delivering high-quality work.
Facilitate regular programme review meetings and implementation planning sessions.
Promote collaboration, accountability and effective communication across project teams.
Support staff performance management and continuous improvement.
Stakeholder and Partnership Coordination
In collaboration with the Advocacy expert, lead in undertaking political economy analysis and conflict sensitivity analysis to establish the baselines: identifying winners and losers, enablers, blockers and in what conditions institutional change will occur and the main change agents.
Develop and implement stakeholder management plans, in consultations with the Advocacy and Organizational Development Experts.
Coordinate engagement with government institutions, Farmer Organizations, private-sector actors, research institutions and consortium partners.
Support the organization of stakeholder consultations, technical meetings, advocacy forums, and learning events.
Maintain productive working relationships that facilitate programme implementation and sustainability.
Monitoring, Reporting and Adaptive Management
Track implementation progress and ensure timely submission of technical and operational reports.
Support programme monitoring, evidence generation and learning processes.
Facilitate regular implementation reviews and promote adaptive management based on programme evidence.
Ensure documentation of implementation progress, lessons learned and emerging risks.
Operational and Risk Management
With oversight from Project Director, set up a Project Direction Committee (PDC) to serve as a governance and accountability group, for steering the project.
Coordinate monthly PDC meetings, for progress updates and decision making.
With support from PDC, assess the project risks and establish a risk management plan for the project.
Monitor operational risks affecting programme delivery and implement mitigation measures.
Coordinate logistics and operational support for programme activities.
Ensure compliance with organizational policies, donor requirements, and approved operational procedures.
Financial and Administrative Coordination
Work closely with the Finance, Contracts, and Compliance Manager to ensure activities are implemented within approved budgets.
Review activity implementation plans for operational feasibility and resource requirements.
Monitor timely utilization of financial and logistical resources.
Quality Assurance
Ensure project activities meet agreed technical and operational quality standards.
Coordinate internal quality assurance processes across implementation states.
Support preparation for donor reviews, field monitoring visits and programme evaluations.
Promote continuous learning and application of best practices across programme activities.
Required Qualifications & Experience
Master's degree in project management, Agricultural Economics, Rural Development, Development Studies, Business Administration, Public Administration or a related field.
Professional certification in Project Management (PMP, PRINCE2 or equivalent) will be an added advantage.
Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience managing complex, multi-state development programmes, preferably in agriculture or rural development.
Demonstrated experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams and managing donor-funded projects.
Proven experience in project planning, implementation, stakeholder coordination, and performance monitoring.
Strong understanding of agricultural market systems, Farmer Organization development, and multi-stakeholder partnerships.
Experience working with government institutions, private-sector actors and development partners in Nigeria.
Excellent leadership, coordination, communication, and problem-solving skills.

Job Description:

Company Details:
The Federal College of Education, FCE Yola was established in 1974, as a middle level Teacher Training Institute. Hitherto, it was known as Federal advance Teacher's College, (FATC) Yola. However, actual academic activities commenced during the 1975/76 session, with a total of one hundred and fifty...read more(150) students under the leadership of the Pioneer Principal Mr. C. Pollock, an expatriate. At the time, the college was under the supervision of the Federal Ministry of Education. Mr, Pollock, as the Pioneer Principal, laid a solid foundation for the smooth take off of the college and he completed his tenure in 1982. 

Mr. M.C Okoye succeeded Mr. Pollock as the next Principal of the college. He continued from where his predecessor stopped. He was the principal of the college form 1982 - 1984. 

Mr. Wagabi O. Shittu, was appointed the next Principal of the college in 1984 - 1987 and it was during he tenure the it was renamed from Federal advance Teacher's College, (FATC) to Federal College of Education, (FCE) Yola and thus, the title of the head of the college automatically changed from Principal to Provost and Mr. Shittu could be said to be the first Provost. 

After, Mr. Shittu came Prof. Gidado Tahir in 1987, Prof. Mustapha Abba's tenure in 1996 and Dr. Aminu Chiroma in 2004. 

Dr. Aminu Chiroma was the first home bred Chief Executive of the college. He rose through the ranks from Assistant Lecturer to Chief Lecturer which gave him added advantages on how to attend to the academic and administrative needs of the college. 

Dr. Chiroma has lifted the college to a higher pedestal, as he touched all aspects of the College. The college has seen tremendous infrastructural development and road network as well as staff development.

Job Description:
What This Role Actually Is
This is a hands-on, high-ownership position. You will be a finance lead for the Nigeria entity — responsible for the monthly management reporting pack, executive commentary, the IFRS 9 Expected Credit Loss model, treasury and compliance matters, and the unit economics that inform commercial decisions across the market.
You'll manage the end-to-end monthly close: accruals, prepayments, intercompany, depreciation, FX. You'll produce variance analysis that isolates market-specific effects from one-off items. You'll monitor the loan book, analyse repayment behaviour by cohort, and own provisioning and bad debt trends. You'll support statutory and regulatory reporting, manage documentation for funding and compliance processes, and support due diligence as needed.
And then — because this is Nigeria — you'll also be a commercial partner. You'll sit alongside the commercial team to interrogate unit economics, model new product launches, assess pricing and supply decisions, and build the financial cases for leadership and board discussions.
This is not a role where the strategy happens upstairs and the finance team keeps score. You'll shape both.
What Makes It Different
Most finance roles at this level have inherited structures, established processes, and reporting cadences that largely run themselves. This one asks for more ownership than that. You'll identify automation opportunities, strengthen controls, and ensure IFRS compliance in areas where judgement genuinely matters: IFRS 9, IFRS 16, IAS 21, revenue recognition, IFRS 18 readiness.
You'll also have direct exposure to one of Africa's largest and most dynamic fintech markets, working alongside local and regional leadership to navigate a fast-changing regulatory and commercial landscape. That's a professional education you can't buy.
What You Bring
Qualified Chartered Accountant (ICAN, ACCA, CA or equivalent), with a demonstrable track record in finance management or a senior finance role, including hands-on ownership of statutory and management reporting cycles.
Deep, applied IFRS knowledge — particularly IFRS 9, IFRS 16, IAS 21, and revenue recognition — and proven ability to manage audit processes end-to-end, from file preparation to auditor queries.
Exceptional financial modelling and communication skills: you can build a complex multi-scenario model in Excel and present its conclusions clearly to a CFO or a lender in the same week.
Big 4 training (PwC, Deloitte, EY, KPMG) is a strong advantage. Working knowledge of the Nigerian fintech, lending, or asset-financing sector is a plus, though not required — curiosity and commercial instincts matter more.
The reality check
This role will ask a lot of you. The business is scaling fast, the reporting obligations are real, and the market's dynamics require precision. There will be months where the close feels tight and the audit feels relentless. You'll be operating across strategic and operational levels simultaneously — and some days the most important thing on your plate will be debugging a provisioning model, not presenting to leadership.
If that sounds manageable, it probably is. If it sounds energising — you're probably the right person.
What You'll Find Here
A front-row seat in strengthening the financial infrastructure of one of Africa's largest asset fintech businesses, in one of its most important markets. A mission where every asset financed is a tangible improvement in a customer's daily life. And genuine ownership — the kind where your judgement shapes how this entity reports, controls, and makes decisions, not just maintains them.

Company Details:
The Federal College of Education, FCE Yola was established in 1974, as a middle level Teacher Training Institute. Hitherto, it was known as Federal advance Teacher's College, (FATC) Yola. However, actual academic activities commenced during the 1975/76 session, with a total of one hundred and fifty...read more(150) students under the leadership of the Pioneer Principal Mr. C. Pollock, an expatriate. At the time, the college was under the supervision of the Federal Ministry of Education. Mr, Pollock, as the Pioneer Principal, laid a solid foundation for the smooth take off of the college and he completed his tenure in 1982. 

Mr. M.C Okoye succeeded Mr. Pollock as the next Principal of the college. He continued from where his predecessor stopped. He was the principal of the college form 1982 - 1984. 

Mr. Wagabi O. Shittu, was appointed the next Principal of the college in 1984 - 1987 and it was during he tenure the it was renamed from Federal advance Teacher's College, (FATC) to Federal College of Education, (FCE) Yola and thus, the title of the head of the college automatically changed from Principal to Provost and Mr. Shittu could be said to be the first Provost. 

After, Mr. Shittu came Prof. Gidado Tahir in 1987, Prof. Mustapha Abba's tenure in 1996 and Dr. Aminu Chiroma in 2004. 

Dr. Aminu Chiroma was the first home bred Chief Executive of the college. He rose through the ranks from Assistant Lecturer to Chief Lecturer which gave him added advantages on how to attend to the academic and administrative needs of the college. 

Dr. Chiroma has lifted the college to a higher pedestal, as he touched all aspects of the College. The college has seen tremendous infrastructural development and road network as well as staff development.

Dr. Chiroma has lifted the college to a higher pedestal, as he touched all aspects of the College. The college has seen tremendous infrastructural development and road network as well as staff development.

Job Description:
Action Against Hunger Nigeria (ACF Nigeria) Ltd/Gte is currently recruiting a Logistics and Supply Chain Manager based in Sokoto. The manager oversees the end-to-end supply chain, ensuring time, cost-effective and compliant procurement, storage transportation and delivery of goods and services to support programme implementation. The role is also responsible for managing base operations infrastructure, fleet, assets, ICT systems and security related logistics functions. The position leads the logistics and supply chain team in the base while also supporting partner capacity building.
Position Details
Reporting to: Field Coordinator
Proposed start date: October 2026
Key Responsibilities:
Supply Chain and Procurement Management
Assess and plan logistics capacity to meet programme requirements.
Monitor logistics performance and analyze key indicators.
Support Programme Managers in identifying and planning logistics needs.
Ensure compliance with ACF policies, procedures, and standards across all logistics activities.
Manage and optimize the supply chain, including procurement, transportation, and warehousing, ensuring cost-effectiveness, quality, and timely delivery.
Provide guidance and updates to requesters on the status of logistics requests.
Maintain up-to-date knowledge of local markets and suppliers.
Develop and implement project procurement plans in collaboration with Programme Managers.
Monitor and track supply plans to ensure continuity of operations.
Oversee the delivery of goods and services, ensuring quality standards are met.
Manage inventory and warehouse operations to ensure accurate stock control and availability.
Base Operations, Infrastructure and Facilities Management
Ensure a safe and functional working and living environment for staff.
Oversee the construction, rehabilitation, and maintenance of facilities supporting base operations.
Plan, allocate, and manage logistics assets and equipment to meet operational needs.
Ensure the continuous provision of water, power, and other essential utilities across the base.
Coordinate and monitor the efficient use and movement of fleet vehicles.
Keep staff informed of maintenance schedules, service disruptions, and equipment issues.
Fleet, Asset and Equipment Management
Maintain accurate and up-to-date asset and equipment inventories.
Establish and enforce guidelines for the proper use of equipment.
Ensure the safe, secure, and efficient use of all equipment and assets.
Monitor and optimize equipment utilization to maximize cost-effectiveness.
Collaborate with the Logistics Head of Department to plan and allocate equipment based on operational priorities and needs.
ICT and Communications Management
Supervise and support the ICT Officer to ensure effective delivery of ICT services.
Ensure the availability, reliability, and proper functioning of all voice and data communication systems in line with ACF standards.
Safeguard communication equipment and promote its safe and appropriate use.
Provide user training, technical support, and troubleshooting assistance to ensure effective utilization of ICT and communication systems.
Security and Risk Management
Support the development and implementation of the base security plan in collaboration with the Field Coordinator.
Ensure compliance with logistics-related security procedures and monitor their effective application.
Assess logistics and operational risks and provide recommendations to support informed partner selection and risk mitigation.
Partnership and Capacity Building Support
Coordinate and oversee logistics activities for projects implemented with partners.
Support the development and implementation of logistics-related provisions in partnership agreements.
Monitor compliance with logistics standards, commitments, and procedures by both ACF and partners.
Strengthen partner logistics capacity through training, coaching, and targeted support based on identified needs.
Team Leadership and People Management
Produce a complete monthly logistics report.
Monitor logistics performance indicators and recommend improvements to enhance efficiency and service delivery.
Reporting and Performance Monitoring
Lead and coordinate the daily operations of the logistics team to ensure efficient service delivery.
Delegate tasks effectively and monitor performance to ensure quality results.
Manage the recruitment, onboarding, and retention of logistics staff.
Identify learning needs and contribute to staff training and development plans.
Coach, mentor, and build the capacity of team members to enhance performance.
Conduct regular performance reviews and provide constructive feedback.
Provide technical guidance and support to the team as needed.
Additional Responsibilities
This job description is not intended to be all inclusive and the employee will also perform other related tasks as required and responsible for reporting and communication of progress and achievement of the specific assigned task.
Maintenance of high technical standards.
Conduct all duties in a professional manner following ACF Nigeria mission staff regulations, ACF mandate and charter including promotion of gender equality.
Position Requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Purchasing and Supply, or a related field; a Master's degree is an added advantage.
Professional certification in Logistics or Supply Chain Management (e.g., CIPS, CILT) is desirable.
Minimum of 3 years of experience in logistics and supply chain management, preferably within humanitarian, development, or I/NGO settings.
Strong leadership, team management, and staff development skills, including the ability to deliver training and build team capacity.
High level of integrity, accountability, and transparency.
Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Excellent organizational, analytical, and reporting skills, with strong attention to detail.
Strong communication, interpersonal, and negotiation skills, with the ability to engage effectively with diverse stakeholders. Well versed in English and Hausa language.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently, and perform effectively under pressure.
Flexible and resilient, with the ability to work in challenging and insecure environments.

Inventory Management & Control:

Mr. Wagabi O. Shittu, was appointed the next Principal of the college in 1984 - 1987 and it was during he tenure the it was renamed from Federal advance Teacher's College, (FATC) to Federal College of Education, (FCE) Yola and thus, the title of the head of the college automatically changed from Principal to Provost and Mr. Shittu could be said to be the first Provost. 

After, Mr. Shittu came Prof. Gidado Tahir in 1987, Prof. Mustapha Abba's tenure in 1996 and Dr. Aminu Chiroma in 2004. 

Dr. Aminu Chiroma was the first home bred Chief Executive of the college. He rose through the ranks from Assistant Lecturer to Chief Lecturer which gave him added advantages on how to attend to the academic and administrative needs of the college. 

Dr. Chiroma has lifted the college to a higher pedestal, as he touched all aspects of the College. The college has seen tremendous infrastructural development and road network as well as staff development.

Job Description:
Work Arrangement:
Hybrid (2–3 days per week in the office)
Reports to:
Founder
Salary:
₦800,000–₦1,000,000 gross per month
About the organization
Our client is a growing media, branding and public relations company based in Victoria Island, Lagos. The company provides services across storytelling strategy, brand messaging and positioning, content creation, digital marketing, publishing support, public relations, and launch and media campaigns.
The company works with clients and creative partners to develop culturally relevant content, strengthen brands and deliver meaningful campaigns.
Role purpose
The General Manager will provide strategic and operational leadership, translate the Founder’s vision into clear business priorities and ensure the company delivers creative, culturally relevant and commercially successful work.
The role will oversee business development, client relationships, project delivery, people, partnerships and financial performance. The successful candidate must be able to balance creative quality with the structures, commercial discipline and relationships required for sustainable growth.
Key responsibilities
Strategy and organizational leadership
Work closely with the Founder to translate the company’s vision and mission into business priorities, annual goals and implementation plans.
Identify opportunities to expand the company’s reach, portfolio and impact within Nigeria and other relevant markets.
Monitor industry, audience and digital-media trends and recommend opportunities for innovation and growth.
Provide the structure and operational leadership required to move ideas from concept to successful execution.
Track performance against agreed commercial, operational and creative objectives.
Business development and partnerships
Establish business-development priorities, revenue targets and performance expectations in collaboration with the Founder.
Oversee the development and management of a strong pipeline of opportunities across media, public relations, branding, content, publishing and digital marketing.
Guide the team in developing relationships with prospective clients and converting qualified opportunities into new business.
Review and provide direction on major proposals, pitches, budgets and commercial agreements.
Provide executive-level support for high-value pitches, negotiations and strategic client relationships where required.
Oversee the development of partnerships with writers, publishers, media platforms, production professionals, creative agencies and other collaborators.
Ensure the team strengthens existing client relationships and identifies opportunities for client retention, repeat business and expanded engagements.
Hold the business-development team accountable for agreed targets and regularly report on pipeline activity, conversion rates, revenue performance and partnership outcomes.
Storytelling, brand and project delivery
Oversee the delivery of storytelling, brand-positioning, public relations, content-development, publishing and digital-media projects.
Ensure each project begins with a clear understanding of the client’s story, audience, objectives, scope, deliverables and measures of success.
Guide project teams in developing compelling and culturally relevant narratives.
Oversee the coordination of writers, designers, content creators, publishers, media professionals and other project partners.
Ensure creative work meets the approved brief and company standards and is delivered within agreed timelines and budgets.
Oversee campaign implementation and ensure results are reviewed against agreed performance measures.
Client and reputation management
Serve as a senior point of contact for clients and maintain clear, professional communication throughout each engagement.
Provide strategic advice on messaging, positioning, storytelling and audience engagement.
Manage client expectations and address delivery concerns promptly.
Protect and strengthen the company’s reputation through consistent quality, ethical practice and strong stakeholder relationships.
Operations and financial management
Oversee day-to-day operations, project workflows, resource allocation and supplier relationships.
Develop practical systems for project planning, approvals, documentation, quality assurance and reporting.
Monitor project budgets, revenue, expenses, invoicing, collections and profitability.
Ensure resources are used effectively without compromising the quality of creative work.
Provide regular business and project-performance reports to the Founder.
People and culture
Lead employees and project partners with clarity, accountability and respect.
Set performance expectations and ensure individuals understand their responsibilities, timelines and deliverables.
Coach team members, address performance concerns and identify development needs.
Support recruitment, onboarding and workforce planning as the business grows.
Foster a collaborative culture that values creativity, excellence, cultural awareness, integrity and continuous learning.
What success looks like
Within the first 6–12 months, the General Manager would have:
Established clear visibility of the business-development and project pipelines.
Improved the consistency, timeliness and profitability of project delivery.
Strengthened relationships with key clients and creative partners.
Generated new business and increased opportunities for repeat engagements.
Introduced practical systems for project management, financial reporting and accountability.
Maintained the creative quality and cultural relevance of the company’s work.
Reduced the Founder’s involvement in routine operational matters while maintaining alignment with the company’s vision.
Candidate requirements
Bachelor’s degree in communications, marketing, business administration, media studies or a related discipline; a postgraduate or relevant professional qualification would be an advantage.
At least eight years of relevant professional experience, including three years in a leadership or senior management role.
Experience in media, public relations, branding, advertising, content development, publishing, digital marketing or a related creative industry.
Demonstrated success in business development, pitching, client acquisition and relationship management.
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and coordinating writers, publishers, creatives, media professionals or external partners.
Strong understanding of storytelling, brand positioning, audience engagement and campaign delivery.
Experience managing project budgets, revenue, costs and profitability.
Strong leadership, communication, negotiation and problem-solving skills.
Ability to introduce structure and accountability without limiting creativity.
The organization’s identity and further information will be shared with candidates who progress in the recruitment process.

Purpose Statement
We are seeking an experienced Treasury Management Officer who will be responsible for supporting our day-to-day treasury operations, with a strong focus on
cash-flow management, liquidity planning, fund allocation, banking operations, financial controls, and cash optimization
. The role will ensure that the business has clear visibility into its cash position and that funds are efficiently allocated across lending activities, operational expenses, investments, partner obligations, and other business requirements. The ideal candidate should be analytical, highly detail-oriented, commercially aware, and comfortable working within a fast-paced fintech environment where cash movements, funding requirements, and business priorities can change rapidly.
Responsibilities
Daily Cash & Liquidity Management:
Monitor daily cash positions across bank accounts, wallets, payment platforms, and other financial channels to ensure adequate liquidity for lending activities, settlements, operational expenses, and other obligations.
Cash-Flow Forecasting:
Maintain short-, medium-, and long-term cash-flow forecasts, incorporating expected inflows, collections, disbursements, operating expenses, investments, repayments, and other financial commitments.
Cash-Flow Optimization:
Identify opportunities to improve the timing and allocation of cash, reduce idle funds, optimize working capital, and improve the overall efficiency of CredPal's cash deployment.
Funding & Lending Support:
Work closely with Finance, Credit, Collections, and Business teams to understand lending requirements and ensure adequate funding is available to support credit-card, installment-loan, and other lending activities.
Collections & Inflow Monitoring:
Track expected collections and other material inflows against actual receipts, highlight significant variances, and support improved visibility into cash available for redeployment.
Banking Operations:
Manage day-to-day relationships with banks and financial institutions, including account operations, transfers, placements, settlements, banking charges, transaction limits, and resolution of treasury-related issues.
Fund Allocation:
Coordinate the movement and allocation of funds across accounts and business units based on approved priorities while ensuring appropriate approvals, documentation, and controls.
Investment & Surplus Cash Management:
Support the placement of surplus liquidity in approved instruments, considering liquidity requirements, risk, tenor, yield, and counterparty exposure.
Foreign Exchange Management:
Monitor foreign-currency requirements and exposures, support FX transactions, track applicable exchange rates, and identify opportunities to minimize unnecessary FX costs and exposure.
Treasury Cost Management:
Monitor bank charges, financing costs, transaction fees, interest expenses, and other treasury-related costs, identifying opportunities for negotiation and optimization.
Reconciliation & Controls:
Ensure treasury transactions are properly documented and reconciled and that movements of funds are supported by appropriate approvals and financial controls.
Treasury Reporting:
Prepare daily and weekly treasury reports covering cash position, liquidity, expected inflows and outflows, funding requirements, investments, liabilities, and significant cash-flow variances.
Management Reporting:
Provide Finance and Executive Management with timely insights on liquidity, cash utilization, funding gaps, treasury risks, and upcoming financial obligations to support decision-making.
Treasury Risk Management:
Monitor liquidity, counterparty, interest-rate, concentration, settlement, and foreign-exchange risks and escalate material exposures appropriately.
Process Improvement & Automation:
Work with Finance, Product, Operations, and Engineering teams to improve treasury processes, reporting, reconciliations, payment workflows, and automation.
Compliance:
Ensure treasury activities comply with internal policies, approval limits, regulatory requirements, contractual obligations, and applicable financial controls.
Cross-Functional Collaboration:
Partner closely with Finance, Credit, Collections, Operations, Product, Compliance, and senior management to ensure financial resources are aligned with business priorities.

Accurate and timely cash-flow and liquidity reporting.
Sufficient liquidity to meet business and lending obligations.
Improved cash utilization and reduced idle funds.
Reduced banking, transaction, and FX-related costs.
Timely reconciliation with minimal unresolved variances.
Early identification and escalation of funding gaps.
Strong compliance with treasury controls and approval processes.
Improved treasury efficiency through process optimization and automation.

Relevant experience in engineering drafting, preferably within a manufacturing, industrial or plant environment.

Knowledge of applicable engineering, construction and safety standards.
3-5 years experience in this role. Experience in manufacturing is an added advantage.

Attention to Detail
Engineering Documentation
Analytical & Problem-Solving Skills

Company Details: Created by the Howdy Corporation in St. Louis, MO, 7UP was an optimistic venture from the very start. After great success with the Howdy Orange drink, company founder C.L. Grigg decided to try his luck with lemons and limes. C.L. Grigg spent more than two years testing over 11 different formulas,...read moreall in search of a drink that was refreshing enough to prove irresistible to the people of Missouri and the world at large. In 1929, C.L. Grigg’s bubbliest drink was born. The public quickly developed a taste for Grigg’s caramel colored lemon-lime soda. Bib-Label Lithiated Lemon-Lime Soda sold, and sold well. As the drink grew more and more popular, the original name was traded in for something short and sweet. Bib-Label Lithiated Lemon-Lime Soda became known as 7UP. Early advertising featured a winged 7UP logo with copy that read "a glorified drink in bottles only. Seven natural flavors blended into a savory, flavory drink with a real wallop." The drink was so successful by 1936 that Grigg changed the name of The Howdy Corporation to The Seven-Up Company. By the late 1940s, 7UP had become the third best-selling soft drink in the world. In the decades to follow, 7UP developed iconic branding, setting it apart from industry front-runners. In 1967, 7UP brought the phrase UNCOLA into the national vernacular. The UNCOLA campaign set 7UP apart from its competition and became part of a counter cultural that symbolized being true to yourself and challenging the status quo. Always at the frontier of taste and pop culture, 7UP was also among the first sodas to introduce sugar-free and caffeine free options. Through the years, advertising for 7UP featured everything from a cartoon mascot named Spot, to the "It’s an Up thing" and "Make 7UP yours" taglines.

Company Details: Created by the Howdy Corporation in St. Louis, MO, 7UP was an optimistic venture from the very start. After great success with the Howdy Orange drink, company founder C.L. Grigg decided to try his luck with lemons and limes. C.L. Grigg spent more than two years testing over 11 different formulas,...read moreall in search of a drink that was refreshing enough to prove irresistible to the people of Missouri and the world at large. In 1929, C.L. Grigg’s bubbliest drink was born. The public quickly developed a taste for Grigg’s caramel colored lemon-lime soda. Bib-Label Lithiated Lemon-Lime Soda sold, and sold well. As the drink grew more and more popular, the original name was traded in for something short and sweet. Bib-Label Lithiated Lemon-Lime Soda became known as 7UP. Early advertising featured a winged 7UP logo with copy that read "a glorified drink in bottles only. Seven natural flavors blended into a savory, flavory drink with a real wallop." The drink was so successful by 1936 that Grigg changed the name of The Howdy Corporation to The Seven-Up Company. By the late 1940s, 7UP had become the third best-selling soft drink in the world. In the decades to follow, 7UP developed iconic branding, setting it apart from industry front-runners. In 1967, 7UP brought the phrase UNCOLA into the national vernacular. The UNCOLA campaign set 7UP apart from its competition and became part of a counter cultural that symbolized being true to yourself and challenging the status quo. Always at the frontier of taste and pop culture, 7UP was also among the first sodas to introduce sugar-free and caffeine free options. Through the years, advertising for 7UP featured everything from a cartoon mascot named Spot, to the "It’s an Up thing" and "Make 7UP yours" taglines.

The role requires someone who understands Nigerian internet culture, youth trends, social media behaviour, and the type of content that drives engagement and shareability.
The Meme Curator will work closely with Content Creators, Graphic Designers, Video Editors, and Social Media Managers to identify opportunities for NOBZO to participate in relevant conversations and trends while maintaining appropriate brand standards.
Key Responsibilities
Monitor TikTok, Instagram, X, Facebook, and other relevant platforms for emerging trends, memes, formats, and conversations.
Identify memes and trending content that are relevant to NOBZO and its target audience.
Recommend creative ways to adapt trending content to NOBZO’s property, lifestyle, and brand context.
Maintain and organise a meme and content bank using Google Drive or other approved platforms.
Collaborate with Content Creators, Graphic Designers, Video Editors, and Social Media Managers on approved content concepts.
Monitor emerging internet culture and identify opportunities for timely and relevant content.
Ensure sourced content is appropriate for NOBZO and does not create unnecessary reputational or brand risks.
Avoid inappropriate, misleading, copyrighted-risk, excessively watermarked, or otherwise unsuitable content.
Submit regular trend updates, meme recommendations, and content opportunities through approved team communication channels.
Follow the established review and approval process for all meme and content concepts.
Requirements
0–2 years of relevant experience in social media, content creation, digital media, community management, or a related area.
Strong understanding of Nigerian internet culture, memes, social media trends, and youth-oriented content.
Active familiarity with platforms such as TikTok, Instagram, X, and Facebook.
Strong awareness of emerging trends and ability to identify them early.
Ability to distinguish between content that is relevant and content that may create brand or reputational risk.
Strong creative thinking and ability to translate trends into brand-relevant concepts.
Good organisational skills and ability to maintain a structured content bank.
Ability to work collaboratively with creative and social media teams.
Strong communication skills and attention to detail.
Candidates with strong demonstrated social media awareness or relevant personal/portfolio experience are encouraged to apply, even without formal professional experience.

Job Description
The Head, Procurement & Vendor Management is responsible for leading and executing the organization's procurement and vendor management strategy, ensuring the delivery of cost-effective, compliant, and value-driven sourcing solutions across the business.
The role oversees procurement planning, strategic sourcing, contract management, vendor governance, supplier performance management, and procurement risk management while driving operational excellence, process improvements, and adherence to regulatory and corporate governance requirements.
The incubent will lead vendor onboarding and due diligence processes, manage supplier relationships and performance, oversee competitive bidding and contract negotiations, and ensure the integrity of vendor data and procurement records.
The role also provides leadership to the Procurement and Vendor Management team, partners with key stakeholders across Finance, Risk, Compliance, Legal, and business units, and delivers strategic insights, reporting, and continuous improvement initiatives that support business objectives and maximize value from supplier engagement.
Qualifications
Type of Qualification: First Degree
Field of Study: Procurement, Economics, Management, Accounting or a related field
Master's degree is an added advantage.
Experience Required:
Minimum of 7-10 years' progressive experience in Procurement, Strategic Sourcing, Vendor Management, Contract Management, Supplier Relationship Management, and Procurement Operations.
Strong experience in supplier risk management, regulatory compliance, audit controls, and third-party risk management within a financial services or regulated industry environment.
Hands-on experience managing procurement processes using SAP or other procurement and procure-to-pay systems.
Demonstrated experience leading strategic sourcing initiatives, vendor negotiations, contract administration, supplier performance management, and cost optimization projects.
Proven leadership experience managing procurement and vendor management teams and engaging senior stakeholders across Finance, Risk, Compliance, Legal, and business functions.
Knowledge of the Pension, Financial Services, Asset Management, or Banking industry and relevant regulatory requirements is an added advantage.
Behavioural Competencies:
Upholding Standards
Generating Ideas
Developing Strategies
Taking Action
Analysing Solutions.
Technical Competencies:
Procurement & Strategic Sourcing
Vendor & Supplier Management
Written Communication
Business Administration Skills
Data Management.

Job Description:
Location:
Sapele, Delta
Job Summary
The Cashier is responsible for accurately processing all customer payments and financial transactions at the filling station while maintaining excellent customer service and strict accountability for cash received.
The role involves receiving payments for fuel, lubricants and other products or services sold at the station, issuing receipts, maintaining accurate transaction records, reconciling daily sales and cash collections, and ensuring that all funds are properly accounted for and handed over in accordance with company procedures.
The Cashier reports directly to the Station Manager and is expected to maintain the highest standards of integrity, accuracy, confidentiality, professionalism and financial accountability.
Key Responsibilities
Cash Handling & Payment Processing:
Receive and process payments from customers for fuel, lubricants and other products sold at the station.
Process cash, POS/card, bank transfer and other approved payment methods accurately.
Verify payments before confirming transactions or releasing goods/services where applicable.
Provide customers with accurate receipts and appropriate change.
Maintain strict accountability for all cash and payment transactions handled during each shift.
Ensure personal funds are never mixed with company funds.
Daily Sales Reconciliation:
Reconcile cash collected against sales records, POS transactions, transfers and other payment records at the end of each shift.
Ensure that total collections correspond with recorded sales.
Prepare accurate daily/shift cashier reports.
Immediately report shortages, overages, payment discrepancies or suspicious transactions to the Station Manager.
Properly hand over cash, transaction records and supporting documents at the end of each shift.
Transaction Recording & Documentation:
Maintain accurate and complete records of all transactions.
Ensure receipts, POS slips, transfer confirmations and other transaction documents are properly maintained.
Follow established procedures for cancelled, reversed, failed or disputed transactions.
Assist with maintaining financial records required for daily, weekly and monthly station reconciliation.
Ensure transaction information is entered correctly into the station's approved system or register.
Customer Service:
Attend to customers courteously, promptly and professionally.
Respond appropriately to customer enquiries relating to payments, receipts and transactions.
Escalate customer complaints or transaction disputes to the Station Manager where necessary.
Maintain a professional attitude even when handling difficult customers or payment disputes.
Help create a positive and efficient customer experience at the station.
Cash & Financial Control:
Safeguard cash and other financial instruments under the Cashier's custody.
Follow all company cash-handling, banking and financial-control procedures.
Never approve unauthorized discounts, refunds, credits or transaction adjustments.
Maintain confidentiality regarding company sales, revenue and other financial information.
Immediately report suspected fraud, theft, counterfeit currency or other irregularities.
Cooperate fully with internal audits, cash counts and financial reviews.
POS & Payment Terminal Management:
Operate POS terminals and other approved payment systems correctly.
Confirm successful POS transactions before treating payments as completed.
Monitor failed or reversed transactions and escalate unresolved issues.
Keep POS terminals and related equipment secure.
Report malfunctioning payment equipment or connectivity problems promptly.
Shift Handover:
Complete all required reconciliation before handing over to another cashier.
Clearly document outstanding transactions or unresolved discrepancies.
Ensure cash, receipts and transaction records are properly transferred and acknowledged.
Never leave the cashier position unattended without following the approved handover procedure.
Compliance, Safety & Station Procedures:
Comply with all company policies, operational procedures and financial-control requirements.
Observe filling-station safety procedures and applicable health and safety requirements.
Maintain a clean, organized and secure cashier/work area.
Participate in staff meetings, training programmes and operational briefings.
Carry out other reasonable duties assigned by the Station Manager.
Qualifications
Interested candidates should possess an HND / Bachelor`s Degree with 1 - 5 years experience.

Job Description:
Program Overview: Association and Chamber Excellence (ACE)
The Association and Chamber Excellence (ACE) Program is a professional development and certificate program established by CIPE in collaboration with the Nigerian Association of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture (NACCIMA) to strengthen the capacity of chamber of commerce and business membership organization (BMO) leaders. The program addresses key institutional challenges such as weak governance, limited leadership development, and inadequate funding models by providing practical training in governance, financial sustainability, policy advocacy, and member service delivery. By equipping chamber and association leaders with essential leadership and management skills, ACE aims to enhance institutional effectiveness, strengthen the credibility of BMOs, and support private sector growth and regional trade integration. ACE is currently being delivered through an academic institution in Nigeria, and efforts are ongoing to expand the program across Nigeria and the African region. CIPE is seeking a delivery partner that can institutionalize, manage, and scale the program while positioning ACE as a recognized certification platform for chamber and association executives and professionals.
Objectives and Expected Outcomes
As an ACE Institutional Partner- Nigeria, the expected objective is to expand and diversify stakeholder engagement while strengthening chambers and business associations through capacity building, leadership development, and strategic partnerships. The partnership will foster a dynamic Community of Practice that promotes peer learning, collaboration, advocacy, and knowledge sharing across institutions. Through effective documentation of success stories, lessons learned, and best practices, as well as strong monitoring, evaluation, and reporting systems, the program will drive continuous improvement and informed decision-making. Ultimately, the expected outcomes include improved organizational performance and service delivery, a larger pool of skilled and certified chamber executives, stronger institutional resilience and resource management, enhanced stakeholder partnerships, and a sustainable certification ecosystem supported by alumni networks, continuous professional development, and regional learning platforms.
Scope of Responsibility for ACE Institutional Partner – Nigeria
The selected academic institution and ACE Institutional Partner- Nigeria will take on a set of responsibilities to ensure the ownership, delivery, management, growth, and institutionalization of the ACE Program, including but not limited to:
Program Delivery and Management
: Manage and deliver the ACE Program as an institutionalized professional program, including operational planning, growth planning, and long-term sustainability of the program.
Certification Strategy
: Develop and implement a roadmap for transitioning ACE from a certificate program into a recognized professional certification program, including a process plan for certification renewal, refresher courses, and continuing professional development opportunities.
Value Transfer
: Ensure the successful transfer of practical management skills from participants back to their respective chambers or organizations, including providing practical tools, institutional action plans, and knowledge-transfer mechanisms.
Alumni Support and Ecosystem Development
: Design, develop, and manage a robust ACE Alumni Network that promotes mentorship, networking, peer learning, advocacy, knowledge-sharing, continuous professional development, and alumni engagement.
Regional Collaboration and Peer Learning
: Develop a collaborative and coordination framework with delivery partners, chambers, associations, and stakeholders across Nigeria and the African region. This should include plans for national, cross-border peer learning and participation in regional business and policy discussions.
Business Development and Strategic Partnerships
: Develop a strategy for engaging international institutions, development organizations, and partners to strengthen the visibility, credibility, and sustainability of the ACE Program.
Incentivizing Participation
: Implement strategic outreach and recruitment campaigns to encourage chambers and business membership organizations (BMOs) to enroll their executive, managerial, and relevant staff in the ACE Program.
Inclusion Strategy
: Implement an inclusion strategy that promotes participation among women-led organizations, youth-led organizations, underserved regions, persons with disabilities, and other underrepresented groups.
Sustainability Model
: Establish a viable model encompassing pricing strategies, cohort sizes, delivery formats, partnership opportunities, and long-term financial planning to ensure the program’s sustainability beyond donor funding.
Marketing and Promotion
: Design and implement a comprehensive promotion strategy, including branding, messaging, participant recruitment, and regional visibility initiatives.
Faculty Recruitment and Management
: In coordination with the current ACE delivery partner in Nigeria, conduct a train-the-trainer workshop for members of faculty newly recruited to join the delivery of the ACE program and manage this qualified faculty pool.
Evaluation and Certification
: Establish clear standards for participant evaluation and issue formal certificates upon successful completion of all program requirements.
Impact Tracking and Reporting
: Develop and implement a robust Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) framework that includes baseline assessments, endline assessments, periodic impact tracking, alumni tracking, and organizational performance measurement. The framework should provide evidence of institutional improvements and business outcomes attributable to the program and include regular reporting to CIPE.
The selected institution will be responsible for putting in place the necessary systems and arrangements to support program delivery; monitoring and evaluation; documentation of success stories, impact stories, and case studies; the ACE program accreditation and certification process; participant management; faculty engagement; and alumni engagement in accordance with the agreed deliverables.
Qualifications & Eligibility Criteria
Prospective ACE Institutional Partner—Nigeria must meet the following minimum qualifications:
Full accreditation by relevant national or international educational regulatory bodies with an established academic reputation in business, management, public policy, leadership, or executive education.
A minimum of 10 years of institutional experience in designing and delivering executive education programs, particularly for membership organizations, business associations, or chambers of commerce.
At least 5 years of experience administering dedicated capacity-building, leadership development, certification, or policy advocacy programs.
Strong active relationships and existing connections with the private sector, industry hubs, chambers, and business associations.
A proven track record of at least two successful collaborations with international development organizations, donor agencies, or NGOs.
Demonstrated experience managing accredited professional certification or executive education programs.
A robust pool of qualified faculty members with at least 10 years of individual expertise in chamber management, strategic planning, business development, advocacy, governance, and leadership development.
Access to appropriate infrastructure to support hybrid (online and in-person) delivery.
Established capacity to administer, and award formally recognized professional certification programs.
Demonstrated experience managing alumni networks, continuing professional development programs, or professional membership communities.
