Job Description:
Position Overview
As Lafiya grows from roughly 25 staff today to a projected 45 by December, we're building our IT function
We're looking for a hands-on IT Generalist to build this out and then run it day to day: specifying and procuring devices, standing up basic cybersecurity controls, and being the person staff go to when something breaks.
Your first major deliverable is to equip and secure the organisation ahead of our all-staff retreat in December: defining device specifications for different roles, building and securing sign-off on a procurement budget, and getting hardware into people's hands in time.
From there, you'll own IT support day to day, managing user accounts and provisioning as staff join and leave, administering our subscriptions and platforms (Slack, SurveyCTO, Personio, Airtable, Capsule, Squarespace, Xero, Claude, Microsoft Excel, and others), teaching staff to use new platforms during onboarding, and troubleshooting issues as they come up. You'll also lead a cybersecurity assessment of where we stand today and put the right controls in place.
This is a generalist role for someone who does the work themselves rather than managing a team: you'll be equally comfortable scoping a device procurement budget, configuring MFA, and walking a non-technical colleague through a password reset.
What You'll Do
Device & Infrastructure:
Build and maintain device specifications for different types of staff roles
Build and get sign-off on device procurement budgets, in coordination with the COO and Finance
Source, procure, and configure staff and Lafiya Sister devices
Establish a device inventory and replacement/refresh cycle
Cybersecurity:
Lead an organisation-wide cybersecurity assessment of our current tools, devices, and practices
Design and implement baseline security controls (MFA, endpoint protection, password management, access controls) appropriate to Lafiya's size and risk profile that meet ISO 27001 requirements
Draft IT and security policies for staff (acceptable use, device policy, data handling)
Monitor for and respond to security incidents
Lead periodic security awareness trainings
User & Account Management:
Manage staff accounts and system access as staff join, change roles, or leave the organisation
Administer user permissions on Google Workspace, Slack, and other core platforms
Manage software subscriptions and licenses, tracking costs and removing unused seats
IT Support:
Serve as the first point of contact for staff IT issues: troubleshoot hardware, software, connectivity, and account problems
Provide IT onboarding for new staff (device setup, account provisioning, platform access)
Document common issues and solutions to build institutional knowledge over time
Systems Strategy & Adoption:
Identify and pilot new IT systems and tools that could improve organizational productivity, evaluating fit before recommending wider rollout
Lead organization-wide rollout of adopted systems, including training and change management to build staff buy-in
Monitor adoption after rollout and troubleshoot the gap between a system being deployed and a system actually being used
Support other departments' migrations to new platforms they've selected (e.g., a new CRM for Growth), including data migration, system integration, and access setup, as needed
Field & Systems Support:
Oversee the distribution and management processes of mobile devices for Lafiya Sisters (our community-based health workers), as needed.
Support the deployment of new organisational systems as Lafiya adopts them (e.g., an electronic Logistics Management Information System (eLMIS)), as needed.
Who You Are
You're someone who:
Is a true IT generalist. Comfortable moving between hardware procurement, user support, systems administration, and security without needing to hand off to a specialist.
Communicates clearly with non-technical staff. You can walk a colleague through an MFA setup or a password reset without jargon or frustration on either side.
Thinks in risk, acts practically. You understand cybersecurity principles like least privilege and defense in depth, but you know how to phase implementation to fit a small nonprofit's budget and capacity, not gold-plate it.
Builds systems from scratch. You're comfortable creating structure where none exists yet: device specs, onboarding/offboarding checklists, security policies.
Is responsive and reliable. Staff need timely support when something breaks; you treat that as core to the job, not an interruption to it.
Works autonomously. You report to a non-technical supervisor and won't have an IT team around you; you're comfortable making technical judgment calls and flagging the ones that need sign-off.
Delivers on deadlines. The device rollout has a hard date tied to a company-wide retreat; you can manage a time-bound project without dropping day-to-day support in the meantime.
Is flexible. You are comfortable working across multiple countries and time zones.
Education, Experience & Skills
Bachelor's Degree or HND in Computer Science, Information Systems, IT, or a related field; or equivalent practical experience and relevant certifications.
3–5 years of experience in IT support or systems administration, ideally as a generalist in a small organisation or NGO context
Experience managing a device fleet of 20+ devices (Windows and/or Mac) for a small-to-midsize organisation is mandatory
Experience administering Google Workspace user accounts and permissions is mandatory
Experience administering Slack or similar collaboration platforms, including license/subscription management
A recognized cybersecurity certification (e.g., CompTIA Security+, ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity, or equivalent) plus demonstrated experience implementing baseline security controls (MFA, endpoint protection, access management, patch management) is mandatory. This function will only grow in importance as Lafiya scales, so we're prioritizing candidates who can show real security credentials, not just familiarity.
Experience conducting or supporting a cybersecurity risk assessment is a plus
Experience with mobile device management (MDM) or endpoint management tools (e.g., Google Endpoint Management, Jamf, Intune) is a plus
Vendor management experience (device suppliers, ISPs, SaaS vendors) is a plus
Professional fluency in English is mandatory
You don't need to check every box here. If this role excites you and you meet the mandatory qualifications, we'd love to hear from you.
Why should you apply:
You will be joining an ambitious and supportive organisation that is growing quickly.
We are serious about impact and serious about investing in our people.
There will be room to take initiative, make decisions, and leave your mark on a critical stage of Lafiya’s growth.
We don’t have layers of approval or slow processes, so if something makes sense, we’ll try it.
Benefits
Benefits include:
40 days of combined holiday and paid annual leave.
Paid parental leave.
Flexibility in where, when and how you work.
Working closely with a team of senior leaders who are collaborative, ambitious and serious about impact.
HMO insurance cover via AXA, travel reimbursements.
Annual team retreat with all expenses paid.

We are seeking a Principal Offshore Structural Engineer to provide offshore civil/structural engineering expertise and support the HA & HB-Buko projects.
These projects aim to deliver approximately 350-450 MMscf/d of gas to the NLNG Train-7 from 2029+, as well as 25-30 kb/d of oil and condensate for export.
The role involves providing technical input and assurance throughout the project lifecycle, from conceptual and FEED through detailed design, procurement, construction, installation, and commissioning, to safeguard design, technical, and operational integrity.
Responsibilities
Ensure engineering design, procurement, fabrication, construction, and installation are done in compliance with standards, project objectives, HSSE, and contractual requirements.
Define civil/structural scope of work, specifications, and requirements as part of ITT packages, applying systems engineering and requirements management best practices.
Perform technical studies and carry out structural analysis and design using SACS and other civil/structural design software.
Provide discipline expertise to manage contractor delivery of design and specialist work in line with project cost, schedule, quality, and HSSE requirements.
Review and provide technical assurance to FEED and detailed design deliverables.
Define geotechnical investigation work scope and perform foundation design.
Supervise and assure quality of fabrication and site construction works.
Drive innovative solutions to achieve economic performance requirements and cost efficiency throughout the facilities lifecycle.
Manage multiple technical and non-technical interfaces and stakeholders, and manage technical risk through expert review of deviations to standards.
Provide discipline input at safety workshops and value assurance events such as HAZID, HAZOP, VARs, and peer reviews.
Requirements
Required:
Minimum of a bachelor’s degree in civil or structural engineering.
NSE and COREN membership.
Minimum of 14 years’ experience in civil/structural engineering within the oil and gas industry.
Proficiency in the use of SACS software for offshore structures design.
Knowledge of HSSE frameworks and international engineering standards, best practices, and systems.
Strong team, personal, and people management skills, committed to learning and continuous improvement.
Good communication skills and ability to function effectively in a multi-ethnic, multi-disciplinary environment.
Good leadership, coaching, negotiating, decision-making, and interpersonal skills.
Preferred:
Experience with offshore platforms, FPSOs, or onshore terminals is desirable.
Demonstrable record of successfully delivering structural engineering solutions for new projects and existing asset integrity.
What We Offer
Competitive compensation and benefits package.
Opportunity to work on strategically important projects supporting NLNG Train-7.
Professional development and continuous learning opportunities.
Collaborative and inclusive team culture.
Health and wellbeing support.
Exposure to a wide range of engineering challenges across the project lifecycle.

Job Description:
We are seeking an experienced Payroll Lending Manager – Public Sector to drive the growth and performance of the public-sector payroll lending portfolio.
The successful candidate will be responsible for developing and managing government/MDA partnerships, driving loan origination and disbursement, managing portfolio performance, and ensuring effective check-off deductions, remittance, credit risk management, and regulatory compliance.
The role requires strong stakeholder and relationship management skills, particularly within government and public-sector environments, as well as the willingness to travel extensively across Nigeria.
Key Responsibilities
Lending Growth & Strategic Partnerships:
Build, onboard, and manage relationships with government MDAs, payroll administrators, employers, corporates, and SMEs to establish and sustain salary deduction and check-off arrangements.
Drive loan origination, disbursement volumes, and portfolio growth across public and private-sector segments in line with approved targets and risk appetite.
Identify and develop new MDA mandates, employer partnerships, and business development opportunities to expand the payroll lending pipeline.
Collaborate with Sales, Business Development, Credit, Risk, and other relevant teams to drive portfolio growth.
Develop and maintain strong relationships with key public-sector stakeholders to support business growth and protect existing lending arrangements.
Underwriting, Deduction & Loan Management:
Develop and continuously improve underwriting criteria for public and private-sector borrowers, considering factors such as grade level, years to retirement, deduction limits, employer standing, industry risk, employment tenure, income verification, and deduction reliability.
Coordinate with government payroll platforms and employer HR/payroll teams to validate employment status, salary, deduction consent, and ongoing remittance.
Monitor deduction and remittance performance and promptly resolve issues relating to non-remittance, partial remittance, or deduction stoppages.
Track employment changes, including redeployment, promotion, transfer, retirement, resignation, termination, and change of employer, to minimise repayment disruptions and portfolio delinquency.
Manage repayment transitions where payroll deductions cease, including moving affected accounts to direct collection arrangements where required.
Portfolio Risk, Compliance & Recovery:
Monitor government policies, public-sector pay structures, employer restructuring, salary delays, financial distress, and other risk indicators that may affect portfolio performance.
Adjust lending exposure where necessary based on emerging portfolio and employer-level risks.
Own portfolio quality across the payroll lending book, including Portfolio-at-Risk (PAR) and Non-Performing Loan (NPL) performance.
Drive appropriate remedial, collections, and recovery actions on delinquent accounts.
Work closely with Legal, Compliance, Credit, and Risk teams to ensure lending activities, deduction arrangements, and employer partnerships comply with applicable regulatory and internal requirements.
Maintain an appropriate balance between portfolio growth, credit quality, risk management, and regulatory compliance.
Stakeholder & Relationship Management:
Maintain effective relationships with MDA officials, government payroll administrators, pension administrators, treasury officials, employer HR/payroll teams, and other relevant stakeholders.
Protect existing deduction arrangements and identify opportunities for portfolio expansion.
Proactively resolve stakeholder, operational, payroll, deduction, and remittance-related issues that could affect loan repayment or portfolio performance.
Navigate complex public-sector and government stakeholder environments while maintaining strong professional relationships.
Reporting & Performance Management:
Prepare periodic management reports covering loan origination, disbursement, portfolio growth, PAR, NPL, remittance rates, MDA mandates, employer partnerships, and other key portfolio indicators.
Track loan approval and disbursement turnaround times and drive improvements against agreed service and performance targets.
Monitor portfolio performance against agreed growth, quality, and operational targets.
Provide management with actionable insights on portfolio performance, emerging risks, deduction trends, and business growth opportunities.
Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.
6–10 years of experience in consumer or retail lending, with demonstrable exposure to public-sector, payroll, or check-off lending.
Proven experience managing a lending portfolio and driving portfolio growth and performance.
Strong understanding of public-sector payroll/check-off lending, deduction, and remittance structures.
Established working relationships with government payroll platforms such as IPPIS, SIFMIS, state equivalents, or MDA payroll units is strongly preferred.
Experience managing lending portfolios through changes in government administration or public-sector policies is an advantage.
Strong credit assessment, underwriting, portfolio management, and analytical skills.
Strong portfolio analytics and performance reporting capabilities.
Proficiency with loan management systems and reporting tools.
Experience in fintech, consumer lending, or digital credit operations is highly preferred.
Relevant professional certification in credit, risk, banking, finance, or a related discipline is an advantage.
CIBN, RIMAN, ICAN, or equivalent certification is an added advantage.
Strong stakeholder management skills, particularly within government, public-sector, and union environments.
Strong negotiation and relationship management skills.
Demonstrated experience driving lending growth, portfolio improvement, or operational transformation initiatives.
Strong regulatory and business awareness, with the resilience and adaptability required to operate in complex public-sector environments.
Strong ownership, judgement, and follow-through.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet portfolio targets.
Willingness and ability to travel extensively across Nigeria.
What We’re Looking For:
The ideal candidate should have strong experience in public-sector payroll or check-off lending, with the ability to build and maintain government/MDA relationships while managing lending growth, portfolio quality, deductions, and remittances.
You should be commercially driven, highly organised, and comfortable navigating complex stakeholder and regulatory environments while maintaining strong portfolio performance.
Note
: Growth Bonus is involved.

Job Description:
The Electrical Technician is responsible for installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing electrical systems and equipment to ensure optimal functionality and safety across the facility.
Key Responsibilities
Ability to Install, connect, commission, and maintain three-phase electric motors.
Ability to Diagnose and troubleshoot motor faults, including electrical and control-circuit problems.
Carry out routine and preventive maintenance on motors and associated equipment.
Troubleshoot and maintain Direct-On-Line (DOL), Star-Delta, and other motor starting systems.

Good understanding of motor alignment, coupling checks, and identification of mechanical conditions that may affect motor performance.

Maintain accurate records of motor inspections, faults, repairs, tests, and maintenance activities.
Carry out emergency breakdown repairs and respond promptly to equipment failures.
Work closely with mechanical, production, and engineering teams to minimize equipment downtime.
Recommend replacement of defective components and identify potential electrical problems before they result in equipment failure.
Test motor windings, insulation resistance, continuity, phase balance, and other electrical parameters.
Ensure all electrical work complies with applicable safety procedures, standards, and company requirements.
Ability to be able to work under pressure and to work extra hours if need be.
Qualifications and Skills:
OND/HND/B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering or a related field.
Minimum of 2–3 years’ experience in electrical maintenance (industrial or manufacturing preferred).
Strong knowledge of electrical systems, wiring, motors, and control panels.
Ability to read and interpret electrical diagrams and technical manuals.
Good troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
Understanding of safety protocols and procedures.
Strong attention to detail and ability to work under minimal supervision.

Responsibilities

Provide support and build capacity of LGA and health facility M&E officers in data quality management
Participate and provide technical support in monthly LGA data validation meetings.

Deep understanding and knowledge of M&E systems in Nigeria and/or comparable country contexts.
Familiarity with data validation tools
Excellent knowledge of use of DHIS2
Excellent computer skills, including in Excel and in at least one statistical software package, preferably Stata, alternatively SPSS or R; knowledge of other data software an advantage, such as mapping software

Deep understanding and knowledge of health systems’ dynamics and challenges in data management
Excellent spoken and written English
Excellent report writing skills
Ability to work under pressure, flexible and open to extra working hours, if necessary.
Very good negotiation and communication skills and ability to express views and ideas.

flexibility, and overall positive attitude.
A neat and professional appearance.
Undertake irregular work schedules, long trips and be ready to perform in short
notice for assignment of a trip.

Availability to travel domestically.
Driving for extended periods of time.
Ability to lift up to 20kg.

People Planning and Alignment - Support the implementation of Africa Regional and Capability HR strategies by
developing and executing HR plans that align with business priorities. Ensure HR activities are integrated, operationally effective, and contribute to business objectives.
Talent Attraction & Onboarding - Implement talent acquisition and onboarding frameworks, policies, and practices to support workforce needs. Partner with the Regional Talent Acquisition CoE and HR Operations tonensure recruitment and onboarding processes are delivered efficiently, consistently, and in line with policy.
Learning, Development and Talent Management - Conduct learning needs analysis and implementing learning and development programmes to facilitate employees’ growth and capability building. Implement DP World talent management frameworks to balance workforce demand and supply by implementing programs that identify, develop, review, and retain critical skills while proactively managing talent-related risks.

Additionally, implement total rewards solutions and practices that align with DP World policies, and procedures, ensuring consistent, fair, and compliant application across the Business Unit.
Organisational Design and Change Management - Support organizational design implementation in alignment with DP World OD principles and frameworks to ensure effectiveness and alignment with Business Unit priorities. Support, guide, and manage change within Business Unit from a people, process and technology perspective.
Culture, Employee Engagement and Well-Being - Implement HR initiatives that drive the DP World culture and enhance employee experience, engagement, inclusion, and wellbeing. Work with CoEs and HR Operations to operationalize programs and practices that are consistent, compliant, and effectively implemented.
Employee Relations, HR Governance, Compliance - Manage employee relations to support, enhance, and strengthen the relationship between employees, their representatives, and the Company. Uphold HR governance, compliance, and ethical standards across all people practices, ensuring all HR solutions and services are delivered in accordance with legislative, regulatory, and organizational requirements.
HR Data, Reporting, Analytics and Technology - Leverage HR data, reporting, and analytics to provide actionable insights and inform business and HR decision-making. Implement, and optimize relevant HR technology solutions, ensuring systems effectively enable HR service delivery, data integrity, and operational efficiency.
Business Partnering and Stakeholder Collaboration - Partner with business leaders to implement HR strategies and programs that support operational objectives and workforce needs. Facilitate adoption of HR initiatives and contribute to business performance through effective planning and execution. Work collaboratively with HR Centers of Excellence and HR Operations to co-create and implement professional, standardized HR solutions that are efficient, scalable, and aligned with business needs.

Experience working with HR Centers of Excellence and HR Operations to implement consistent, scalable, and compliant HR practices.

Job Description:
Job Summary
We are seeking a highly analytical and detail-oriented QA Engineer to join our Technology team and take ownership of the quality assurance process across our fintech products and digital platforms.
The QA Engineer will be responsible for testing and validating lending workflows, credit systems, payment transactions, APIs, POS solutions, mobile and web applications, and third-party integrations to ensure that our products are reliable, secure, scalable, and provide a seamless customer experience.
The successful candidate will work closely with Software Engineers,Credit, Operations, Customer Service, and other stakeholders to identify defects, prevent production issues, improve testing processes, and ensure that products meet business and technical requirements before deployment.
Key Responsibilities
Product & Functional Testing:
Develop and execute comprehensive test plans, test cases, test scenarios, and test scripts for fintech products.
Perform functional, regression, integration, system, usability, exploratory, and end-to-end testing.
Test new features, product enhancements, bug fixes, and system changes before deployment.
Validate that products function according to approved business requirements and acceptance criteria.
Conduct cross-browser, cross-device, and responsive testing for web and mobile applications.
Identify edge cases and scenarios that could result in financial, operational, or customer-impacting issues.
Lending & Credit System Testing:
Test the complete loan lifecycle, including: Customer onboarding., KYC and profile creation, Loan application, Eligibility assessment, Credit scoring.
Credit decisioning.
Loan approval/rejection.
Offer generation.
Loan disbursement.
Repayment scheduling.
Repayment processing.
Loan restructuring and modifications.
Delinquency and overdue management.
Loan closure.
Validate credit rules, eligibility criteria, loan limits, interest calculations, fees, penalties, repayment schedules, and other lending parameters.
Test different customer profiles and loan scenarios to ensure accurate credit decisions.
Verify that approved loan amounts and repayment obligations are accurately reflected across relevant systems.
Identify discrepancies between loan records, customer balances, transaction records, and accounting/reconciliation systems.
Test negative scenarios, including duplicate applications, failed disbursements, failed repayments, partial payments, reversals, and duplicate transactions.
Payments & Transaction Testing:
Test payment initiation, processing, confirmation, failure, reversal, refund, and reconciliation workflows.
Validate payment transactions across different payment channels and providers.
Test transaction status updates and ensure accurate synchronization between internal systems and third-party payment platforms.
Verify that successful and failed transactions are correctly reflected in customer wallets, loan accounts, and transaction histories.
Test scenarios involving:
Duplicate transactions.
Failed transactions.
Timeout transactions.
Reversed transactions.
Partial payments.
Overpayments.
Underpayments.
Incorrect transaction references.
Ensure financial transactions maintain data integrity and accuracy throughout the transaction lifecycle.
API & Integration Testing:
Design and execute API test cases using tools such as Postman or equivalent platforms.
Validate REST APIs, request/response structures, status codes, authentication, authorization, and error handling.
Test integrations between internal systems and external service providers.
Validate data passed between lending, payment, credit, customer, POS, and other systems.
Conduct positive and negative API testing.
Verify API response times, reliability, data consistency, and appropriate error messages.
Identify integration failures and work with developers to troubleshoot and resolve issues.
POS Testing:
Test POS onboarding, activation, assignment, and transaction workflows.
Validate POS payment transactions and transaction status updates.
Test successful, failed, reversed, and declined POS transactions.
Validate transaction limits, settlement processes, and transaction records.
Test communication between POS devices, backend services, payment processors, and customer accounts.
Verify that POS transactions are accurately reflected in relevant dashboards and reports.
Support investigation of POS-related production issues.
Mobile & Web Application Testing:
Perform functional and usability testing across mobile and web applications.
Test customer registration, authentication, login, password reset, profile management, loan applications, repayments, payments, notifications, and transaction history.
Test application behaviour across different browsers, operating systems, screen sizes, and supported devices.
Validate user interfaces against approved product designs and requirements.
Identify usability issues that may affect customer adoption or product experience.
Defect Management:
Identify, document, classify, and track software defects using tools such as
Jira
or similar platforms.
Provide clear reproduction steps, screenshots/logs, expected results, and actual results when reporting defects.
Prioritize defects based on severity and business/customer impact.
Work closely with developers to investigate and resolve defects.
Retest resolved defects and conduct regression testing to ensure fixes have not introduced new issues.
Monitor recurring defects and recommend preventive measures.
Automation & Continuous Testing:
Develop and maintain automated test scripts for critical product workflows.
Identify suitable test cases for automation, particularly repetitive and high-risk financial transactions.
Support the implementation and maintenance of automated testing frameworks.
Integrate automated tests into CI/CD pipelines where applicable.
Continuously improve test coverage and reduce reliance on repetitive manual testing.
Security, Data & Performance Testing:
Conduct basic security testing to identify vulnerabilities in applications and APIs.
Validate authentication, authorization, session management, and access controls.
Ensure that sensitive customer and financial information is appropriately handled.
Conduct basic performance and load testing on critical systems where required.
Identify system bottlenecks, slow API responses, and performance issues that could affect customers or transaction processing.
Release & Production Support:
Participate in sprint planning, backlog refinement, daily stand-ups, and other Agile ceremonies.
Review requirements and acceptance criteria before development begins.
Provide QA input during product development to identify potential risks early.
Perform pre-release testing and provide QA sign-off before production deployment.
Monitor newly released features and support post-release validation.
Investigate production incidents and work with relevant teams to determine root causes.
Maintain proper documentation of test results, release status, defects, and quality reports.
Qualifications & Experience
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field.
2–4 years of experience in Software Quality Assurance, Software Testing, or a related role.
Experience testing fintech, banking, lending, payments, e-commerce, or other transaction-based applications is highly desirable.
Experience testing both web and mobile applications.
Experience with API testing and third-party integrations.
Strong understanding of SDLC and STLC.
Good understanding of Agile/Scrum methodologies.
Experience working with development and product teams in an Agile environment.

Job Summary
We are seeking a responsible, reliable, safety-conscious, and professional Junior Driver to provide safe and efficient transportation support for the organization.
The successful candidate will be responsible for driving assigned vehicles, transporting staff, executives, clients, documents, and other authorized items as required, maintaining vehicles in good operating condition, observing all traffic laws and safety procedures, and ensuring timely arrival at assigned destinations.
The ideal candidate must have practical driving experience and be comfortable driving both automatic and manual vehicles.
The candidate must have a strong knowledge and understanding of Abuja routes, major roads, districts, landmarks, alternative routes, traffic patterns, and commonly used destinations within Abuja.
The successful candidate should demonstrate punctuality, good judgment, professionalism, discretion, basic vehicle maintenance awareness, excellent road safety practices, and the ability to work responsibly with minimal supervision.
Key Responsibilities
Driving & Transportation:
Safely operate assigned vehicles for authorized official duties.
Drive both automatic and manual vehicles confidently and responsibly.
Transport staff, management, clients, visitors, documents, equipment, and other authorized items as required.
Ensure passengers arrive at their destinations safely, comfortably, and on time.
Follow assigned schedules, routes, destinations, and transportation instructions.
Plan journeys appropriately to allow for traffic, road conditions, weather, and other possible delays.
Demonstrate flexibility when routes, schedules, or transportation requirements change.
Provide transportation support for meetings, official appointments, business visits, airport transfers, errands, and other approved activities.
Remain available and responsive during assigned working periods.
Ensure all journeys are conducted professionally and in accordance with organizational requirements.
Abuja Route & Navigation Knowledge:
Demonstrate strong knowledge of Abuja roads, districts, neighborhoods, landmarks, business areas, government offices, residential areas, hotels, airports, and other commonly visited locations.
Navigate efficiently across Abuja and identify suitable alternative routes where necessary.
Stay informed about traffic conditions, road closures, construction, diversions, and other factors that may affect travel time.
Use approved navigation tools such as Google Maps or other GPS applications when required.
Understand major Abuja routes and connections between key districts.
Demonstrate the ability to reach unfamiliar destinations using available navigation tools.
Minimize unnecessary delays by selecting safe and efficient routes.
Provide reasonable route guidance when requested.
Vehicle Safety & Maintenance:
Conduct basic pre-trip and post-trip vehicle checks.
Check fuel level, tyres, lights, brakes, engine condition, fluids, wipers, mirrors, and other essential vehicle components.
Keep assigned vehicles clean, presentable, and in good condition.
Report mechanical faults, unusual sounds, warning lights, tyre issues, accidents, or other vehicle concerns promptly.
Ensure vehicles are serviced and maintained according to approved schedules.
Monitor fuel consumption and report unusual or excessive usage.
Ensure the vehicle contains required safety and emergency items where applicable.
Keep vehicle documents, insurance information, inspection records, and other required documentation properly maintained.
Do not operate a vehicle that appears unsafe or unfit for use and promptly report any safety concerns.
Ensure personal belongings and organizational property are handled responsibly while using the vehicle.
Road Safety & Compliance:
Observe all applicable traffic laws, road signs, speed limits, and driving regulations.
Maintain safe driving practices at all times.
Avoid reckless, aggressive, distracted, or dangerous driving.
Do not use a mobile phone in a manner that compromises driving safety.
Always use seat belts and ensure passengers comply with applicable safety requirements.
Exercise additional caution in heavy traffic, poor weather, unfamiliar areas, and difficult road conditions.
Maintain appropriate speed and safe following distances.
Report traffic incidents, accidents, vehicle damage, or other road-related issues immediately.
Cooperate appropriately with relevant authorities following an accident or traffic incident.
Never drive under the influence of alcohol or any substance that may impair driving ability.
Maintain a professional and safety-conscious attitude on the road.
Staff & Passenger Support:
Provide courteous, respectful, and professional service to passengers.
Assist passengers with loading and unloading reasonable luggage or official items where required.
Maintain punctuality for staff pickups, appointments, meetings, and scheduled trips.
Confirm pickup and drop-off locations where necessary.
Maintain confidentiality regarding passenger movements, conversations, schedules, and organizational activities.
Respect the privacy and personal space of passengers.
Communicate professionally with staff, management, clients, visitors, vendors, and other stakeholders.
Maintain a calm and respectful attitude even under traffic pressure or challenging circumstances.
Administrative & Errand Support:
Support authorized administrative, logistics, and operational errands.
Collect and deliver documents, parcels, equipment, supplies, and other approved items.
Assist with bank runs, office errands, procurement-related transportation, and other assigned duties where required.
Maintain proper records of assigned trips and official journeys where required.
Submit receipts, fuel records, parking records, toll information, and other relevant documentation as requested.
Follow all organizational procedures relating to vehicle use, transportation, expenses, and official errands.
Support the Administration, Operations, Logistics, or other relevant teams with transportation-related activities.
Vehicle Documentation & Reporting:
Ensure assigned vehicle documentation is properly maintained and available.
Monitor vehicle service dates, insurance, roadworthiness, registration, and other applicable requirements.
Report vehicle mileage and usage as required.
Maintain accurate trip, fuel, maintenance, and other vehicle-related records where applicable.
Immediately report accidents, damage, traffic violations, mechanical issues, or other incidents involving the assigned vehicle.
Provide management with relevant information regarding vehicle condition and transportation activities.
Ensure all vehicle-related documents and records are properly handled and submitted when required.
Professional Conduct & Confidentiality:
Maintain a high level of professionalism when representing the organization.
Maintain confidentiality regarding company operations, management activities, client information, locations, schedules, and other sensitive matters.
Demonstrate honesty, integrity, reliability, and accountability.
Avoid unauthorized use of company or assigned vehicles.
Do not transport unauthorized passengers or items using organizational vehicles.
Follow instructions from authorized supervisors and management.
Maintain appropriate appearance and personal hygiene while on duty.
Treat colleagues, clients, visitors, and members of the public respectfully.
Protect organizational property and use vehicles and other resources responsibly.
Key Performance Areas
Performance in this role will be assessed based on:
Safe and responsible driving.
Punctuality and timely arrival at assigned destinations.
Knowledge and effective navigation of Abuja routes.
Ability to drive automatic and manual vehicles.
Vehicle cleanliness and presentation.
Proper vehicle care and maintenance reporting.
Compliance with traffic laws and organizational driving policies.
Reliability and availability for assigned duties.
Professional conduct when interacting with staff, clients, and visitors.
Accurate handling of official documents, items, and deliveries.
Proper fuel and vehicle usage.
Timely reporting of vehicle faults, accidents, and incidents.
Passenger satisfaction and quality of transportation support.
Proper completion of assigned transportation and administrative tasks.
Overall contribution to efficient transportation and operational support.

Education: Minimum of SSCE/WAEC/NECO; OND, NCE, HND, or equivalent qualification is an advantage.

Job Description:
The Role
We are looking for an experienced Business Analyst with a strong foundation in accounting, finance, financial analysis, or financial services to join our team.
The role combines hands-on business analysis and project delivery with the opportunity to lead and mentor a small team of Business Analysts. The ideal candidate will be comfortable working at the intersection of business, finance, data, and technology, with the ability to understand complex financial processes, translate business needs into practical system requirements, and work closely with technical teams to deliver effective solutions.
The successful candidate should have a genuine interest in financial modelling, financial analysis, data interpretation, and process improvement, and be able to apply these skills when analysing business requirements and developing solutions.
Working closely with stakeholders—including clients, project managers, QA, IT development teams, and senior leadership—you will lead requirements gathering, create and prioritise Agile user stories, oversee solution delivery and user acceptance testing, and contribute to the long-term development of our products and services.
Key Responsibilities
Lead, mentor, and support a small team of Business Analysts, providing guidance, coaching, and performance feedback.
Work with clients and internal stakeholders to capture, analyse, refine, and prioritise business and financial requirements.
Analyse existing business processes, financial workflows, systems, and data to identify gaps, inefficiencies, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
Translate complex business and financial requirements into clear functional requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, process flows, and other relevant documentation.
Oversee the delivery of multiple projects, including process improvements, software implementations, system enhancements, data migrations, reconciliations, and financial or data-focused projects.
Own and manage prioritised product backlogs, define user stories, and work with development teams to ensure the timely delivery of new features, enhancements, and fixes.
Apply financial and analytical thinking to support the design of systems, processes, reports, calculations, and business rules.
Develop, review, or contribute to financial models, forecasts, analytical models, and financial reporting requirements where relevant to projects.
Analyse financial data and business information to support decision-making, identify trends, validate assumptions, and ensure the accuracy of system outputs.
Lead or coordinate User Acceptance Testing (UAT), including test planning, scenario development, defect identification, resolution tracking, and sign-off.
Validate system calculations, financial outputs, reports, reconciliations, and data integrity against agreed business requirements.
Act as a key liaison between business stakeholders and technical teams, ensuring effective communication and alignment throughout the project lifecycle.
Essential Requirements
Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business, Information Technology, or a related discipline.
Significant experience working as a Business Analyst, Financial Analyst, Management Accountant, Business Systems Analyst, or in a similar analytical role, preferably within financial services.
Strong understanding of accounting and financial principles, with the ability to understand and analyse financial processes, transactions, reports, and data.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work with complex financial and business data.
Experience working with software development or technology teams and translating business requirements into actionable technical requirements.
Strong experience with Agile methodologies, including backlog management, user story definition, prioritisation, and acceptance criteria.
Strong ability to produce high-quality functional documentation, process maps, business rules, and other business analysis artefacts.
Nice to Have:
Experience in insurance, reinsurance, financial services, or the London Market, particularly Lloyd's-related systems and processes.
Professional qualification or progress towards a qualification such as ACCA, ACA, CIMA, CFA, or a relevant financial/accounting qualification.
Experience developing or working extensively with financial models, forecasting models, pricing models, investment models, or financial planning tools.
Strong Excel skills, including experience with advanced formulas, PivotTables, financial modelling, data analysis, and reporting.
Experience working with financial reporting, accounting systems, ERP systems, or financial data platforms.
Experience with data migration, reconciliation, data validation, and financial data integrity.
Proactive approach, with the ability to build strong, trusted relationships quickly.
Why Join Us
At our core, we believe in delivering excellence while fostering a collaborative and supportive environment. Joining our team means working on high-impact projects in the global insurance and reinsurance sector, with opportunities to shape products used across multiple markets.
You’ll enjoy the autonomy to make a real difference, the support of an experienced leadership team, and a culture that values innovation, growth, and work-life balance.

Company Details:
May & Baker, Nigeria Plc was founded on September 4, 1944 as Nigeria’s first pharmaceutical company. It has its origin in England, the United Kingdom where in 1834, three chemists founded Grimwade, May & Pickett, a firm for manufacturing chemicals for pharmaceutical products. In 1839...read moreGrimwade, May & Pickett transformed into May & Baker United Kingdom Limited following some changes in the ownership. May & Baker UK Limited transformed into a mega European conglomerate through a web of mergers and acquisitions over years. Consequently the name of the company has changed at different times and today, only the Nigerian offshoot is known by the original name. 

In Nigeria the company started as May & Baker (West Africa) Limited at 17A Tinubu Street, Lagos in 1944, a trading outpost to serve the West Coast of Africa. The company relocated to its present site at Ikeja, Lagos state during the Nigerian civil war. In 1976, it built its factory at Ikeja where it began local manufacturing of pharmaceuticals. That same year it changed from May & Baker (West Africa) Limited to May & Baker Nigeria Limited

In 1979, following the indigenisation decree which required that foreign interests in companies operating in Nigeria be of a minority nature, May & Baker, United Kingdom relinquished 60 per cent of its equity holding in May & Baker Nigeria to Nigerians while retaining 40 per cent. The company’s name was changed to Embechem Nigeria Limited but this was dropped later and the name reverted to May & Baker Nigeria Limited.

May & Baker Nigeria Limited became a publicly quoted company following its listing by introduction on the Nigerian Stock Exchange on November 10, 1994 and became May & Baker Nigeria Plc.

For many years expatriates sent by the parent company managed May & Baker Nigeria but in 1997, the first indigenous Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Joseph Ikemefuna Odumodu, was appointed.

In 2002 the foreign partners decided to divest. However, represented by Aventis SA, France, they remained technical associates of May & Baker Nigeria Plc. Following the merger of Aventis and Sanofi, another French firm to form Sanofi Aventis in 2004, the technical relationship transferred between May & Baker Nigeria Plc and Sanofi-Aventis of France. But that relationship was renegotiated in 2005 to give May & Baker Nigeria, the leeway to have its own products.

The company thereby began an aggressive expansion and diversification programme since 2005 which has culminated in the creation of new businesses and subsidiaries. In 2005, Biovaccines, a local vaccine production subsidiary was set up in partnership with the Federal Government of Nigeria. In 2006, the company constructed a multi-billion naira food processing factory, constructed a local plant for the production of anti-retroviral drugs in Nigeria while the construction of a World Health Organization Standard Pharmaceutical production facility was constructed and commissioned on June 27, 2011

Job Description:
We are looking for an Antenatal Risk Stratification (ARS) Technical Consultant to provide clinical and research expertise in the review, expansion, validation, and digitization of its Antenatal Risk Stratification tool.
The consultant will lead the technical and clinical refinement of the tool, expanding its application beyond antenatal care to include the postnatal, newborn, and non-pregnant periods.
The role will work closely with clinical, programme, data, product, and technology teams to ensure the tool is evidence-based, scientifically rigorous, ethically sound, and accurately translated into a digital product.
Responsibilities
Review and refine the existing ARS tool, including its questions, risk classification logic, clinical recommendations, and referral pathways.
Expand the tool beyond antenatal risk assessment to appropriately assess risks during the postnatal period, newborn period, and non-pregnant state.
Ensure that the expanded tool and its clinical logic are aligned with appropriate clinical guidelines and evidence.
Design the validation approach for the tool, including methodology, study design, sampling approach, testing procedures, data requirements, outcomes, and analysis framework.
Lead the preparation and submission of the ethical approval application, including development of the required research protocol and supporting documentation, and manage responses/revisions required through the approval process.
Provide technical leadership for testing and validation of the tool, working with the program, clinical, data, and implementation teams to ensure the process is scientifically and ethically sound.
Develop the research methodology and scientific documentation arising from the validation work and support preparation of research manuscripts/publications.
Support the digitization of the ARS tool, working with the product and technology teams to ensure that the approved clinical questions, algorithms, risk classifications, recommendations, and workflows are correctly translated into the digital product.
Review findings from testing and implementation and recommend evidence-based modifications to the tool where required.
Provide ongoing technical input to the program team on maternal, postnatal, newborn, and women's health risk stratification as required during the consultancy.
Requirements
Medical degree with significant clinical experience; Obstetrics & Gynaecology or a related maternal/newborn health specialty is strongly preferred.
7+ years of relevant clinical and/or public health experience, with strong expertise in maternal and newborn health.
Demonstrated experience in clinical research, study design, research methodology, and scientific writing.
Strong understanding of research ethics and IRB/ethical approval processes, including preparation of research protocols and ethics applications.
Experience designing or supporting the validation of clinical tools, decision-support tools, screening tools, or risk-stratification models.
Strong ability to interpret clinical evidence and translate it into practical clinical algorithms, recommendations, and referral pathways.
Experience working collaboratively with clinical, programme, data, product, and technology teams.
Strong scientific writing skills, including experience developing research reports, manuscripts, abstracts, or publications.
Excellent analytical, communication, and stakeholder-management skills.
Ability to work independently and deliver clearly defined outputs within a short, deliverables-based engagement.
Benefits
This role is on a short term contract basis and offers a competitive pay and other benefits and perks.

Team Leadership
Lead, organize, and supervise the electrical assurance team, allocating engineers across contractor packages and project areas to match site progress.

Technical Assurance

Validate project progress and provide technical input into contractor interim and final account certification, including evaluation of variation claims relating to electrical scope.
Identify technical risks, non-conformities, and quality concerns.
Prepare and review assurance reports, audit findings, and monthly progress reports.
Support schedule and procurement-compliance reviews within the electrical discipline as part of IPMC's wider audit mandate.

Bachelor's degree (minimum) in Electrical Engineering, Electrical & Electronics Engineering, Power Engineering, or a related discipline; a Master's degree is an advantage.
Minimum 12 years of relevant post-qualification experience, including demonstrated time in a lead or supervisory capacity, on industrial, oil & gas, petrochemical, refinery, fertilizer, power generation, transmission, or major infrastructure projects.
Professional registration such as COREN, PE, CEng, or an equivalent international body.

PMP, ISO 9001 Lead Auditor, NEBOSH, IEEE Senior Membership, Electrical Safety Certification, Protection & Control Certification, or equivalent.

Strong leadership and people-management skills, with a track record of developing and motivating a technical team.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, comfortable producing client-facing reports and presenting findings to senior stakeholders.
Cultural adaptability and the interpersonal skills to work effectively within a Nigerian/West African project environment and multinational team.
High personal integrity and impartiality, consistent with an independent assurance role that certifies payments on the Employer's behalf.

Job Description:
ROLE PURPOSE
The Transformation Manager is the execution backbone of ARM’s Strategy & Transformation function. The role exists to bring structured delivery discipline, rigorous problem-solving, and hands-on execution support to the CEO-prioritised transformation initiatives that underpin ARM’s FY2026 executive scorecard.
This is not a project management role. The holder will diagnose execution bottlenecks, design workable solutions alongside BU teams, drive initiatives through resistance, and hold BU counterparts accountable for delivery — all without line authority. The role demands someone who has both shaped recommendations at consulting-grade standard and landed change inside a real business, with the scars to prove it.
Key Relationships
Head of Strategy & Transformation — line manager; sets transformation priorities and reviews portfolio
BU Managing Directors and initiative sponsors — primary working relationship on active initiatives; the holder operates as the CEO’s execution partner inside BU-owned work
BU initiative leads and workstream owners — day-to-day counterparts for initiative delivery
Group CEO — periodic reporting on transformation portfolio progress; escalation on genuinely stuck items
Strategy team colleagues — integration between strategic direction and transformation execution
Core Responsibilities
Transformation initiative delivery. Own the execution rigor on a CEO-prioritised subset of BU-owned transformation initiatives. This includes structuring the initiative into deliverable workstreams, establishing milestones and tracking cadence, diagnosing execution bottlenecks as they emerge, and driving resolution. The holder does not own the initiative (the BU does) but is accountable for the quality and pace of execution discipline applied to it.
Problem-solving and solution design. When an initiative stalls, the holder diagnoses root cause (whether capability, resourcing, political, or design) and works with BU counterparts to build a workable path forward. This requires consulting-grade problem structuring applied in an operating environment where the holder has no positional authority and cannot simply recommend; they must land.
BU engagement and accountability. Work directly with BU initiative leads and sponsors to maintain momentum. Hold BU counterparts to commitments on timelines, data provision, and resourcing, escalating only when organic traction has been exhausted. The holder’s standing comes from the quality of their contribution and the credibility of their judgment, not from hierarchy.
Portfolio monitoring and reporting. Maintain a clear, honest view of the transformation portfolio — what’s on track, what’s drifting, and what should be escalated or killed. Prepare portfolio updates for the Head of Strategy & Transformation and for CEO-level reviews. The holder is expected to call problems early and honestly, not to present optimistic narratives.
Transformation methodology and tools. Bring and adapt structured transformation approaches — initiative charters, milestone frameworks, risk and dependency tracking, benefits realisation — appropriate to ARM’s operating context. Avoid imposing heavyweight methodology for its own sake; the standard is what accelerates delivery, not what produces the most documentation.
Capability transfer. Build transformation execution capability within BU teams over time. The long-term measure of success is not that the holder is indispensable, but that BU teams are materially more capable of executing change after working with them.
Success Criteria
At 12 months, the holder is expected to have:
Delivered measurable progress on all CEO-prioritised transformation initiatives, with BU sponsors confirming the quality of execution support
Established a functioning transformation portfolio tracking and reporting cadence accepted by the Head of Strategy & Transformation and the CEO
Earned standing with BU MDs and initiative sponsors as a credible execution partner, measured by BU engagement quality, not by volume of deliverables produced
Built a working relationship with the Transformation Analyst that enables delegation of workstream-level execution
Experience and Background
7–8 years of experience combining management consulting and operational/line experience
At least 3 years at a top-tier consulting firm (PwC, EY-Parthenon, Deloitte S&O, KPMG) or equivalent
At least 2 years in a line role, transformation role, or operating role inside a business, not advisory-only
Demonstrated experience delivering transformation or large-scale change initiatives end-to-end, including managing through organisational resistance
Financial services exposure, preferably in asset management, banking, pensions, or adjacent sectors
Direct experience working with senior executives; confident holding ground at MD and C-suite level
Strongly Preferred
Experience in the Nigerian or broader African financial services market
MBA or equivalent postgraduate qualification from a leading institution
Prior experience in a group-centre or shared-services transformation role within a holdco structure

Job Description:
Overview
The Terms of Reference for the consultancy are to review existing legal and policy frameworks related to Gender-Based Violence and develop a community-centred GBV Framework that strengthens the leadership role of community and faith-based women in abolishing harmful social norms and traditional practices in Bokkos and Jos East Local Government Areas of Plateau State.
Description
This term of reference is to identify and engage a consultant or consultancy firm to engage Traditional, religious, and community stakeholders to understand existing laws and develop a gender-based violence (GBV) framework. This will enable structured systemic change and strengthen collective community accountability whilst mobilizing Paramount rulers and key TRC stakeholders to abolish social norms and harmful gender attitudes in Bokkos and Jos East Local Government Areas of Plateau State.
Women for Women International in Nigeria (WfWI-Nigeria) is seeking an experienced gender-based violence “He4She” qualified legal consultant or consultancy firm for a short-term project to engage TRCs in understanding existing laws and to develop a GBV community framework document/manual.
This framework will create a community-led system for the abolition of social norms and traditional practices and strengthen protective mechanisms by empowering local actors to drive lasting behavior and social norm change (from police, traditional and Religious Leaders, wives of traditional/religious leaders, men allies, graduates CSOs, etc.) and mobilize these stakeholders to collectively address violence in two target Local Government Areas (Jos East and Bokkos). By strengthening collective community stakeholder accountability for addressing GBV in the target communities, we anticipate this will lead to changes in social norms and reductions in GBV. This would complement our existing work at the individual and household levels.
The Consultant shall:
Engage with the WfWI project team to understand the project scope, objectives, expectations, methodology, timelines, and deliverables.
Conduct a comprehensive desk review of relevant national, state, and community-level laws, policies, research, GBV frameworks, guidelines, and existing interventions, including relevant traditional and community structures.
Assess the GBV prevention and response landscape in Bokkos and Jos East LGAs, identifying gaps, opportunities, barriers, existing practices, and community structures relevant to GBV prevention and response.
Develop a consultation methodology and facilitate stakeholder consultations and community dialogues with relevant stakeholders, including Paramount Rulers, TRC leaders, women leaders, faith-based leaders, community representatives, and other key stakeholders. The Consultant will gather, analyze, and document stakeholder perspectives and recommendations. WfWI will provide coordination and logistical support, including facilitating access to identified stakeholders and communities.
Analyze findings from the desk review and stakeholder consultations and use the evidence generated to inform the development of the Community-led GBV Prevention Framework.
Design and develop a context-specific Community-led GBV Prevention Framework for Bokkos and Jos East LGAs, incorporating practical strategies for community ownership, sustainability, accountability, leadership engagement, prevention of harmful norms and practices, and community-led action.
Develop recommendations for strengthening women-led advocacy and community action to address harmful gender norms, practices, and other drivers of GBV.
Present preliminary findings and the draft framework to the WfWI team for technical review and discussion, and incorporate relevant feedback.
Facilitate a stakeholder validation process for the draft framework. WfWI will support stakeholder mobilization, invitations, logistics, and coordination of the validation sessions.
Revise and finalize the framework based on stakeholder feedback and validation outcomes, ensuring that the final document is evidence-based, practical, contextually appropriate, locally owned, and implementable.
Present the final Community-led GBV Prevention Framework to WfWI, including key findings, recommendations, and proposed implementation considerations.
Present the final framework at the high-level Paramount Rulers’ Roundtable, providing the technical overview and facilitating discussion towards community leadership and endorsement.
Expected Deliverables
The Consultant is expected to deliver the following:
Inception Report: Outlining the proposed methodology, stakeholder engagement approach, work plan, key activities, deliverables, timelines, and any assumptions or risks identified at the outset of the assignment.
Desk Review Report: Presenting findings from the review and analysis of relevant national, state, and community-level laws, policies, frameworks, guidelines, research, and existing GBV prevention and response mechanisms.
Stakeholder Consultation Report: Documenting the consultation process, stakeholders engaged, key findings, community perspectives, identified gaps and opportunities, and recommendations emerging from the consultations.
Draft Community-led GBV Prevention Framework: A context-specific framework for Bokkos and Jos East LGAs, incorporating practical strategies for community ownership, leadership engagement, accountability, sustainability, prevention of harmful norms and practices, and community-led action.
Validation Workshop Report: Documenting the validation process, participants, key feedback, areas of consensus and concern, and recommendations for strengthening the draft framework.
Final Community-led GBV Prevention Framework: A revised and finalized framework incorporating relevant feedback from WfWI and stakeholders and reflecting the realities, priorities, and capacities of communities in Bokkos and Jos East LGAs.
Final Consultancy Report: Summarizing the overall methodology, activities undertaken, key findings, lessons learned, recommendations, and practical implementation considerations for operationalizing and sustaining the Community-led GBV Prevention Framework.
Methodology
The consultant is expected to adopt participatory approaches, including:
Literature and document review
Key informant interviews
Stakeholder consultations
Focus group discussions
Participatory workshops
Validation meetings
Duration of Assignment
The assignment is expected to be completed within 9 months of the contract signing date.
Reporting and Supervision:
The consultant will report directly to the Social Empowerment Manager and work closely with the project team throughout the assignment.
Required Qualifications and Experience
The Consultant should possess:
A Master’s Degree in Gender Studies, Law, Social Sciences, Development Studies, Peace and Conflict Studies, International Development, or a related field.
Must have 7-10 years of demonstrated professional experience in GBV prevention and response, gender equality, social and behavioural norm change, policy or framework development, and community engagement.

Job Description
The Reconciliation & Settlement Manager is responsible for ensuring the accurate, timely, and complete settlement and reconciliation of Duplo’s financial transactions across its banking partners, payment processors, payment schemes, merchants, and internal platforms.
The role serves as a critical control function within Operations, ensuring that funds processed through Duplo’s ecosystem are properly accounted for, settled to the appropriate parties, and fully reconciled across Duplo’s internal records and external partner statements.
Responsibilities
Settlement Management:
Own the end-to-end daily settlement process for Duplo’s payment products, including payouts, collections, card acquiring, and other payment channels.
Ensure merchants and other beneficiaries receive settlement within agreed SLAs.
Review and validate settlement reports received from banks, payment processors, and other partners.
Prepare and submit settlement files to banking partners where applicable.
Monitor settlement processing from initiation through confirmation of beneficiary credit.
Investigate failed, delayed, partial, duplicate, or incorrect settlements and drive resolution.
Maintain accurate records of all settlement activities and outstanding settlement positions.
Ensure settlement processes comply with agreed commercial, operational, and regulatory requirements.
Reconciliation:
Perform daily reconciliation of transactions across Duplo’s internal systems, bank accounts, wallets, payment processors, and merchant settlement records.
Reconcile transaction-level data against bank statements and provider settlement reports.
Identify discrepancies between transaction records, ledger balances, settlement files, and bank positions.
Investigate and resolve reconciliation breaks within agreed timelines.
Track outstanding reconciliation items and maintain an ageing report.
Ensure all financial transactions are appropriately accounted for from transaction initiation through settlement.
Develop and maintain robust reconciliation controls to minimise financial leakage and operational risk.
Liquidity & Funding Management:
Monitor liquidity positions across Duplo’s operational and settlement accounts.
Ensure sufficient funds are available to support payout and settlement obligations.
Monitor funding requirements across banking partners and payment providers.
Coordinate with Finance and relevant stakeholders on funding and account movements.
Escalate potential liquidity shortfalls or funding risks proactively.
Maintain appropriate controls around movement of funds between Duplo accounts and partner accounts.
Payment Provider & Banking Partner Management:
Act as a key Operations contact for Duplo’s banking partners and payment service providers on settlement and reconciliation matters.
Monitor provider performance against agreed SLAs.
Escalate recurring downtime, delayed reversals, failed transactions, settlement discrepancies, and other provider-related issues.
Follow up on outstanding reversals, refunds, chargebacks, and recovery transactions.
Participate in partner reviews and provide operational performance reports and insights.
Work with partners to improve settlement reliability and reduce operational exceptions.
Exception & Incident Management:
Own the investigation and resolution of settlement and reconciliation incidents.
Monitor pending transactions and determine appropriate resolution based on transaction status and provider confirmation.
Coordinate with Product and Engineering teams when system-related issues affect transaction processing or reconciliation.
Ensure appropriate controls are applied before reprocessing transactions to prevent duplicate payouts or financial exposure.
Maintain an incident and exception log with clear ownership, ageing, root cause, and resolution status.
Conduct post-incident reviews and recommend preventive measures.
Payout & Transaction Operations:
Monitor payout transaction performance across Duplo’s payment providers.
Track transaction success rates, failures, pending transactions, reversals, and processing times.
Analyse provider routing performance and recommend improvements.
Support the development and implementation of payout reprocessing and exception-handling processes.
Ensure transactions are processed within defined operational SLAs.
Card Acquiring Operations:
Support the operational settlement and reconciliation processes for Duplo’s card acquiring business.
Reconcile card transactions against acquiring bank settlement reports.
Monitor authorisation, capture, refund, reversal, and settlement flows.
Work with acquiring banks and internal teams to resolve settlement discrepancies.
Support merchant onboarding and operational readiness from a settlement perspective.
Ensure merchant settlement processes are properly configured and validated before going live.
Reporting & Analytics:
Prepare daily, weekly, and monthly settlement and reconciliation reports for Operations, Finance, and Management.
Track key metrics, including:
Settlement accuracy
Settlement SLA adherence
Reconciliation completion rate
Outstanding reconciliation items
Provider approval/success rates
Transaction failure rates
Reversal and recovery status
Liquidity position
Settlement exceptions
Provide insights into trends, operational risks, and areas requiring improvement.
Maintain accurate dashboards and management reports.
Process Improvement & Automation:
Identify manual and inefficient processes within settlement and reconciliation operations.
Work with Product and Engineering to automate settlement, reconciliation, exception management, and reporting processes.
Define business requirements for operational tools and dashboards.
Develop and maintain Settlement & Reconciliation SOPs.
Continuously improve controls to reduce financial leakage, operational errors, and reconciliation breaks.
Risk, Compliance & Controls:
Ensure settlement and reconciliation processes comply with Duplo’s internal policies and applicable Nigerian regulatory requirements.
Maintain appropriate segregation of duties and approval controls.
Ensure all settlement and reconciliation activities have adequate supporting documentation and audit trails.
Support internal and external audits by providing settlement records and reconciliation evidence.
Proactively identify operational and financial risks and recommend mitigating controls.
Technical and Professional Requirements
8+ years’ experience in settlement, reconciliation, payment operations, treasury, or financial operations.
Experience in fintech, banking, payment services, or related financial services.
Strong understanding of the Nigerian payments ecosystem and hands-on experience with bank and payment provider settlements.
Experience handling transaction exceptions, reversals, failed transactions, and financial discrepancies.
Experience managing relationships with banks and payment service providers.
Experience working cross-functionally with Product and Engineering teams.
Advanced Microsoft Excel/Google Sheets and strong data analysis and reconciliation skills.
SQL knowledge is highly desirable, while experience with BI/reporting tools such as Metabase, Power BI, or Looker is an advantage.
Understanding of payment APIs, transaction flows, wallets, ledgers, settlement files, NIBSS, card acquiring, and Visa/Mastercard settlement.
Strong attention to detail, analytical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Demonstrated ownership and ability to drive issues through to resolution.
Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.
Process-oriented approach with the ability to build scalable and controlled operational processes.
Ability to lead, manage, and develop members of the Settlement & Reconciliation team
Strong written and verbal communication skills with excellent attention to detail.

Job Description:
Job Summary
The Senior Auditor - Field Compliance & Investigations supports field compliance, investigation oversight, and audit quality across assigned NI-ABAE states.
The role combines field audits, investigation review, evidence validation, report review, and auditor supervision.
This is a field-facing role requiring up to 3 field days per week, focused on high-risk clinics, priority operational issues, investigations, and gaps identified through audit trends or report reviews.
The successful candidate must be able to assess whether field findings are supported by evidence, identify missed risks, and provide clear, actionable feedback to improve audit quality and program accountability.
Key Responsibilities
Risk-Based Field Audits & Compliance:
Conduct field audits and investigations across assigned states.
Prioritize high-risk clinics based on audit trends, unresolved issues, dashboard indicators, staff performance gaps, and operational risks.
Review clinic operations, conditional cash transfer compliance, and adherence to NI-ABAE protocols.
Validate findings using field observations, caregiver interviews, staff interviews, dashboards, records, and supporting documentation.
Identify operational risks affecting compliance, retention, coverage, fraud prevention, and program quality.
Investigation Review & Fraud Risk:
Support confidential investigations involving staff conduct, clinic operations, caregiver payments, and suspected fraud.
Conduct field validation where necessary to assess allegations and gather supporting evidence.
Review investigation reports for missing evidence, unsupported conclusions, inconsistencies, and weak validation.
Distinguish between fraud, protocol violations, performance gaps, training gaps, and operational control weaknesses.
Escalate serious concerns with clear evidence and recommended action.
Report Review & Evidence Quality:
Review Staff Work Day, audit & investigation reports, and related field outputs.
Identify weak validation, missed risks, unclear recommendations, and unsupported conclusions.
Provide clear and actionable feedback to auditors to improve field validation, evidence quality, and reporting standards.
Ensure reports clearly explain the findings, the evidence reviewed, the actions taken, and the required follow-up
.
Team Supervision & Coaching:
Provide technical supervision and guidance to auditors across assigned states.
Review auditor work plans to ensure field activities are prioritized based on risk.
Coach auditors on investigation quality, field validation, escalation standards, and report writing.
Identify repeated performance gaps and support auditor development through follow-up and coaching
.
Risk Monitoring & Continuous Improvement:
Use dashboards, audit trends, field reports, and investigation findings to identify high-risk clinics, staff, or operational processes.
Support improvements to audit tools, protocols, and training materials.
Contribute to fraud prevention, compliance monitoring, and audit quality improvement initiatives.
Support ongoing training for auditors, managers, and field teams on compliance and investigation standards.
What Success Looks Like in This Role
A strong Senior Auditor will be able to:
Plan field audits based on risk, not routine clinic rotation.
Identify high-risk clinics, unresolved issues, and operational gaps requiring follow-up.
Review reports critically and identify unsupported conclusions or weak evidence.
Conduct field validation and investigations professionally and objectively.
Escalate serious concerns with clear evidence and recommended next steps.
Improve the quality of auditor submissions through coaching and feedback.
Maintain strong follow-up and support issue resolution through closure.
Balance field presence, investigation quality, and timely reporting.
Requirements
Required Experience:
3-5 years of experience in field audit, compliance, internal control, fraud investigation, program assurance, field verification, monitoring and evaluation, or related roles.
Experience conducting field audits, investigations, or operational reviews.
Experience reviewing field reports, validating evidence, and assessing operational compliance.
Experience using data or audit trends to prioritize high-risk field visits.

Prior experience supervising or coaching auditors or field teams is an advantage.

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Social Sciences, Public Health, Development Studies, Criminology, Statistics, or a related field.
Professional certification, such as ICAN, ACCA, ACA, CIA, CFE, or relevant compliance/investigation training, is an added advantage.
Required Skills & Competencies:
Technical Skills:
Strong field audit and investigation judgment.
Risk-based audit planning and operational review.
Evidence validation and report review.
Fraud risk and compliance assessment.
Strong written reporting and documentation skills.
Ability to review dashboards, records, and operational data.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Google Sheets, Google Docs, and smartphones.
Behavioral Competencies:
Strong accountability and follow-up.
Clear communication and feedback skills.
Ability to handle confidential matters professionally.
Independent thinking and sound judgment.
Ability to work under pressure and adapt in field environments.
Strong organizational and time management skills.

Train non-technical staff on new tools, systems, or policies in plain language.

Support the Administration team on CCTV, access control, and any technology tied to physical security.

Bachelor’s Degree (minimum of second class lower) in Computer Science, Information Technology, Computer Systems Engineering, or Information Systems.
At minimum 3 years of hands-on IT support experience - not theoretical, not just certifications. You have sat across from a frustrated user with a broken system and fixed it.
Working knowledge of Windows OS, Microsoft 365 (Teams, Outlook, Excel, OneDrive), and general networking (routers, switches, Wi-Fi, basic IP troubleshooting).

Experience managing users and permissions across an Active Directory or cloud-based environment.
